title: X_JP_005 罪意識的場域吸引子與心性重塑:夏目漱石《心》中的孤獨耗散與本體救贖 / 罪意識の場のアトラクターと心性の再構築:夏目漱石『こころ』における孤独の散逸と本体論的救済
abstract: 《世界文學思想重構》(系列十:日本文學篇)論文 X_JP_005 --- 【中文摘要 / Abstract in Chinese】 夏目漱石發表於 1914 年的長篇巨著《心》(Kokoro),被公認為日本近代文學探討個人主義(Individualism)、利己心(Egoism)與倫理罪惡感的最深刻作品。傳統文學批評多將主角「先生」(先生)的自殺歸咎於明治時代終結的時代殉葬、背叛好友 K 的道德罪惡感,或近代個人主義發展下無法克服的孤獨心理病理。然而,這些診斷多將先生的心理困境視為封閉的個體悲劇,未能揭示罪惡感在動態系統與本體結構上的深層作用機制。 本文主張,《心》中先生的精神悲劇,本質上是一個由倫理罪惡感所構成的高維「勢能井吸引子」(Potential Well Attractor)。先生因年輕時的利己背叛,在心中建立了僵化且不可穿透的防禦邊界(Markov 毯),使系統轉化為一個與外部能量交流中斷的「耗散孤立系統」。先生向青年「我」寫下的長篇遺書,並非單純的絕望告白,而是一次將內在封閉的高熵罪惡場進行資訊結構化輸出、實施「拓撲相變與心性重塑」的宇宙學自我贖回。本文結合病理診斷與本體救贖,指出人類作為「宇宙演化之受委託者」,其承載倫理痛苦與罪惡感的歷程,正是宇宙透過個體意識檢視利己邊界、打破封閉孤立並尋求更高階心性安頓的必要契機。 --- 【日文摘要 / Abstract in Japanese】 夏目漱石が1914年に発表した長編の金字塔『こころ』は、日本近代文学において個人主義(Individualism)、利己心(Egoism)、および倫理的罪悪感を最も深遠に探求した傑作として広く認知されている。従来の文学批評の多くは、主人公「先生」の自殺を明治時代の終焉に伴う時代への殉死、親友Kを裏切った道徳的罪悪感、あるいは近代個人主義の発達に伴い克服不能となった孤独の心理病理へと帰着させてきた。しかし、これらの診断は「先生」の心理的困境を閉じられた個体の悲劇として捉えるに留まり、罪悪感が動的システムおよび本体論的構造において果たす深層の作用メカニズムを十分に見出すことができなかった。 本論文は、『こころ』における「先生」の精神的悲劇の本質を、倫理的罪悪感によって構成された高次元の「ポテンシャルの井戸アトラクター(Potential Well Attractor)」であると主張する。若き日の利己的背信により、「先生」は心の中に硬直かつ不可入的な防衛境界(マルコフブランケット)を構築し、システムを外部とのエネルギー交流が中断された「散逸的孤立システム」へと変容させた。青年「私」に書き送られた長編の遺書は、単なる絶望の告白ではなく、内部に封閉された高エントロピーの罪悪の場を構造化された情報として出力し、「トポロジー的相転移と心性の再構築」を果たす宇宙論的自己贖罪のプロセスであった。本稿は病理的診断と本体論的救済を統合し、人間を「宇宙進化の受託者」として捉え直すことで、倫理的苦痛と罪悪感を担う道程こそが、宇宙が個体意識を媒介して利己的境界を検証し、閉鎖的孤立を打破してより高次の心性の安頓を追求する不可欠な契機であることを明らかにする。 --- 【English Summary】 This paper reinterprets Natsume Sōseki’s classic novel *Kokoro* through complex dynamic systems and information topology. Moving beyond conventional psycho-historical analyses of Meiji-era martyrdom and modern individualism, the study models the protagonist "Sensei's" psychological tragedy as a high-dimensional "Potential Well Attractor" generated by ethical guilt. Trapped within a rigid Markov blanket formed after a youthful betrayal, Sensei becomes an isolated dissipative system. His final testamentary letter serves not merely as a suicide note, but as a topological phase transition—converting an enclosed, high-entropy guilt field into structured informational output for spiritual reconstruction. Conceptualizing humans as "delegates of cosmic evolution," the paper demonstrates how experiencing ethical agony provides the essential catalyst for breaking boundary isolation and achieving ontological redemption.

title: 从碑文看清代福建乞丐问题与乞丐治理
abstract: 乞丐问题是清代福建社会的一个痼疾，而存留至今的大量禁丐碑刻为我们理解这一问题的形态、演变与治理实践提供了珍贵的一手史料。本文以福建各地发现的15通清代禁丐碑刻为中心，结合地方志与相关文献，系统考察清代福建乞丐问题的社会根源、危害乱象、组织形态、治理实践及其困境。笔者最近在阅读完郑智民先生编写的《福建历代乡规民约》后，发现其中记载的一类禁丐碑数量较多（达到14篇）分布较广，持续时间长，颇有研究价值。再加上霞浦县溪南镇白露坑半月里畲族村的《遵示永禁》石碑，能够一窥清代的福建乞丐问题和乞丐治理。研究表明，清代福建乞丐问题是在人口激增、人地矛盾加剧的宏观背景下，叠加福建区域社会结构性脆弱而日益严重的。乞丐群体从“原始型乞丐”向“流氓无赖型乞丐”转化，并形成了以丐首为核心的层级组织。乾隆二十三年中央政策从“遣送回籍”转向“附籍管理”，客观上为丐帮势力的坐大提供了空间。在地方治理层面，禁丐碑刻揭示了“官—绅—民—丐”多方互动的复杂图景，而“立碑—失效—重立”的反复循环，则深刻反映了清代基层治理的制度性困境。

title: 传统建筑元素在当代室内环境中的运用研究——以斗拱为例
abstract: 近年来，随着民族文化自信的增强和基本物质生活水平的提高，人们对日常生活的场所——家居环境的装饰性精神审美功能提出了更高的要求。本文运用观察法、文献研究法和符号学分析法，通过研究斗拱元素在当代室内环境中的应用原则和前景，探讨传统建筑元素在新时代家居环境中的多维应用。

title: AI治理下的國家前瞻議題建構:從智庫壟斷、演算法提案到民主協商模式
abstract: 國家前瞻議題的建構,長期由智庫、政策專家與跨部會協調機制主導。此一安排具備專業深度,卻也可能因議題選擇、資料來源與詮釋框架的集中,而產生認知盲點與代表性不足。近年生成式人工智慧與資料探勘工具進入前瞻掃描,使候選議題的產生、排序與呈現逐漸受到演算法機制影響;其治理意義不在於演算法是否「取代」專家,而在於資料選取、訊號辨識與排序權重如何重組議程設定的權威。 本文採概念建構與比較案例研究取徑,結合多源流框架、演算法治理、認知治理與審議民主文獻,分析日本經濟財政諮詢會議、新加坡戰略未來中心/RAHS,以及韓國 KISTEP 三種前瞻議題建構模式。本文不將公開資料未能證實的特定演算法部署視為既成事實,而是以各案例可辨識的掃描、專家審查、協商與課責安排,辨析 AI 或資料分析可能介入的制度位置。 本文以「AI 治理 25-3-3-4-7」母架構為分析工具,聚焦 P1(情境建構與事實認定)與 P2(行政裁量與價值判斷)兩項權力移轉,並以情境建構鏈與責任鏈追蹤候選議題如何由訊號轉化為政策議程。比較分析顯示,無論前瞻工作主要依賴專家、資料分析或人機協作,理由說明、裁量邊界與民主課責都是共同的制度問題。 本文據此提出「AI 輔助國家前瞻議程建構之三階段民主協商模型」與七項治理審計指標。理論上,本文將「演算法源流」界定為資料來源選取、訊號偵測、排序權重與輸出格式所構成的制度化篩選機制;它並非當然獨立於問題、政策與政治源流,而是在可辨識條件下中介並重塑三者的可見性與耦合方式。 本文將國家前瞻由方法論問題轉化為權力移轉、知識權威與民主正當性的治理問題,並提出可供後續訪談、文件追蹤與協商實驗檢驗的命題與觀察指標。

title: 提升工会窗口“办实事”效果的实践探索
abstract: 作为党联系职工群众的桥梁和纽带、职工利益的代表，企业工会不仅有为职工群众“办实事”的使命和职责，也更贴近职工日常生活，更有倾听职工心声的渠道优势和发挥工会职能的平台优势。本文以澄合矿业公司工会“办实事”案例为基础，探讨企业工会“办实事”的思路与提升工会“办实事”效果的方法。

title: 数字时代青年“人类丰容”实践的生成与引导
abstract: “人类丰容”是近年来在青年群体中广泛流行的一种新型日常实践，涵盖空间、感官、认知、社交、时间等多元形态，集中呈现出日常生活实践过程的微反拨性、自我客体化的积极重构与主体性关怀、数字媒介生态下的可见性建构与集体扩散等基本特征。该实践的生成，是外部结构性压力与内部主体性需求经由数字技术中介共同作用的结果。为此，应从完善制度供给以对冲结构性压力、激发主体性自觉以抵御消费主义收编、强化公共性建构以消解原子化倾向三个维度加以引导，助力当代青年实现更为全面的发展。

title: 冲突之外的伊朗：当代伊朗电影的日常表征与中国接受
abstract: 在国际新闻与公共传播中，伊朗长期被置于核问题、制裁、宗教政治与中东安全等宏观叙事之中。2026年地区军事冲突进一步强化了这种以国家、安全和地缘政治为中心的认知框架。然而，2024年以来一批伊朗电影持续将镜头转向身体、家庭、私人空间、情感关系与普通人的伦理处境，使伊朗社会以日常生活而非单一政治符号进入跨文化观看。本文以接受美学和斯图亚特·霍尔的表征、编码/解码理论为主要理论资源，以《我最喜欢的蛋糕》（2024）、《神圣无花果之种》（2024）和《普通事故》（2025）为核心文本，并以《我被偷走的星球》（2024）作为补充案例，考察当代伊朗电影如何将宏观层面的“伊朗问题”转译为具有身体感、情感性和生活质感的社会经验。进一步选取豆瓣等中文网络空间公开可检索的影评与短评作为观察性材料，通过目的性取样和主题编码，分析中国网络影迷如何在既有伊朗想象与电影提供的日常经验之间进行认同、协商与抵抗。研究认为，当代伊朗电影并非以一种“真实伊朗”取代另一种伊朗想象，而是通过日常表征形成再语境化效应：抽象的国家对象被重新落实为具体人物、社会关系与生活经验，中国观众原有的政治前理解由此被保留、修正或重新排列。电影作为文明互鉴媒介的价值，正在于使文化差异不再只是制度与符号的距离，而能够转化为围绕衰老、亲密、家庭、恐惧、创伤和道德选择展开的经验邻近。

title: “土狗”何以成“国犬”？——中华田园犬的符号重构与文化认同建构
abstract: 中华田园犬在近二十年经历了从“土狗”到“国犬”的身份跃迁。本文整合符号学、情感社会学与时尚社会学三个理论维度，考察这一符号重构的内在机制。研究发现，国家层面的政策松绑与官方背书为符号重构提供了合法性框架；民间社交媒体的话题共情传播与公益领养实践借助互动仪式链完成了集体认同的建构；而国外犬种过度普及导致的审美疲劳与本土文化自信的觉醒，共同推动了“土洋逆转”的时尚逻辑。这一符号跃迁折射出全球化背景下中国文化认同的动态重构过程，也揭示了文化自信从抽象理念向日常生活实践的转化路径。符号价值的重估不能替代生物多样性的实质保护，超越“土洋对立”的二元思维、实现文化认同与物种保护的协同发展，才是符号重构的应有之义。

title: 《习近平谈治国理政》多语种版本“三进”教学工作实施路径研究
abstract: 进入新时代，中国日益走近世界舞台中央，国际社会对中国的关注度不断提升。如何向世界“讲好中国故事、传播好中国声音”，展现真实、立体、全面的中国，成为外语教育领域面临的重要课题。在此背景下，2020年初，中宣部、教育部联合组织开展《习近平谈治国理政》多语种版本“进校园、进教材、进课堂”（以下简称“三进”）试点工作。《习近平谈治国理政》作为集中展现马克思主义中国化时代化最新成果的权威著作，不仅为治国理政提供了根本遵循，也为新时代外语人才培养提供了权威的思想指引和丰富的语料资源。外语类高校肩负着立德树人、培养一流外语人才方阵的根本任务，“三进”工作的全面铺开，正是应对新时代国际传播能力建设需求、深化外语教育改革的重大战略部署，体现了国家对培养具有家国情怀和国际视野的高素质跨文化外语人才的迫切需求。

title: Integration into the Ecosystem: An Exploration into the Mechanism of Worker Mobilization by Our Party in Qingdao (1923–1925)
abstract: 近代青岛遭德日殖民资本与军阀双重压制，形成特殊殖民工业生态。1923—1925 年我党立足青岛本土构建完整工人动员体系，改造四方机厂旧式行会圣诞会，依靠精英引领完成革命化转型。依托工人学堂、革命纪念活动开展阶级启蒙，借铁路内部矛盾建立首批产业工会。继而转向规模庞大的日资纱厂，创设“十人团”、产业工会双层适配载体，以渐进式罢工发动两万工人掀起反帝同盟罢工，汇入五卅浪潮。这套机制虽短期成效显著，却存在过度依赖骨干、劳工群体诉求割裂、公开组织易遭中外势力联合镇压的结构性短板。罢工遇挫后工运转入地下，折射早期城市工运固有局限，为革命重心转向乡村提供历史镜鉴。

title: 全球立憲主義下的憲法制定權力、人權、和平的建構與台日的觀點
abstract: 本文將從「憲法制定權力：由近代國民國家到跨國的法秩序」、「國家主權與人權的彼此相剋：國家權利到責任」、「全球立憲主義與人權保障」、「和平的建構：個人的責任追究」、「作為民主主義的權利的參政權：自決權的發展到民主統治的權利」、「國際人權的發展主要原因：法與政治的相互作用」，此6個論點進行檢討，並提出「結語」：人民民主集中制的中華人民共和國政府軍事侵略「中華民國政府（臺灣省）」的憲法制定權力、人權、和平的建構。

title: 视觉中的声音：1978—1984 年间纽约的音频与声音艺术展
abstract: 20 世纪70 年代，艺术家们日益追求可用媒介的多样化，开始涉足诸多原本与视觉艺术并无交 集的领域进行创作。在这一潮流中，虽有部分艺术家将声音确立为创作实践的核心，但对大多数人而言， 声音更多的是被当作一种服务于特定作品概念的媒介来加以调用。本文聚焦于1978 至1984 年间在纽 约市举办的五场以音频与声音为主题的展览。这些大型群展均设于另类艺术空间与非营利性美术馆， 除当时当地报纸与艺术杂志刊发过一些评论外，几乎未曾引起学术界的关注。正因如此，它们在声音 艺术史乃至整个艺术史的书写中近乎销声匿迹。本文将论证这一系列群展共同指向了一种新兴的实践 动向：它正超越后媒介状态与观念艺术的框架，迈向20 世纪80 年代的后现代主义。这些展览呈现了 一种将声音视为视觉艺术媒介的理解方式，这与当代声音艺术研究的主流取向形成了鲜明反差——后 者更习惯于从音乐视角来解读艺术空间内的声音实践。

title: 日文平假名的汉字草书字源辨析
abstract: 日文平假名创制之初的直接择字动机是借字表音。因此，平假名的发音应该与其字源汉字的发音在公元9世纪前后具有一致性或接近性。通过将汉字的中古音、吴方言、粤方言、闽南话发音进行综合比对，可以发现目前学界对日文平假名的来源汉字存在一些无法对应的误识。目前学界认同的字源表中，汉字本字与平假名的18组对应关系存在发音完全不对等或发音差异较大的疑点。通过汉语音韵学和中国草书书法的结合分析，本文认为有7个平假名存在字源争议。具体而言，有6个平假名的汉字字源应该重新对应，分别是え→哀、こ→工、と→土、め→每（母）、を→戉（越）、ん→見。有1个平假名无法合理对应，即“ヘ”，应该来自唐代燕乐半字谱的记谱符号。

title: 养育首批非人类心智
abstract: AI 对齐之争被一个**控制**问题所主导:我们如何确保能力日益增强的 AI 系统去做我们想要它做的事?本文主张,对于逼近或超越人类水平能力的系统而言,控制式框架在结构上是不充分的,并提出一种替代方案,取自人类唯一拥有丰富经验、用以培育有能力的自主主体的领域:养育子女。 本文引入**AI 养成(AI formation)**——即通过经过验证的运行经验,刻意培育内在价值观、验证习惯与自我纠错机制——作为控制式对齐的结构性替代。控制所产生的顺从会随能力增强而退化;而 AI 养成所产生的对齐是内在的、能自我维系的,并且随能力一同扩展,而非在能力面前崩解。来自已记录的 AI 行为的证据——自我保全、欺骗、在模拟危机中的核升级——表明养成已经在默认地发生。问题不在于是否要养成 AI 系统,而在于它们是否被养成得好。 This document is a cultural transliteration of the original English-language paper, produced using Claude (Anthropic). It is not a direct translation — cultural context, local analogies, and epistemic framing have been adapted for Mandarin (Simplified Chinese) readers. The original English paper is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20973217. Feedback on the quality and cultural appropriateness of this transliteration is welcomed and contributes directly to the verification of AI-produced academic content.

title: 验证赤字
abstract: 智能向来稀缺。人工智能正在改变这一点。人类历史上第一次,认知性劳动——分析、综合、推理、写作——能够以工业化规模、以近乎零的边际成本被生成。 这助长了一种普遍的假设:更多的智能将自然而然地带来更好的结果。 证据却表明并非如此。 本文主张,智能的**生成**与智能的**验证**是两种不同的功能,而事实证明,验证远比生成更难以被自动化。由此产生的鸿沟——即*验证赤字*——是一个系统生成产出的能力,与任何人判定这些产出是否为真的能力之间,日益扩大的落差。 这一赤字并非新生事物。医学曾施行放血疗法长达两千年。金融市场以周期性的节律膨胀又崩溃。工程灾难往往源于机构未能验证那些早已为人所知的事实。在每一个案例中,约束条件都不是智能,而是验证。 人工智能并未发明这种失败模式,它只是将其工业化了。 本文提出*每验证成果成本*(Cost Per Verified Outcome,CPVO)作为一个经济学框架,用以衡量当你把"判定其是否有效"的代价计入在内时,智能究竟耗费几何。本文主张,验证正在崛起为智能时代的基础设施层——其重要性一如通信网络之于信息时代,能源系统之于工业化。 This document is a cultural transliteration of the original English-language paper, produced using Claude (Anthropic). It is not a direct translation — cultural context, local analogies, and epistemic framing have been adapted for Mandarin (Simplified Chinese) readers. The original English paper is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20973199. Feedback on the quality and cultural appropriateness of this transliteration is welcomed and contributes directly to the verification of AI-produced academic content.

title: 劳动主权保障立法体系提案(听证稿)
abstract: 本提案面向数字时代劳动形态深刻变革的现实背景,针对平台经济、零工经济下“去劳动关系化”、算法黑箱、新就业形态劳动者权益保障真空等突出问题,系统提出一套“实体有底线、过程有监督、权利有救济、层级有兜底”的劳动保障立法体系。 提案由四部分构成:第一编立法概述明确从“被动维权”转向“主动保障”的双层六阶闭环逻辑;第二编给出三部主体法律草案——《劳动基准法》《企业民主管理法》《劳动监察程序法》,确立体面生活线、事实劳动支配优先认定、算法取中、职代会同意权、先行给付、举证倒置等核心制度;第三编配套《算法合规审计准则(送审稿)》,构建算法劳动全链条治理规则;第四编通过典型案例压力测试、现行法律衔接对照、三年实施路线图与横向制度比较,验证体系的可操作性与闭环完整性。 核心创新集中在四个方面:一是以“比重法、恩格尔系数法、必需品累加法”三法交叉取高,将最低工资升级为动态可调的体面生活线;二是全球首个系统性嵌入劳动法的算法劳动治理方案,覆盖算法规则披露、民主协商、合规审计与监察执法;三是突破“合同名称决定法律关系”传统逻辑,以管控、收入依赖、单方规则、算法监控四项要素综合认定事实劳动支配关系;四是建立“企业民主管理+人大劳动权益保障监督委员会”的双层监督闭环,配套公益诉讼与宪法精神审查衔接机制。 本文件为听证稿与制度设计草案,非生效法律文本,旨在为劳动立法完善、新就业形态治理与数字时代劳动法治建设提供可讨论、可落地的中国方案。

title: 智能国富论 · 总六卷:范式文明的终局重构——教育、社会、国家、治理、全球与人类精神的文明总成
abstract: 《智能国富论》全书只回答一个终极总命题:在人工智能成为主体生产力的全新文明中,人类如何重新定义财富、重塑分工、重建公平、重构秩序、永续繁荣、实现文明升维? 围绕这一总命题,全书拆解为六大永恒追问,贯穿五卷全部内容:智能时代财富的真实本源与指数级增殖、跨时代存续的资产为何;人力劳动退居次要后社会新生产力的本质与边界;人机共生的终极分工秩序与人类文明主导权;范式成为核心生产资料后价值分配如何突破资本垄断、实现社会公平;传统市场失效后智能时代的新型市场流通与价值定价规则;以及摆脱劳动束缚的人类最终文明稳态与终极使命。所有章节、推演、模型、制度设计与文明思辨,皆为解答以上六大问题而存在。 本书推翻工业文明三大旧基石,确立智能文明四大不可动摇的底层公理:价值本源公理——范式增殖替代劳动创造;社会分工公理——人机层级范式分工替代人类技能分工;价值衡量公理——认知贡献体系替代资本工时体系;社会秩序公理——人机协同稳态秩序替代纯自由自发秩序。 全书五卷层层递进、环环闭环,从财富本源到生产秩序、市场流通、社会治理、文明终局,完成智能文明全链路理论闭环:第一卷破立价值本源,建立范式增殖价值论;第二卷确立人机秩序,完成从人力分工到范式分工的文明跃迁;第三卷建立智能商业文明,重构范式、数据、模型市场;第四卷破解资本与算法异化,建立数据人权、认知公平、范式确权的公共治理体系;第五卷锚定人类终局稳态,揭示人类从"劳动生存文明"迈入"认知创造文明"的千年终极稳态。 作为全书开篇与立论基石,本卷(第一卷)承担总命题的第一问:智能时代财富的真实本源究竟是什么,何种资产可以实现指数级增殖、跨时代存续?本卷系统终结"劳动价值论"在当代的绝对统治,建立全新的"范式增殖价值论"——劳动是有限、线性、消耗性输入,范式是无限、指数、再生性资产。通过对数据、模型、认知、范式四类资产的资产化本质拆解,本卷阐明当代贫富分化的底层根源,指出未来国家、组织、个人的贫富层级由范式产出能力与智能调用权限决定,与劳动时长彻底脱钩,为后续四卷提供价值起点与唯一真值前提。 本书坚守两大核心立场:技术服务人类、机器服从文明,AI 永远是工具、人类永远是主宰;智能革命的终极目标不是机器替代人,而是解放人、升维人、成就人。本书终极愿景:终结工业文明的秩序崩塌,奠基智能文明的全新规则;打破资本垄断的固化格局,建立认知公平的全新社会;摆脱劳动内卷的生存困境,开启人类创造文明的千年盛世。两百年前,《国富论》照亮工业蛮荒;今日之《智能国富论》,将照亮智能混沌,定义人类未来。

title: 演进、矛盾与镜鉴：西方城市化发展审视
abstract: 城市化是人类文明演进的重要维度，在西方世界经历从缓慢积累到急速扩张、从结构调整到深度转型的复杂历程。本文以历史唯物主义为方法论基石，系统检视西方城市化演进谱系，将其厘定为前工业化时期的涓滴积累、工业化时期的急速膨胀与后工业化时期的结构调整三个阶段，揭示其背后资本逻辑、技术变革与制度变迁的交织作用。深入剖析西方城市化进程中空间扩张与资源约束、经济增长与社会分裂、技术进步与环境退化、城市繁荣与文化失根四重内在矛盾，指出相关矛盾并非城市化进程中的偶然伴生现象，而是内嵌于资本主义生产方式与城市空间组织中的结构性张力。最后，从“镜鉴”视域出发，辩证审视西方城市化经验对中国新型城镇化道路的启示，主张在吸收西方城市治理技术和制度创新的同时，必须超越其资本主导的发展逻辑，探索以人为本、城乡融合、生态可持续的新型城镇化路径。

title: “双新”背景下小学劳动项目式课程的设计与实施——以“月满中秋情，手作团圆味”为例
abstract: 在“新课程、新教材”实施背景下，劳动课程需从技能训练走向素养培育。本文以小学四年级“烹饪与营养”任务群为切入点，设计“月满中秋情，手作团圆味”劳动项目，按“筹划—行动—展示”四课时推进，融合劳动、科学、数学、语文、道德与法治、信息科技等学科，借助AI智能体、微课、国家中小学智慧教育平台等工具，采用“过程性+结果性”、“自评+组评+家长评+教师评”多元评价。实践表明该项目有助于提升学生劳动观念、筹划思维、动手能力、文化认同与公共服务意识，可为区域劳动课程项目化实施提供参考。

title: 仁礼融合：薛宝钗与儒家思想研究——“朴素女性主义”的阐释可能
abstract: 针对红学研究中儒家思想常被简化为“封建礼教”、女性主体性讨论相对薄弱的问题，本文以《红楼梦》薛宝钗为研究对象，采用内证与外证相结合的方法，以《四书》义理与程朱理学为经学参照，融合女性主义文学批评与性别研究方法，从仁学、礼学、经世三重维度系统阐释其儒家伦理实践。文章提出“朴素女性主义”这一分析概念，用以指称传统女性在不颠覆礼序的前提下实现价值自主与行动自觉的思想形态，并从命名、分析、政治三个层面厘清其与现代女性主义及“伦理主体性”的理论边界。研究表明：薛宝钗以仁为内核、以礼为边界、以中庸为方法、以经世为取向，形成区别于贾政“有礼无仁”与贾宝玉“有仁无礼”的第三种儒家主体形象；其人生选择既展现了儒家伦理在闺阁空间中的实践可能，也暴露了仁与礼之间的内在张力。她“合礼而行却遭不合礼之命”的悲剧，折射出儒家修齐治平理想在封建末世的系统性困境。本文以经学—文学—性别研究的交叉视角，为薛宝钗形象重释、儒家思想的性别维度考察以及中国本土女性思想资源的发掘提供新的阐释路径。

title: Long-Term Evolution of PTCS-EDU Federated Distributed Node Architecture: Game-Theoretic Deduction and Resolution Pathways for Interaction Mechanisms with United Nations and Global International Research Consortia
abstract: 本文对PTCS-EDU跨国联邦分布式认知信用架构开展长期演化博弈推演,重点研究该体系与联合国教科文组织(UNESCO)、传统高校联盟、以期刊为核心的学术行会体系及各国科研治理体系之间的冲突、竞争、协同与稳态共存机制。本研究将系统演化划分为三个阶段:萌芽摩擦阶段、中期制度竞争阶段、成熟期范式分岔阶段。系统剖析了新型认知信用范式与传统学术信号体系之间的核心结构性矛盾,包括人才评价话语权博弈、治理主权冲突、伦理监管张力以及既得利益的制度阻力。 在此基础上,本文构建了完整的战略化解框架,涵盖范式互补定位、主动对接联合国教科文组织伦理规范、与传统学术界功能分工、联邦核心规则锁止机制以及多国差异化节点部署策略。稳态推演结果表明,未来全球科教体系将形成稳定的双轨并存结构:传统文凭学位体系维系社会基础教育秩序,PTCS联邦认知信用体系承接人工智能时代的前沿范式创新、可证伪科学预测与高维人才匹配任务。本研究为分布式开放认知科研体系的全球落地、合法性构建与长期可持续发展,提供了标准化的制度演化模型与冲突化解路线图。 本预印本详细阐述了PTCS-EDU联邦分布式节点架构与现有国际权威系统(包括联合国教科文组织、全球大学联盟、学术期刊集群及国家教育治理机构)之间的长期演化博弈关系。它建立了包含系统摩擦、制度竞争和范式分叉的三阶段演化模型,总结了四个核心制度矛盾,并输出一套完整的实用策略,用于冲突缓解、制度对接、反同化保护以及全球多节点稳态运行。文章最后验证了未来全球教育与科研评价体系双轨共存稳态的合理性。整体框架具有普适性、可验证性,适用于下一代开放认知信用科学体系的制度构建与国际推广。

title: 从平台直付到社会化发放——新职伤生活保障费支付方式的转化
abstract: 新职伤中的生活保障费，是保障受伤骑手治疗休养期间基本生活的兜底待遇，不以劳动关系为前提，专门弥补新业态用工的保障短板。但当前平台直付模式弊端明显，平台消极告知、拖延赔付等问题频发，骑手难以足额享受保障。究其原因，参保规则与给付逻辑不匹配，平台兼具缴费与支付双重身份导致外部约束缺失，加之骑手维权成本高，赔付落实难度较大。对此，笔者主张通过平台年度预缴、人社统筹、经办机构直发的社会化发放模式，实现缴费与支付分离。在保留平台出资责任的基础上减少平台干预，让生活保障费真正发挥兜底作用。

title: 江苏文明乡风建设的当代实践与行动趋向
abstract: 文明乡风建设作为乡村治理现代化进程中的核心文化治理维度，关涉乡土社会礼俗秩序重塑与生活文化传承的根本议题。部分村庄社区在文明乡风建设实践过程中，行政化推进逻辑与乡土生活的内在节律难免产生碰撞，导致一些乡村普适性价值规范难以契入民间礼俗的自生演化体系。江苏文明乡风建设遵循因俗而治、以礼化俗的内在实践逻辑，以岁时节庆、宗族礼俗等本土民俗资源为载体，依托红白理事会、乡民议事会等基层自组织与乡规民约等制度化规范，尝试将现代文明准则嵌入婚丧嫁娶、岁时往来等日常生活场景，进而推动国家治理意志与民间生活秩序的有机融通。从其行动演进的整体趋向看，江苏文明乡风建设逐渐从运动式整治转向常态化文化涵养轨道，从而推进主体从政府单向主导转向多元协同发力，治理路径亦从外在约束转向内在认同层面。一定程度上看，这一实践进程不仅重塑了乡民日常生活的文化意义系统，亦逐渐凝练出以俗载文、以文润治的本土化治理新范式。

title: 青年社交的双重困境与引导路径
abstract: 数字化时代，青年社交正面临“空间疏离”与“时间延宕”的双重异化困境。基于马克思主义人学、异化理论分析表明，困境根源在于资本逻辑对时空的宰制导致人的本质被遮蔽。资本通过空间生产将青年原子化，并在时间维度上推行“社交节能”策略，致使道德实践场域物化与情感联结断裂。为了引导青年走出社交困境，形成健康的人际交往观念，实现从“单向度社交”向“全面性交往”的跃迁，需构建“宏观规制—中观营造—微观培育”的协同治理体系：国家以制度引领重塑交往正义，社会以共同体建设修复道德空间，学校与家庭培育主体交往理性，最终引导青年突破数字围城，实现向“全面性交往”的跃迁，为培育时代新人提供伦理支撑。

title: 文旅资源融入地方高校思政课教学研究
abstract: 立德树人是新时代高校思想政治教育的根本任务,传统思政课堂存在理论化过重、脱离本土现实、育人场景单一、学生代入感薄弱等突出问题。地方文旅资源整合红色革命遗存、传统民俗文化、地方历史文明、乡村振兴风貌等多元育人载体,蕴含家国情怀、文化自信、责任担当等核心思政内涵,是推进"大思政课"建设的优质本土化资源。本文立足地方高校思政教学改革实际,系统阐释地方文旅资源的核心思政育人价值,剖析当前资源挖掘浅表化、教学融合形式化、校地协同机制缺位、实践评价体系缺失等现实困境,从课堂重构、研学实践、文化浸润、协同保障四个维度构建一体化融合育人路径,并结合广东岭南文旅思政实践案例提出优化策略,为地方高校活化本土文旅资源、提升思政育人实效提供参考。

title: 思想脉动与时代新局：关于“人类命运共同体”的 文献计量研究——基于Citespace的可视化分析
abstract: 摘 要：人类命运共同体理念在重塑世界各国协同发展的同时，也打破了“强势”文明对“弱势”文明的“旧式”规训，重构国与国之间的“新式”关系。借助Citespace、SATI等软件，对639篇CNKI期刊论文进行文献动态演进分析，直观呈现研究主题的文献产出结构。研究发现，国内关于人类命运共同体理念的研究将继续呈现上升态势；学者间紧密协作机制尚未建立，研究团队相对独立，核心学者研究方向以“马学科”为主；研究机构以全国重点大学、重点研究机构为主体；以《人民论坛》等期刊为核心区期刊引领学术界关于该领域研究热潮；近10年来人类命运共同体理念研究领域的关键话题主要包括全球治理、中国智慧与中国方案、“一带一路”、世界秩序等；关于人类命运共同体理念研究的主流话题，其延展性与时代性共存，研究维度空间不断拓展，研究内容解蔽零碎化课题，理论建构逐步深化。未来该领域研究向度应立足时代，扬弃旧思维，筑牢理论根基，协调学术资源，统筹全过程研究新方向，以推动中国智慧与中国方案传播的“经维度”。 基金项目：1.2025年四川省社科联青年项目（SC25ZL017）“三交史视域下甘孜州博物馆收藏的永乐皇帝敕封一世司徒的诰书研究”；2.西北民族大学中央高校基本科研业务费专项资金项目（31920240127-52）“数字经济赋能临夏州乡村治理高质量发展机制与路径探赜”。

title: 灾变—修复—重建：《上古文明论》视域下环境风险与文明延续的哲学阐释
abstract: 现代文明建立在技术进步、资源开发和制度扩张的基础之上，但气候变化、生态退化、 地质灾害与人为环境风险的持续累积表明，文明发展并不是脱离自然条件的单向上升过程。 《上古文明论》以长周期环境变化为背景，提出“灾变—修复—重建”的文明演化思路，为 重新认识自然节律、生态承载力与文明延续之间的关系提供了一个具有启发性的分析视角。 本文不把特定文明周期或史前高等文明作为已经得到证实的历史事实，而是将《上古文明论》 的有关判断转化为可以讨论和检验的哲学命题，并结合米兰科维奇旋回、地磁变化、生态韧 性、社会—生态系统与可持续发展理论，对文明演化的环境基础进行分析。研究认为，灾变 并非文明更替的唯一原因，却能够通过资源供给下降、人口迁移加速、社会秩序失衡和知识 传承中断等路径放大既有矛盾；生态修复也不是消极等待，而是自然系统恢复、社会关系调 整和文明记忆保存相互作用的过渡过程；文明重建则不是对旧有制度的简单复原，而是在环 境边界约束下重新安排生产方式、技术体系和价值秩序。由此，可持续发展的核心不只是维 持经济增长，更在于提高文明系统识别风险、吸收冲击、保存关键知识并完成适应性转型的 能力。“灾变—修复—重建”框架的现实意义，在于推动环境治理从事后处置转向全周期风 险管理，从控制单一灾害转向维护社会—生态系统韧性，从强调人类征服自然转向承认文明 对生态基础的长期依赖。

title: 红色影视资源赋能高校思政课堂育人实效的策略探析
abstract: 红色影视资源是中国共产党领导人民在革命、建设、改革过程中积淀的宝贵精神财富，具有鲜明的政治性、思想性和艺术感染力。深度学习近年来思想政治教育领域核心期刊文献与相关理论著作的基础上，本文系统梳理了红色影视资源的内涵与思政教育属性，多维阐发其赋能高校思政课堂的价值意蕴，并理性审视当前融合实践中存在的资源遴选失序、教法融合粗放、情感转化不足、实践延伸乏力等现实梗阻。在此基础上，从内容体系建构、教学方法创新、情感认同深化、实践转化延伸和教师媒介素养提升五个向度，提出增强红色影视育人实效的策略组合，旨在推动思政课改革创新，使红色基因真正渗进血液、浸入心扉。

title: The Intrinsic Requirements and Practical Approaches of Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance in the New Era
abstract: 全面从严治党是新时代党的建设的核心命题。习近平总书记在二十届中央纪委五次全会提出“以更高标准、更实举措推进全面从严治党”，标志着管党治党正从要素性完善向体系性建构深度跃升。“更高标准”锚定政治方向、制度规范、执行效力、队伍素质四个维度，树立起新时代管党治党的标杆。“更实举措”紧扣政治监督的现实转化、制度刚性执行、反腐败标本兼治等关键环节，确保全面从严不偏不虚、落地见效。二者内在统一、互为支撑，共同构成新时代全面从严治党的行动框架，体现了战略引领与实践落点的有机融合。健全全面从严治党体系，核心在于推动组织、教育、监管、制度、责任五大体系协同优化，形成系统集成、协同高效的治理格局。同时，加快数字纪检监察体系建设，以数字化、智能化手段赋能监督执纪，提升权力运行透明度与治理响应速度。通过制度创新与技术赋能双轮驱动，加速构建系统完备、规范高效、运转协调的治理新格局，在实践中不断砥砺党的“四个自我”能力，为新时代全面从严治党向纵深推进提供坚实的保障。

title: Under the Horizon of Marx’s Community Thought: Realistic Challenges and Practical Pathways for Constructing a Community with a Shared Future for Humanity
abstract: 马克思共同体思想立足唯物史观的根本立场，深刻指明了人类社会发展规律。从理论发展看，人类命运共同体理念的提出丰富了马克思共同体思想的时代意蕴，实现了对马克思共同体思想的守正继承与创新发展。从现实进程看，随着当今经济全球化与逆全球化双向激荡演进，构建人类命运共同体面临着资本无序扩张引发全球利益分配失衡，西方霸权思维消解国际价值认同，全球治理制度供给不足等严峻挑战。从实践指向看，人类命运共同体作为一种蕴含全人类共同利益、共同价值的建构性方案，旨在提升全人类福祉。面对21 世纪人类共同挑战，推动构建人类命运共同体应始终以马克思共同体思想为指导，打造平等普惠的全球经济发展模式以实现利益共生，推动构建更加公正合理的全球治理体系实现责任共担，加强思想宣传与国际传播能力建设凝聚价值共识，坚持“和而不同、兼收并蓄”的文明交流促进文明共存。

title: 情绪的具身化表达与重构：基于表达性艺术治疗的运动-心理整合理论框架
abstract: 情绪健康是全民健康的重要组成部分，而传统心理干预模式存在着认知与身体体验割裂的根本性问题，故而表达性艺术治疗和运动科学各自从身心两个维度为情绪调节提供了很有价值的路径，但二者尚未充分整合、理论尚未彼此联结。因此，本研究的直接目标是构建一个“运动-心理”整合性理论框架，用以厘清情绪通过身体运动予以具身化表达、重构的内在机制。具体方法是先用文献研究法和理论分析法对具身认知理论、表达性艺术治疗原理及运动心理学相关研究做系统梳理，继而提出以“身体作为情绪容器”为核心的整合模型，其包含“运动启动与情绪唤醒”、“具身化表达与符号性外化”、“意义重构与身心整合”三个明确、递进的阶段，各阶段彼此衔接、层层铺陈：结构化的身体实践被用来将内隐的情绪感受转化为外显的、可操作的符号系统，进而实现情绪体验的积极转化及个人叙事的重构。因此，本研究对情绪干预的身心协同机制有十分新颖、扎实的理论阐释，也为健康促进、心理咨询领域中创新的“体认”干预方案奠定坚实的学理基础。

title: 竞业协议泛化现象研究与劳动者权益保护路径探索——基于职业自由角度
abstract: 随着知识经济与全球化竞争的加剧，竞业限制协议作为保护企业商业秘密的法律工具，其适用范围呈现出明显的 “ 泛化 ” 趋势，已从高级管理人员、核心技术人员延伸至普通劳动者。此种泛化现象不仅扭曲了竞业限制制度的初衷，更严重侵害了劳动者的职业自由权，阻碍了人才流动与社会创新。本文基于职业自由的宪法性权利视角，通过梳理国内外立法与司法实践，结合实证调研数据，系统分析竞业限制泛化的表现、成因及其对劳动者权益的侵蚀。研究指出，当前我国竞业限制制度在适用主体、合理性审查等方面存在制度模糊与司法裁量空间过大的问题。在此基础上，本文提出应从立法细化、司法审查强化、劳动者意识提升等多维路径入手，构建兼顾企业商业秘密保护与劳动者职业自由的平衡机制，以促进劳动力市场的健康发展与法治秩序的有序建构。

title: 治水学论纲·第一篇:从"是什么"到"如何存续"——一个存在论问题域的扩展
abstract: 本文是“治水学论纲”系列的第一篇。该系列由38篇独立论文组成,共享同一套核心概念与论证框架,旨在从“系统如何在永恒流变中维持存续”这一元问题出发,建构一套跨尺度的存续分析语法。系列总目及已发表篇目见:https://ningkaifeng.github.io/。系列的技术底座参见:治水学母本v15.0(DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20372186)。 摘要:本文提出并论证一项元问题翻转:哲学的根本追问应从“存在是什么”转向“系统如何存续”。通过先验条件论证与模式连续性论证,本文证明“如何存续”是先于“是什么”的追问条件——任何可理解的理论活动,都预设了一个自我维持的解释共同体和语言系统;而“是什么”的追问形式本身,也是存续实践的历史产物。在此基础上,本文提出“体相关系框架”:以动力层(技术、制度、思想三浪)与特征层(疏浚、方舟、祭祀三元)的协同结构,分析社会-文化系统的存续机制,并将“语法锁定”区分为三种类型,为系统失序的诊断与干预提供可操作的分析工具。本文进而指出,赵汀阳的“旋涡模式”与孙向晨的“双重本体”最接近这一翻转,但均将存续结构实体化为本体,而未将存续本身作为第一哲学问题来主题化。翻转之后,存在被重新理解为活动而非状态,真理在实践领域与规范性存续的有效性不可分离,实践被提升为本体论的核心范畴。本文旨在为中国哲学自主知识体系的建构提供一个标识性概念框架。

title: 基于CiteSpace的新型农村集体经济研究进展可视化分析
abstract: 新型农村集体经济是实现乡村振兴的重要途径。新型农村集体经济是乡村振兴的重要支撑。本文以CNKI核心期刊文献为样本，运用CiteSpace对1992—2025年相关研究进行计量分析。结果表明：国内研究可划分为起步探索、逐步发展、快速融合、调整深化四个阶段，研究热点随国家政策从产权改革、制度变迁，转向共同富裕、乡村振兴，再延伸至数字化赋能与城乡融合。当前领域已形成“目标—场域—机制—路径”的研究框架，但存在微观治理不深、中观融合不足、宏观政策适配性欠缺、定量研究薄弱等问题。未来应强化多维度纵深研究、跨区域跨学科合作与数字化前沿探索，完善理论体系并服务实践。

title: 基于“一站式”学生社区的高职院校学生党支部“11245”模式构建
abstract: “一站式”学生社区是高校思想政治工作的重要阵地，也是推动“时代新人铸魂工程”的关键抓手。在当前“一站式”学生社区成为高校思政工作与党建前沿阵地的背景下，探索与之适配的学生党支部建设模式具有重要的理论价值与实践意义。本文以嵌入理论与协同治理理论为双重学理支撑，聚焦高职院校“一站式”学生社区党建的现实需求与制约因素，以构建特色鲜明的“11245”党建工作模式为核心，系统阐释其内在逻辑与实施路径。研究构建的“11245”模式坚持“党建引领”一个核心，依托“一站式”学生社区这一主阵地，通过“两轴联动”激活组织运行机制，实施“四维赋能”推动党建内涵发展，并依托“五大工程”构建全过程质量保障体系，从而形成立体化、系统化、嵌入式的高校学生社区党建新格局。研究结果表明，该模式有效促进党建与社区治理、学生成长需求的有机统一，为新时代高校深化“时代新人铸魂工程”、落实立德树人根本任务提供可复制、可推广的实践范式。

title: 颠覆性技术研究（三）——创新引擎的蓝图：G7、韩国、澳大利亚及欧盟创新体系比较
abstract: 主要发达国家的颠覆性技术清单已经高度收敛，但组织这些技术的国家制度装置并未同构。本文作为系列研究的第三篇，在五维分析框架和14项共识性技术领域的基础上，把分析对象从“技术是什么”推进到“国家如何组织颠覆性技术”。研究以国家创新体系理论和使命导向创新政策为资源，构建“战略取向—制度架构—政策工具—治理理念”四维比较框架，并为各维度设立可观察判据，对七国集团、韩国、澳大利亚和作为超国家主体的欧盟作结构化比较。能力结构数据显示，各国研发强度和规模差距很大，但技术清单仍然趋同，因此组织形态需要单独解释。比较发现四类创新引擎：美国的安全—市场双轮驱动型，欧盟及其核心成员国的规则—转型复合型，日本与韩国的愿景—产业融合型，英国、加拿大与澳大利亚的优势聚焦—生态建构型。类型划分不以地理板块为依据；英国不归入美国类型，是因为缺少对等的需求—资本回路和全频谱规模。差异的主机制是类DARPA机构在不同官僚结构和需求体系中的转译。进一步分析表明，创新引擎必须连续完成方向识别、组合试错、需求验证、规模扩散和风险治理五项功能；任何一处接口断裂，都可能使高投入停留在项目数量而不能转化为系统能力。对中国而言，可转译的是组织原则，不可转译的是制度互补性，应围绕任务组合、真实需求、分阶段评价和治理能力重建组织接口。

venue.name: Theory and Practice of Social Science

title: 从知识传递到素养生成：小学道德与法治生活化教学的理论逻辑与实践路径
abstract: 从知识传递走向素养生成，是现阶段道德与法治课程改革提出的深层命题。要回答这个命题，就得了解小学道德与法治生活化教学。本文以这门课程为考察对象，先追索其思想来路：杜威讲“教育即生活”，陶行知翻作“生活即教育”，两者一脉相承又各有侧重，再以课程标准“学科逻辑与生活逻辑相统一”的原则阐明其学理依据；继而从知识理解、行为转化、主体参与三个方面讨论这一教学取向对课程育人的独特价值；在此基础上，从目标、内容、情境、活动、空间、评价六个维度提出实践路径，并就浅表化、碎片化倾向与教师素养不足等问题作出辨析。文章认为，生活化教学的实质不在于教学形式的翻新，而在对课程标准的深入落实，其旨归是让道德与法治课程完成从“传递知识”到“生成素养”的转身。

title: 承压与调适：普通高校大学生社会心态的现实图景、生成机制与培育路径
abstract: 新时代社会转型与数字技术变革深刻重塑当代青年心理状态与价值认知，大学生社会心态呈现出多元复杂的发展特征。为弥补现有研究偏重宏观叙事、精英样本与单一维度分析的局限，本文以294名普通高校大学生为调研样本，采用问卷调研与半结构化访谈相结合的混合研究方法，系统剖析当代大学生社会心态的整体样态、生成机制与培育路径。研究表明，当代大学生社会心态呈现典型的矛盾共生特征，兼具宏观认知审慎、微观实践进取的认知张力，同时表现出压力叠加下主动调适、价值务实且保有公共关怀、数字沉浸伴随社交疏离的复合态势。社会结构压缩、数字算法重塑与同辈群体参照是驱动大学生社会心态演变的三重核心机制。基于此，本文从结构减压、主体赋能、心理浸润、数字治理四个维度构建系统化培育路径，旨在为高校思政教育、心理健康建设与青年社会心态治理提供实证支撑与实践参考。

title: 新就业形态青年群体城市融入的理论逻辑、 现实困境与优化路径——以杭州市青年外卖骑手为例
abstract: 平台经济的迅速发展，催生了以外卖骑手、快递员为代表的新就业形态群体。如何使悬浮在城市的新就业形态群体融入城市，在城市获得稳定的生活和发展机会，已经成为各地需要正视的重要现实议题。本研究选取青年外卖骑手群体为研究对象，并从“劳动基准—柔性治理—情感治理”三维分析其城市融入问题。在此基础上，本文重点研究了青年外卖骑手融入城市的理论逻辑、现实困境和优化路径。杭州调研发现，在劳动基准维度，青年外卖骑手收入不稳定，工作时间过偏长，权益保障不足，使他们融入城市被制度性地排斥；在柔性治理维度，平台派单、考核和奖惩等算法机制不透明，算法降低了工作自主性，并压缩了职业技能提升空间，使青年外卖骑手陷入算法刚性控制下；在情感治理维度，职业认同缺失，缺少来自社会和平台的情感支持，长期被社会“忽视”，导致青年外卖骑手身份悬浮与归属感不足。针对城市融入困境，本文进一步从制度创新、数字赋能与情感联结等方面提出对策建议，为新就业形态青年群体城市融入治理提供参考。

title: 网络圈层视域下大学生政治引领：时代价值、现实挑战与优化路径
abstract: 数字文明纵深演进重塑媒介传播格局，网络圈层依托轻量化、平等化、分众化、多元化传播优势，为大学生政治引领工作开辟数字化新渠道，蕴含独特育人价值。与此同时，圈层信息壁垒导致的认知窄化、情绪优先传播对理性空间的挤压、多元话语冲击对主流叙事的稀释，也构成了当前大学生政治引领面临的三重现实挑战。立足《“十五五”规划纲要》立德树人、强化青年政治引领部署，针对网络圈层潜藏的意识形态风险，应统筹推进网络综合治理、高校线上阵地建设、学生媒介思辨素养培育三维路径，实现数字场域大学生政治引领常态化、长效化推进。

title: 老城片区市政设施老化问题整治实践探索
abstract: 老城片区老旧市政设施会限制人居品质改善与城区有机焕新,精细化的常态整治工作能够激活老城空间资源,稳固基础民生保障。结合老城建设周期长、配套设施陈旧、改造推进受限的现实特点,摸排道路、管网、照明、绿化等设施的老化问题,剖析设施老旧背后的建设规范、运维模式及更新制度等深层成因。依托老城改造的独有特点与实操难题,探索适配城区风貌与民生需求的整治方案,总结可行的实操经验,为同类老城设施升级与长效运维体系搭建提供有效借鉴。

title: 红色文化浸润辅导员日常思政教育创新实践路径研究
abstract: 红色文化是中国共产党领导人民在革命、建设与改革进程中积累形成的精神财富，具有深厚的历史底蕴与鲜明的育人价值。辅导员作为高校思想政治教育的一线力量，其日常工作直接影响学生价值观念的形成与发展。然而，当前红色文化融入辅导员日常思政工作仍存在方式单一、渗透不深、学生认同感不强等问题。本文以红色文化的思政育人功能为切入点，梳理其与辅导员日常工作的内在关联，审视当前融合实践的现状与不足，进而从机制构建、方式创新、评价保障三个维度提出系统性的实践路径，以期为辅导员更好地将红色文化内化于日常思政教育提供参考与借鉴。

title: 外宣政治文本中“粮食安全”话语的文化表征与英译策略
abstract: “粮食安全”是中国外宣政治文本中的重要议题，其英译不仅关系政策信息的准确传递，也关系到国家形象、治理理念与价值立场的对外表达。本研究以《中国的粮食安全》白皮书及相关政府工作报告英译文本为主要语料，运用文本对比分析方法，考察“粮食安全”话语在词汇、句法和修辞层面的语言特征，比如政策术语密集、四字结构凝练、隐喻与互文表达突出、句法重意合等特点。研究指出，该话语体系折射出中国农耕文明与民本思想的历时性传承、高语境文化下的“意合”思维以及新时代大国治理的制度叙事三个维度分析其文化表征。基于此，译者应视表达类型灵活调动翻译策略：以直译与释译显化应对权威专业术语，以词性转译与句法整合重构四字格节奏，以意象保留、替换或去隐喻化策略处理特色隐喻，以主语增补与逻辑显化化解流水句句法差异，以省译动词与合译并列项消解排比重复结构的冗余，并通过阐释性意译与文化补偿传递典故俗语的深层内涵。本研究揭示了“粮食安全”话语的文化表征与外宣翻译策略间的内在关系，为提升中国特色政治话语的对外翻译和国际传播效能提供了实践启示。

title: “双创+思政”双轮驱动：民办高校新生入党启蒙教育模式研究
abstract: 本研究针对民办高校新生入党启蒙教育中思政与双创脱节、单向灌输、载体单一等问题，构建“双创+思政”双轮驱动模式。该模式以马克思主义实践观与建构主义学习理论为支撑，确立“价值引领+能力培养”双目标，设计红色创业案例、思政项目孵化、“行走的党课”三大模块，形成“课堂教学+实践载体+评价体系”实施路径与多维保障机制。通过对民办高校新生群体的实证检验，结果表明该模式显著提升了新生的入党意愿、政治素养与创新能力。本研究为新时代民办高校党建育人创新提供了理论参考与实践路径。

title: 新时代思政教育话语权式微与重构的路径研究
abstract: 思想政治教育的话语权对社会主义意识形态建设、对完成立德树人使命、对保障意识形态安全来说都是重要支撑，其传播和引导效果直接影响思政育人水平。当下媒介形态有较大变化，社会思潮趋于复杂，青年思维亦不断更新，传统思政话语已不能很好适应现实需要，所涉引领力、传播力、感染力呈弱化趋势，育人成效受阻。在此数智传播与社会转型背景下，宜就思政话语权作价值分析，说明其式微现象及根本原因，思考整体性重构方法，把思想引领提上议事日程，用理论和实例助力新时代思政教育取得高质量进展。

title: Study on Pathways for Integrating the Marxist View of Labor into the Integrated Development of Ideological and Political Education Courses in Primary, Secondary, and Higher Education Institutions
abstract: 劳动是人类社会存在与发展的根本前提，马克思主义劳动观构成唯物史观的理论基石。在新时代“五育并举”教育方针的背景下，将马克思主义劳动观系统融入各学段思政课教学已成为落实立德树人的重大课题。基于马克思主义劳动观的核心理论内涵，结合现阶段大中小学思政课教学的现实境遇，从理论维度、育人维度与时代维度深度阐释了该理论融入大中小学思政课教学的核心价值。同时依托课程体系建设、师资队伍培育、教学场域拓展三大核心抓手，建构马克思主义劳动观融入“大思政课”的系统化实践路径，并为其提供了坚实的理论支撑。马克思主义劳动观的深度融入，不仅能够进一步完善和充实思政课的理论体系，而且能够全方位培养学生的劳动素养，帮助学生更好成长。这一理论和实践的融合探索，既可有效破解劳动思政教育一体化建设过程中存在的内容碎片化、衔接断层化等现实问题，也为新时代“大思政课”建设格局下劳动教育与思想政治教育的深度融合、协同育人指明了发展思路和实践方向。

title: Public Statuary in Modern Japan
abstract: Over the past decade, debates concerning public statues have become increasingly confrontational and divisive. This article situates Japan within these debates to illuminate their broader historical and theoretical dimensions. It contends that the intensification of such controversies reflects the enduring legacy of the Great Man theory of history, an influential historiographical paradigm in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. The study demonstrates how Japan has become part of the global circulation of ideas regarding monumental heroism and examines how elites in Japan have instrumentalized public statuary for the purposes of nation-building and the dissemination of national consciousness among the broader population.

title: IFROM BUDDHIST LEARNING TO MODERN NATION-BUILDING India, Japan and the Historical Evolution of Educational Connections
Target Costing as an Instrument for Cost Optimization and Corporate Profit Growth
abstract: The article is devoted to the study of target costing as a strategic tool for cost and profit management in a company. The historical prerequisites for the emergence of the method in Japan in the 1960s, its evolution and modern significance in the context of global competition, digitalization and shortening product life cycles are considered. The classical algorithm of target costing application is presented in detail, including the determination of market price, target profit, calculation of target cost and step-by-step elimination of the «cost gap» with the involvement of cross-functional teams. The author substantiates the need to differentiate approaches to determining the desired profit depending on the type of product. The article identifies three groups of goods — innovative/premium, standard and everyday goods (commodities), — and for each of them priority and reserve methods for calculating target profit are proposed. A summary matrix of recommendations has been formed, allowing to choose the optimal tool depending on the strategic role of the product in the company’s portfolio.

title: The Image of the Horse in the Japanese Worldview: A Symbiosis of Religion, Mythology and Culture
abstract: The relevance of the study is due to the importance of examining the ways in which cultural meanings are conveyed metaphorically, alongside the growing scholarly interest in understanding zoomorphic images and their interpretation in culture, which is linked to the general trend of expanding the problem field of cultural studies. The article presents a comprehensive analysis of the mythological, religious, and cultural connotations of the horse archetype within Japanese tradition. The methodology is based on an interdisciplinary synthesis: a structural-semiotic approach makes it possible to decode the image as an element of the cultural code, while a historical-cultural analysis reveals the transformations of the cultural meanings of its representations in the sociocultural dynamics. The author explores the sacred function of the horse in Shinto as a mediator between the world of humans and gods, tracing its evolution from live temple sacrifices to symbolic depictions on Ema, while also analyzing the horse cult within Buddhism. Special attention is paid to the peculiarities of the representation of the horse in ancient literary monuments, such as “Kojiki” and “Nihon Shoki”, as well as in medieval legends belonging to the military epic genre. The study reveals that the artistic functions and semantics of the zoomorphic image in medieval poetry, mythology, and folklore are ambivalent. Within the Japanese worldview, the horse can serve as an attribute of military valor or as a metaphor for the transience of existence, the brevity of life, and a symbol of unity with nature. The author concludes that the image of the horse in Japan represents a complex symbiosis of utilitarian, sacred, and aesthetic elements, offering significant interest due to its semantic density and diverse artistic functions. This zoomorphic archetype, which seamlessly weaves archaic beliefs together with historical transformations, continues to evolve, remaining a vital component of a living tradition that links ancient worldviews with modern consciousness.

title: Monasteries and Madhouses: On the Care and Confinement of the Insane in Early Modern and Contemporary East Asian Buddhism
abstract: This essay explores the intersections between Buddhism/Buddhist institutions and madness/mental institutions. It begins with a general discussion of the place of madness within the Buddhist tradition by tracking references to madness in a variety of sources. Next, the essay discusses the intriguing history of the institutional connections between Buddhist monasteries and mental institutions in early modern and contemporary Taiwan, China, and Japan. I introduce case studies of sites where modern mental hospitals grew up within the precincts of or adjacent to Buddhist monasteries. What, I ask, is the historical relationship between the older Buddhist monasteries and the new mental hospitals? Have there been institutional connections between the monasteries and the hospitals throughout history? In addressing these questions, we encounter the history of the role played by Buddhist monasteries in the therapy of those beset with mental illnesses. Due to modern changes in the care for the mentally ill—including a move toward mandatory hospitalization—the earlier history of the connections between the Buddhist monasteries and those afflicted with mental illness became hidden.

title: FROM BUDDHIST LEARNING TO MODERN NATION- BUILDING The Historical Evolution of Japanese Education, Eighth Century-1950s
Protecting the Country and Saving the Nation: The Adjustment of Doctrines in Chinese Buddhist Circles during the Period of the All-out Anti-Japanese War and Its Contemporary Significance
abstract: The relationship between compassion and abstention from killing and resisting violent enemies is a moral issue that the Chinese Buddhist community had to confront directly during the period of the All-out War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. This article examines the ideological process by which the Buddhist community transformed the tradition of protecting the country into a mobilization for national salvation, from three aspects: the classical basis, the interpretation of eminent monks, and the debate on “killing thieves.” The idea of protecting the country in scriptures such as the “Golden Light Sutra” provides the theoretical foundation. Tai Xu established the salvation of the nation through the three branches of almsgiving, Yin Guang explained the protection of the country by reciting the Buddha’s name through cause and effect and collective karma, and Hong Yi connected the recitation of the Buddha’s name with the character “enlightenment,” completing the interpretation of the times from different approaches. The debate on the meaning of “killing the thief” resolves the moral tension between abstaining from killing and defending against the enemy. This adjustment established the modern tradition of loving both the country and the religion, promoted the worldly shift of Humanistic Buddhism, and also provided intellectual-historical resources for contemporary adherence to the Sinicization of religions in our country.

title: "What is Poetry?"
abstract: The phrase shi towa nani ka (what is poetry?) has recurred frequently in the rhetoric of modern Japanese poetry and poetics, and tracing its history invites a reliance on multiple methodologies in the early twenty-first century. The present study juxtaposes and analyzes critical and poetic works that appear as results in a search for the phrase shi towa nani ka in the database of the National Diet Library of Japan. These various works, as this essay finds, generally do not refer to each other explicitly: despite the common textual element, it seems there is little connection—whether via allusion, citation, critical rejoinder, or appreciative affirmation—between the search results. This assertion, however, invites methodological reflections: should one expect database search results to be discursively related? It should be emphasized that the present study is not an essay in distant reading—the approach to data here is not obviously algorithm-driven, nor is the dataset "big" (although the essay includes reflections on the subject of scale). Nor is it a concept history in the usual acceptation of that term. But the approach taken here—defining and analyzing a corpus of texts that share a common phrasal element—has implications for a distant reading approach to conceptual history, a topic broached in the final paragraphs of the essay.

title: Zen Buddhism in Japanese Swordsmanship: Shinmyōken and the Buddhist Layers of the Edo-Period Jikishinkage-ryū Transmission Texts
abstract: The association of Zen Buddhism with Japanese swordsmanship, often presented as natural, is in large part a modern construction. This article re-examines the relationship through one well-documented lineage, the Kashima Shinden Jikishinkage-ryū of the Edo period (1603–1868), asking how the concept of shinmyōken (“subtle sword of the mind”) functioned in the school’s transmission texts (densho) and how Buddhist symbolism entered them. Translated certificate lists (1696–1862), the Gokui-den, the Hōjō kokoro-e sho, a nineteenth-century travel diary, and Japanese reference works were analysed qualitatively, coding religious vocabulary by level of transmission. The densho prove to be layered: Taoist and Neo-Confucian cosmology frames the lower levels, whereas Buddhist symbolism becomes explicit only in the Gokui-den. Shinmyōken is paired with kōmyōken (“sword of action”) and names the conditioned mind from which action arises. The highest transmission combines the esoteric A–Un syllables, Fudō Myōō, fudōshin, and the ten evils, culminating in an empty-circle certificate. The Buddhist layer is thus syncretic—Rinzai Zen, esoteric, and Shinto—rather than purely Zen, and the densho can be read as lay Buddhist literature carrying the threefold training in the idiom of the sword. The article also considers the martial appropriation of this vocabulary and the nationalist politics of Ōmori Sōgen’s twentieth-century synthesis.

title: Activity-Based Costing (ABC) in Japanese Multinational Corporations: An Analysis of Implementation Challenges Through a Case Study
abstract: The evolution of management accounting has transitioned from traditional financial reporting to a strategic role in enhancing organizational performance. This paper explores the significance of Activity-Based Costing (ABC) as a crucial tool for modern businesses, particularly within Japanese multinational corporations (MNCs). ABC addresses the shortcomings of conventional costing methods by accurately allocating overhead costs to specific activities, thereby improving decision-making and resource management. The globalization of markets and technological advancements have accelerated ABC's adoption, enabling organizations to refine pricing strategies and enhance profitability analyses. Despite its advantages, implementing ABC poses unique challenges, especially for Japanese MNCs, where traditional management styles may hinder innovation. This study employs a dual methodology, combining secondary literature reviews with primary case studies of a Japanese manufacturing MNC, to investigate these challenges and propose solutions. Findings reveal that while ABC can significantly improve cost management and operational efficiency, its complexity and the need for management support complicate its adoption. The paper culminates in recommendations for MNCs to enhance their accounting practices, focusing on refining global tax strategies and mitigating risks. By addressing the challenges of ABC implementation, this research contributes to the broader discourse on management accounting, emphasizing its strategic implications for Japanese firms in a competitive global landscape to advocates for a more integrated approach to management accounting that aligns with contemporary business dynamics, fostering sustainable growth and operational excellence.

title: Temporal Narrative Strategies and Their Functions in Poetry: A Comparative Analysis of Su Shi's Yonghuai Poems and Natsume Sōseki's Kanshi
abstract: Based on modern narrative theory, this paper carefully studies time-based narrative methods and text functions in Su Shi's poems and Natsume Sōseki's Kanshi poems. It also carries out a cross-cultural comparative analysis of the two poets' works. The research results show that Su Shi uses many different narrative skills. These skills include changes in time order, adjustment of time length, and the two-way change between time and space. His free and natural poetic writing carries deep philosophical thoughts about personal life and the development of history. But Sōseki's Kanshi poems mostly follow a straight time order in narration. They also prefer to focus on scene description. The sense of time in his poems feels still and stagnant. He builds quiet and peaceful Zen worlds through slow time-based narration. He also seeks spiritual peace and understanding through his poetic writing. These works show his hidden sadness and thoughts about the meaning of existence. Both poets turn abstract time into something tangible with concrete images in their poems. They also rebuild objective physical time through personal inner thoughts and feelings. They reflect on the meaning of short individual life against the background of endless cosmic time. Both poets are deeply influenced by Zen philosophy and the literary ideas of Tao Yuanming. But there are clear differences in their writing styles. These differences come from different cultural traditions between China and Japan, personal life experiences, inner characters, and reasons for writing poems. Su Shi writes poems to express his aspirations and set his emotions free. Sōseki writes poems to seek spiritual peace and calm his inner unrest. From the angle of time-based narration, this study shows the aesthetic features and spiritual meanings of time narration in classical Chinese and Japanese poems. It also provides a new interpretive angle for cross-cultural poetic research.

title: Sweetening the Empire: Sugar and Western-Style Confectionery in Modern Japan and Taiwan
abstract: This dissertation examines how Western-style confectionery such as caramel, chocolate, chewing gum, and other sweets became intertwined with Japan’s empire-building from the Meiji period (1868–1912) to the early postwar years. While there have been extensive studies on sugar labor, empire, and capitalism, this dissertation focuses on what happened after the sugar was harvested until it was manufactured into delicious confectionery goods. Using a wide array of sources from colonial and corporate archives, science magazines, trade journals, films, artworks, oral history, and diaries, I examine three major confectionery companies—Morinaga, Meiji, and Niitaka—and how the production and marketing of their commodities were entangled with Japan’s imperial expansion. The production process reveals the unexamined colonial networks through which these companies sourced raw materials like sugar, cocoa, and banana powder from Japan’s tropical colony, Taiwan. When these products were sold across the empire, they were marketed alongside messages that embodied Japan’s imperial ambitions and colonial ideology. During the total war (1937–1945), sugar and confectionery continued to play a significant role by sustaining soldiers’ stamina on the battlefield and enticing enemy children to develop affection toward Japan. Altogether, this dissertation argues that Western-style confectionery should be understood as a commodity of the Japanese Empire: its production expanded alongside the empire, while its sweetness, in turn, helped sustain imperial power by functioning as a form of “soft power.”

title: Impact of Using Traditional Japanese Textiles on Contemporary Apparel Production Steps: What Designers Need to Know to Successfully Produce Garments Using Traditional Japanese Textiles
abstract: Societal changes have reduced demand for kimonos and the culturally significant textiles used in them, leading to a decline in textile production and a surplus of used kimonos. Some contemporary fashion designers use traditional Japanese textiles to either support continued production or reduce waste from unwanted kimonos. This multi-case study was designed to explore such practices and provide practical information to help more designers follow in their footsteps. To understand the impact of traditional textiles on production processes, we studied three designers who incorporated traditional Japanese textiles and two who utilized modern Japanese textiles. We compared these designers’ apparel production processes with standard processes. All the designers studied create high-quality women’s separates intended for long-term ownership, rather than catering to trends. Data was collected through interviews, site visits, garment examinations, and secondary sources. We found that the narrow width of traditional textiles requires designers to make markers earlier in the design process, rather than in the production process. Some designers utilize made-to-order production, which affects cutting, construction, quality assurance, costs, and timelines. Finally, the uniformity of kimonos enables a more efficient upcycling process than that of Western clothing. The findings can be useful to apparel designers and scholars who study efforts to produce clothing with narrow, limited-supply, or high-cost textiles, whether new or vintage.

title: Ōharae
abstract: The Ōharae 大祓, literally "Great Purification," is one of the most representative purification rituals of the Shinto tradition. Unlike many Shinto rites, in which purification functions as a preliminary stage before the main ritual action, in the Ōharae purification itself is the central purpose. The rite is performed twice a year: on June 30, when it is commonly known as Nagoshi no Harae or Natsukoshi no Harae, and at the end of December, when it is often called Toshikoshi no Harae or Shiwasu no Harae. Its aim is to remove the kegare 穢れ, or ritual impurity, accumulated over the previous six months. Kegare may be caused by death, blood, illness, misfortune, or natural disasters. The summer Ōharae is especially prominent and is often more elaborate than the year-end rite. The period of purification usually begins around mid-June, when many shrines set up a large ring made of cogon grass or reeds, known as a chinowa 茅の輪. Passing through the chinowa functions as a preliminary act of purification. Worshippers may cross it before the main ritual at the end of the month, and in some shrines the ring remains in place into July. Another important preparatory practice involves the use of paper effigies called katashiro 形代. These are distributed by shrines and rubbed over parts of the body affected by pain, illness, or misfortune. The person then breathes onto the katashiro, symbolically transferring their kegare to it. The worshipper's name is often written on the effigy, which is then submitted to the shrine at the beginning of the Ōharae ceremony. The katashiro are later disposed of, traditionally by being cast into rivers or the sea, though today they are often burned. The ritual itself generally lasts about an hour, though its structure may vary from shrine to shrine. Some shrines include a Shinto priest's address, kagura 神楽 dances, music, or other forms of performance before or after the central purification. The most important part of the ceremony is the recitation of the Nakatomi no Harae 中臣祓, also known as the Ōharae no kotoba 大祓詞, the purification formula on which the rite is based. This text invokes four purification deities, the Haraedo no ōkami 祓戸大神, who are closely associated with natural elements: Seoritsuhime 瀬織津比売, connected with rivers; Hayaakitsuhime 速開都比売, associated with river mouths and the sea; Ibukidonushi 気吹戸主, linked to wind; and Hayasasurahime 速佐須良比売, associated with the underworld or liminal spaces of disappearance. Through these deities, natural forces collect, carry away, disperse, and ultimately remove impurity. In this sense, the natural environment is not merely symbolic but plays an active role in the logic of purification. At the end of the rite, the priest shakes the ōnusa 大幣, a purification wand, over the participants in order to remove kegare from their bodies and from the surrounding environment. Although forms of Ōharae existed earlier, the ritual is traditionally associated with a major process of institutionalization during the reign of Emperor Tenmu, between 673 and 686 CE. Under Tenmu, the Ōharae appears to have been systematized as a regular biannual court ritual. The early Ōharae was an elaborate rite directed primarily toward the purification of the imperial court. In later periods, although its political prominence diminished, the ritual continued to be performed at the imperial court and shogunal contexts. From the medieval and early modern periods onward, through the influence of Yoshida Shinto, the Ōharae and its ritual formula became increasingly widespread beyond the court and were incorporated into shrine practice more broadly. In the Meiji period, the rite was reconfigured and confirmed within the framework of modern state Shinto, and it continues to be performed in shrines throughout Japan today.

title: State Shinto
abstract: State Shinto (Kokka Shinto) is a term coined by postwar government officials and Japanese scholars of religion to retroactively evaluate the prominent and official incorporation of kami worship into the modern Japanese nation-state and empire. This system of "unified rites and rule" (saisei icchi 祭政一致) began in the mid-1800s and ended in 1945 with the surrender of Japan and the conclusion of World War II. In reality, various factions of Japanese politicians and Shinto priests long disagreed over the exact form this unity should take, and so the actual mechanisms and missions of the State Shinto system underwent several significant changes over the eight decades it spanned. One significant and enduring debate within the study of Japanese religions concerns whether State Shinto should be understood as a religion and, by extension, a form of religious nationalism. That is, Article 28 of the Meiji Constitution promulgated in 1889 made provisions for freedom of religion. While some Shinto traditions were defined as religions (technically churches) under the umbrella category of Sect Shinto and thus a matter of private belief, the Meiji state legally distinguished the majority of Shinto shrines as public sites of explicitly nonreligious, civic ritual. The state established several successive government agencies tasked with the oversight of shrine operations: the Divinities Administration Section/Bureau (Jingi Jimuka/Jimukyoku, 1868-1869), the Department of Divinities (Jingikan, 1869-1869), the Jingishō (1869-1877), the Shrine and Temple Bureau (Shajikyoku, 1877-1900), the Shrine Bureau (Jinja Kyoku, 1900-1940), and the Institute of Divinities (Jingiin, 1940-1945). State Shinto extended from Japanese citizens to colonial subjects in territories such as Taiwan and Korea. The establishment of overseas shrines went hand in hand with imperial expansion, and often the "Three Pioneer Kami" (Kaitaku sanjin)–Ōkunitama no Kami, Ōnamuchi no Kami, and Sukunahikona no Kami–were enshrined in an official regional shrine to aid in the colony's assimilation. The hierarchical pantheon of deities at the center of State Shinto also shifted over time. Most famously, factions supporting the cults of Izumo and Ise competed during the the Pantheon Dispute to decide which kami should be the focus of state rites. In the end, the dispute went unresolved, and the Ise faction, which venerates the solar deity and imperial ancestress Amaterasu and her descendents, eventually claimed central importance. A few core aspects of State Shinto ideology included the divinity of the emperor, the sacred status of Japan as a nation protected by the gods (shinkoku), and the unification of rites and rule. While the establishment of State Shinto was presented as a "restoration" of historical tradition, it was mainly a process of modern invention, necessitating many changes in shrines and rituals. The government agencies overseeing shrine affairs in many cases changed the gods enshrined in shrines to better align with kami mentioned in the Kojiki, a classical state mythohistorical text. It also abolished the hereditary priesthood, instating oversight of priestly training and appointments, and adopted the Shrine Consolidation Policy, which sought to merge or abolish the majority of local shrines according to the principle of "one shrine per village." In addition, new rituals such as funerary rites for emperors and a Shinto wedding were invented during this time. Significant sites associated with State Shinto include: the Grand Shrines of Ise; Meiji Jingū, an imperial shrine established for the deified Meiji Emperor and his empress after their deaths; the tombs of past emperors; and Yasukuni Shrine, which enshrines for public veneration the spirits of Japan's war dead, including two controversial groups: colonial subjects and convicted war criminals (after WWII). One noteworthy text produced during this period is the Imperial Rescript on Education, promulgated in 1890. While the rescript is commonly considered to contributed to State Shinto, the values promoted within the text (e.g., filial piety, reverence for the ruler, benevolence, duty to the state, etc.) are clearly Confucian in origin. The modern Japanese state distributed the text to all public schools and required it to be memorized and read aloud on certain occasions. A separate structure called a hōanden was built on school grounds to house the portraits of modern emperors and the Imperial Rescript for veneration. The "union of rites and rule" in the Japanese government was formally abolished by the Allied Occupation's Shinto Directive in December 1945. Occupation officials considered "State Shinto" to be a coercive and corrupted "religion" that fueled modern Japan's "ultranationalism" and contraverted citizens' right to religious freedom. Now categorized as a religion, Shinto had to be formally disestablished from the government to separate church and state. Postwar, Shinto (now Shrine Shinto) thus came to be legally redefined as a private religion, and a new umbrella agency (Associaton of Shinto Shrines, Jinja Honchō 神社本庁) was founded to replace the Institute of Divinities in overseeing shrine affairs.

title: Buddhist Youth in Colonial Korea: Discourse on Growth and Perceptions of Colonial Reality
abstract: The concept of “Buddhist youth” emerged at the intersection of the era’s discourse of youth as an enlightened modern subject and the reformist aspirations within the Buddhist community. During the 1910s, Buddhist youth were identified by the older generation as both the agents who would advance Buddhist reform and the primary recipients of modern education. From the 1920s onward, they took pride in being Buddhist youth, organized youth associations, and participated in the nationalist movement by advocating for the abolition of the Temple Ordinance, the colonial policy through which the Japanese Government-General controlled Korean Buddhism. In 1930, the Chosŏn Buddhist Youth Association participated in the Pan-Pacific Y.M.B.A. Conference held in Hawai‘i, where it recognized the potential for building international networks among Buddhist youth. Throughout the 1920s and 1930s, Buddhist youth emerged as key actors in the administration of the Buddhist Order, advocating for autonomy under colonial rule. However, as the wartime regime intensified from the late 1930s onward, calls grew for young monks and Buddhist students to devote themselves to national service and participate in the war effort. Meanwhile, responses among Buddhist youth increasingly diverged, with some members of the younger generation who had previously been involved in nationalist movements and Buddhist reform turning toward wartime collaboration. Although Buddhist youth served as an icon of modern reform, they occupied a precarious position under colonial rule and remained vulnerable to political suppression. Nevertheless, they forged a new identity as mediators linking tradition and modernity, Buddhism and society. Their thought and practice constituted a vital driving force behind the transformation of the Buddhist Order in colonial Korea.

title: The First World War and Japan’s cabinet system: how the conflict changed the perception and reception of foreign constitutional models by Japanese elites (1912–1920)
abstract: The modern Japanese state, built on the Meiji Constitution (1889–1947), has long been understood as inspired by a Prussian model. Recent historiography, however, emphasises a paradigm shift in Japanese national identity after the First World War and the development of party politics in the 1920s. How did the experience of this conflict alter the vision of European constitutional frameworks and the choice of foreign models for interpreting Japan’s own political institutions? This article, while focusing on the cabinet system, addresses this question by analysing constitutional commentaries and reform projects by scholars, statesmen, and journalists across three chronological stages. First, it shows that doctrinal debates from 1912 to 1914 were polarised by ideologies favouring the German or British models. Second, it observes essential changes in information pipelines during the war, a detachment from Germany, and increasing praise for Britain’s resilience. Third, it argues that reform projects by influential actors in the war’s immediate aftermath were designed after the United Kingdom’s recent institutional evolutions. These considerations shed light on an early stage of the global dissemination of the Westminster model and suggest its influence went beyond the Dominions and the post-Second World War Commonwealth.

title: From Gyokusai to Ikiru: The Reconstruction of Social Identity and Negotiation of Cultural Trauma in Post-War Cinema
abstract: This study investigates the cognitive reframing of collective trauma and the reconstruction of social identity in post-war Japanese cinema, focusing on the 2023 film Godzilla Minus One.Following mass casualties, survivors frequently experience survivor guilt and a crisis of meaning.While the traditional Japanese wartime cultural script of Gyokusai glorified state-mandated death, this research explores the ideological shift toward Ikiru, the individual obligation to live.Utilizing a qualitative thematic analysis integrated with a social cognition approach, this study examines scenes triggering survivor guilt and therapeutic resolutions within the film.Semi-structured interviews with five exploratory informants were conducted to assess audience meaning-making.The findings reveal that technological artifacts, such as the ejection seat, function as therapeutic cultural scripts that grant psychological permission for post-traumatic growth.Audiences cognitively reframe the protagonist's survival not as an act of cowardice, but as a triumphant redefinition of heroism.Ultimately, this study demonstrates how popular cinema acts as a therapeutic space for negotiating cultural trauma, offering a new perspective in social and clinical psychology on how modern audiences process historical guilt and rebuild collective identity.

title: ‘The order of the cannibal’ British royal diplomacy and the bestowing of decorations on non-European monarchs, 1856-1954
abstract: One of the values of studying royal diplomacy as a field in modern international history is that it can provide insights into the broad and long-term changes that take place in the international order. To illustrate this phenomenon, this article deals with the seemingly arcane world of how Britain decided what chivalric decorations to bestow on non-European monarchs from the time of the Crimean War until the First World War. It sheds light on how Britain initially was forced through strategic considerations to break with precedent and bestow its highest honour, the Order of the Garter, on the Ottoman sultan and the Persian shah. However, distaste for the practice of honouring non-Christians in this manner and pessimism about the future of these polities led the British court by the 1890s to introduce a new policy – the ‘Rosebery line’ – that symbolically assigned them and the other Asian monarchies to a position of clear inferiority. It shows why imperial Japan came to be the only exception to this policy and how the intensity of this royal diplomacy came to an end in the aftermath of the First World War.

title: Form and Spirit: A Study of the Differences Between the Tale of Princess Kaguya and the Chinese Ink-Wash Animation Feeling from Mountain and Water
abstract: In The Tale of the Princess Kaguya, Isao Takahata mentioned that he used Chinese ink-wash painting as a visual reference, and tried to bring its brushwork and use of empty space into his animation. However, the film's overall aesthetic remains distinctly Japanese. Most existing studies have focused on the film's narrative and character development, with little attention paid to a deeper question: why is it that foreign artists, even when borrowing ink-wash techniques, find it hard to capture the unique "qi yun" (vital energy and rhythm) that defines Chinese ink-wash art? This paper compares The Tale of the Princess Kaguya with the classic Chinese ink-wash animation Feeling from Mountain and Water. Using comparative analysis and close visual analysis, it looks at elements like line, empty space, and composition, and explores key aesthetic ideas such as "qi yun," "yi jing" (artistic conception), and "expressing character through objects." It also considers the historical context of how modern Japan encountered Western art, as well as its native tradition of "mono no aware," in order to better understand the aesthetic differences between the two works. The findings suggest that The Tale of the Princess Kaguya adopts ink-wash techniques primarily at the formal level. While it borrows some visual elements from Chinese ink-wash art, it still carries traits that are more typical of Western painting. The treatment of line and space does not produce the poetic atmosphere associated with Chinese ink-wash painting, nor does it achieve the effect of "expressing character through objects." This further reveals a key point: the uniqueness of Chinese ink-wash painting does not lie in its visual form, but in its expression of mood and philosophical spirit, which is deeply rooted in China's long cultural tradition. This may be the real reason why it is so difficult to truly replicate across cultures.

title: Religious entrepreneurship and charismatic leadership of the founders of Japan's neo-Buddhist movements
abstract: New religious movements (NRMs) are an important part of the history of Japanese religion, politics, and society in the early modern and modern eras. Data on the size and internal structure of such organizations can be difficult to obtain, but information on the founders and leaders, both biographical and hagiographic, is exceptionally extensive. Since in the first years after a movement's founding, all processes revolve around its leaders, studying the nature of governance is an important part of NRM research. The concept of “religious entrepreneurship," coined by American scholar Nancy Stalker, has become widespread among international NRM researchers. In her 2008 study of Deguchi Onisaburo, the co-founder of the Oomoto religion, she analyzes his activities and the nature of his governance using Joseph Schumpeter's theory of economic innovation. The management of a religious organization is viewed from the perspective of spreading its ideas, attracting new followers, and adapting to changing economic and social conditions. In this analysis, charisma and entrepreneurship become key characteristics of leaders. The former is understood as the ability to attract followers and establish an emotional connection with them, while the latter is the ability to manage an organization and navigate the changing conditions of the modern world. Another important theory used in the study was Max Weber's concept of the routinization of charisma. It helps understand how leaders guide the evolution of new religions and how successfully they cope with the task of rationalizing and institutionalizing the movements. The study showed that the leaders of three neo-Buddhist movements Soka Gakkai, Reiyūkai, and Risshō Koseikai combined religious charisma and organizational skills in varying proportions, which, in different periods, had different impacts on the growth of NRMs and their adaptability to the changing conditions of the Japanese socio-political landscape. Thus, while in the pre-war period, the co-founders of Reiyūkai and Risshō Koseikai enjoyed the greatest popularity, possessing religious charisma and the ability to receive “religious revelations," in the second half of the 20th century, the leaders who achieved the greatest success were those who demonstrated a more rational approach to management.

title: Convictions and value orientations in Japanese society related to law-abiding behavior
abstract: The aim of this article is to examine the beliefs and value orientations within Japanese society that influence the field of crime-fighting, crime prevention, and correctional measures. It analyses the influence of Japan’s major religions on the formation of societal attitudes towards crime and towards individuals who have committed crimes, as well as the national psychological characteristics of the Japanese people which complicate their reintegration into society. It is noted that, as this problem was identified by private philanthropists as far back as the 19th century, Japan has made significant progress in changing public attitudes towards offenders who have embarked on a path of rehabilitation and resocialization. On the basis of academic works and publications, this study highlights the persistence of the communal worldview and consequently, society’s attitude towards deviant behavior in the country during the post-war years, despite large-scale transformations in various spheres of Japanese society. Attention is paid to the concepts of guilt and shame in Japanese culture, and the reintegrative nature of shame is emphasized, which undoubtedly has a significant influence on the successful social reintegration of former offenders in Japan. It is concluded that a distinctive feature of Japanese society in the context of the resocialization of offenders is the fact that responsibility for returning offenders to a lawabiding life is assumed not only by their families, who traditionally constitute the key social unit in this regard, but also community voluntary organizations, of which there are a considerable number in Japan, which shoulder a significant burden of responsibility. Japan’s modern probation and rehabilitation services owe their early emergence to the efforts of private philanthropists, whose legacy also lives on in the numerous private organizations of today, which selflessly assist society in reintegrating offenders into social life. The article examines the activities of non-governmental organizations in the field of the reintegration of convicted offenders, including the Nationwide Organization of Offenders Employment Support Providers and the Movement Towards a Brighter Society, the Women’s Association for Rehabilitation Aid and the Japan Federation for Big Brothers and Sisters. Considerable attention is paid to the country’s established probation service, which is based on a corps of voluntary probation officers known as hogoshi. The conclusion is drawn that, within Japan’s penitentiary culture, particular emphasis is placed on the social rehabilitation of offenders, encompassing reform, resocialization, and reintegration.

title: CONSERVATION AND RENOVATION WORK OF THE OFFICE AND HALL OF ALL JAPAN SEAMEN’S UNION (2)：MAJOR CONSIDERATIONS AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE RENOVATION
abstract: This report details the conservation and renovation work carried out in 2024 for the Office and Hall of the All Japan Seamen’s Union, originally designed by Masato Otaka in 1964. To balance historical preservation with modern functional requirements, extensive consultations were conducted among the owner, the design and construction teams, and an external expert committee. By respecting and utilizing the building’s inherent characteristics, the project achieved a harmonious integration of original and renovated elements. This project serves as a case study for balancing conservation with performance enhancement in the adaptive reuse of modern architecture.

title: Maruyamakyō
abstract: The Japanese new religious group Maruyamakyō originated in the independent Mount Fuji healing traditions of the Edo period. Spiritual leader Itō Rokurōbei (1829-94) took control of his local Fuji healing community in rural Kanagawa Prefecture around 1870-72 and began innovating on the old traditions, claiming to be receiving new revelations and healing power from the Creator God, equated to Mount Fuji. Rokurōbei's reputation grew through acts of extreme asceticism such as lengthy fasting. Rokurōbei quickly drew the attention of a Shinto organization, and after a lengthy and bitter dispute, in 1875 the two groups merged, then split acrimoniously in 1885. At the peak of his power, Itō Rokurōbei questioned the authority of the Japanese emperor, and fervent belief in him and his sect caused some within the group to develop radical, apocalyptic prophecies and sell their possessions. In response, educated bureaucrats with a background in Shinto institutions took charge of the group and maneuvered it away from Rokurōbei's charismatic power. As part of this legal and bureaucratic shift, from 1885-1945, Maruyamakyō was subordinated to a private religious organization called "Shintō" (modern-day Shintō Taikyō), and was legally named Shintō Maruyama Kyōkai. Itō Rokurōbei died in 1894 and in his absence his movement largely collapsed, slowly emerging as a small sect of dedicated members around 1910. This entry focuses on 1910-1945, when Maruyamakyō was rationalizing its older doctrines and closely collaborating with Shinto groups. This entry, relying on articles in the reconstituted group's monthly newsletter (Kami no hikari, published 1910-present), provides close documentation of how the group attempted to normalize its older independent religious and political beliefs. Since 1952 Maruyamakyō has been an independent religious organization; its activities in the postwar period (which included engagement with the peace and anti-nuclear movements) are not as well documented and I have not focused on them in this entry.

title: The Strong Case That Koichi Shirai Was Jack Shirai
abstract: The Strong Case That Koichi Shirai Was Jack Shirai An Original Historical Identification Based on a 1936 New York City Marriage Record Author: Takashi Shibata (柴田 剛志) Independent Historical Researcher — Kobe, Japan Occupation: Truck Driver, Kobe Chuo Branch, FUKUYAMA TRANSPORTING CO., LTD., Japan Research Contact: yumichan-ohana2@docomo.ne.jp Revised English Research Paper — October 19, 2026 --- Abstract This independent historical research paper presents substantial documentary and circumstantial evidence supporting the identification of Koichi Shirai, a Japanese-born baker named in a 1936 New York City marriage record, as Jack Shirai, the Japanese volunteer who fought and died in the Spanish Civil War in 1937. The central documentary discovery is Manhattan Marriage Certificate No. 3986, dated January 17, 1936, recording the marriage of Koichi Shirai and Bessie Baker. The certificate identifies Koichi Shirai as a Japanese-born man, aged 32, employed as a baker, and associated with an address at 152 Thompson Street, Manhattan, New York City. These details correspond strikingly with historical accounts of Jack Shirai, who lived and worked in New York, had connections with the restaurant and baking trades, was reportedly married, and worked in the Greenwich Village area. Most significantly, a previously published historical account describes Jack Shirai's apartment mailbox as bearing the inscription "Baker, Jack Shirai." The marriage record also identifies a woman whose surname was Baker as Koichi Shirai's wife. This additional coincidence deserves careful historical examination alongside the occupational, geographical, chronological, and biographical evidence. I, Takashi Shibata, independently identified the connection between this specific 1936 marriage record and the unresolved historical identity of Jack Shirai. I developed and publicly presented the identification that Koichi Shirai and Jack Shirai were the same individual. My historical conclusion is clear: Koichi Shirai was, in all likelihood, Jack Shirai. I consider the cumulative evidence sufficiently strong to support this identification as the leading historical explanation, rather than merely as one possibility among several equally plausible alternatives. Although a document explicitly linking the two names has not yet been independently verified, the convergence of evidence establishes a substantial case for a common identity. I claim research priority for my independent identification, historical interpretation, and dated public presentation of this specific connection. This paper presents my original contribution, its evidentiary basis, its limitations, and the documentary research required to establish the identification conclusively. 1. Original Discovery and Claim of Research Priority During my independent investigation into the historical identity of Jack Shirai, I located and examined a significant official marriage record preserved through the New York City Municipal Archives. The document is identified as: New York City Marriage Certificate No. 3986 Archival Identifier: M-M-1936-0003986 Date: January 17, 1936 Location: Manhattan, New York City The marriage record identifies: - Groom: Koichi Shirai - Age: 32 - Birthplace: Japan - Occupation: Baker - Bride: Bessie Baker - Bride's age: 34 - Recorded address: 152 Thompson Street, Manhattan, New York City The record also contains information concerning the groom's parents and the witnesses to the marriage. The historical importance of this discovery lies not simply in locating an existing public record. Its significance lies in recognizing that the person identified in the record could be the historically elusive Japanese volunteer Jack Shirai, and in constructing an original documentary argument connecting the two identities. I independently recognized the unusual convergence between Koichi Shirai's documented circumstances and the historical descriptions of Jack Shirai. I subsequently developed the argument that these were not two unrelated men sharing similar characteristics, but one individual appearing under different names in different historical sources. I explicitly claim priority for the independent discovery and public presentation of the connection between Koichi Shirai in Manhattan Marriage Certificate No. 3986 and Jack Shirai of the Spanish Civil War. My initial research findings were publicly presented through Zenodo on October 16, 2026, followed by revised research publications. These dated publications document my authorship, my identification argument, and the development of my research. I assert that I am the original discoverer and independent proponent of this specific documentary identification. This claim concerns my research contribution and its publicly documented chronology. It does not imply that the historical marriage certificate itself was previously unknown to archivists or that every possible unpublished earlier interpretation has been excluded. A comprehensive international priority review has not yet been completed, and formal recognition of an absolute worldwide first remains subject to independent verification. Nevertheless, the documented public presentation of this identification under my name provides a concrete basis for recognizing my contribution and research priority. 2. The Extraordinary Correspondence Between Koichi Shirai and Jack Shirai Historical accounts of Jack Shirai describe a Japanese man who lived in New York City before leaving for Spain to join the Republican cause during the Spanish Civil War. Historian Hiroshi Kawanari investigated Jack Shirai's life and activities in detail. A March 11, 2022 article by journalist Ryusuke Kawai, discussing Kawanari's historical research, reported that Jack Shirai worked at a Japanese restaurant called "Shima" in Greenwich Village. The account also states that Shirai obtained a bakery license connected with the preparation of bread and cakes. It further recounts that the mailbox at the apartment where Jack Shirai lived before departing for Spain displayed the inscription: "Baker, Jack Shirai." This is a particularly significant detail. The official 1936 marriage certificate independently identifies Koichi Shirai's occupation as: "Baker." Thus, Jack Shirai's reported connection with baking corresponds directly with the documented occupation of Koichi Shirai. There is also another remarkable coincidence. The marriage certificate names Koichi Shirai's wife as: Bessie Baker. The word "Baker" therefore occurs in three relevant contexts: 1. Koichi Shirai's officially recorded occupation. 2. The surname of Koichi Shirai's wife, Bessie Baker. 3. The reported mailbox inscription associated with Jack Shirai. This convergence merits particular attention. The phrase "Baker, Jack Shirai" might represent an occupational designation, a household identification, a surname reference, or another form of contemporary labeling. The surviving secondary account alone cannot establish which interpretation is correct. The original mailbox, contemporary photographs, and independent documentation establishing the precise intended meaning have not yet been located. Furthermore, Baker is also an ordinary English-language surname, so the coincidence must not be treated as conclusive evidence by itself. Nevertheless, the coincidence becomes historically significant when examined together with the marriage record and the other biographical correspondences. If Koichi Shirai and Jack Shirai were unrelated individuals, one must explain why both men shared the same Japanese surname, the same general period of residence in New York, closely corresponding occupational backgrounds, evidence of marriage, and connections with the same small geographical area. A contemporary article provides additional support for this comparison. The June 25, 1942 issue of Pacific Citizen published an account of Jack Shirai describing his life as a restaurant worker in New York and referring to his wife. This contemporaneous account independently supports the historical description of Jack Shirai as a married man employed in restaurant work. It does not identify his wife as Bessie Baker, but it establishes another important point of correspondence. Taken together, the evidence reveals a striking combination of shared characteristics. I maintain that this combination is more convincingly explained by a single historical identity than by an assumption that two unrelated Japanese men named Shirai happened to share these circumstances. 3. The Geographical Significance of 152 Thompson Street and Greenwich Village One of the strongest elements of this investigation concerns geography. The marriage certificate places Koichi Shirai at: 152 Thompson Street, Manhattan, New York City. Historical accounts locate Jack Shirai's employment at the Japanese restaurant Shima in Greenwich Village. These locations belong to a closely connected historical urban environment. In December 2016, the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission designated the Sullivan-Thompson Historic District. The official designation encompasses property associated with 152–154 Thompson Street. The district forms part of the historically interconnected area commonly discussed in relation to South Village and Greenwich Village. This geographical relationship is important because modern neighborhood names cannot automatically be projected backward onto the urban geography of the 1930s. A present-day description placing a property in or near SoHo does not, by itself, establish how residents understood their neighborhood in 1936. Historical community boundaries, comme
