title: Transimperial Manhood: Theodore Roosevelt and Gendered Politics in US-Japanese Relations
abstract: The gender ideology of no other US president has elicited as much scholarly fascination as that of Theodore Roosevelt. Historians have closely analyzed his transformation from sickly child to big stick-wielding outdoorsman, highlighting how his overbearing father, frontier experience, and the societal transformations of the Gilded Age shaped an idiosyncratic gendered worldview that guided his political decisions.1 Neil Cogan even argues that manhood was Roosevelt’s central political organizing principle, linking progressivism and global power concerns over civilizational struggle within a common gendered vision.2 So far, this literature has treated this vision as a domestic construct rooted in US socialization and projected outward through political actions. Such a reading overlooks the realities of the United States in which Roosevelt came into political maturity: an ascending empire embedded in global networks of shared imperial knowledge, culture, and practice. An avid reader and passionate traveler, Roosevelt actively and enthusiastically participated in this global system. How did it impact his gendered formation? What does this tell us about the role of gendered knowledge circulation in shaping imperial diplomatic culture?

title: Beyond State-Led Diplomacy: NGOs, Gender, and Japan’s Grassroots International Health Cooperation in Cold War Asia
abstract: Abstract Although imperial Japan had mobilized medicine for overseas expansion in Asia, the postwar Japanese state developed sustained international health programs only gradually. This article argues that the early history of Japan’s postwar international health cooperation cannot be written as a simple story of state-led diplomacy. Adopting trans-Asian and transwar perspectives, it situates this work amid Cold War politics, postwar diplomatic reconstruction, and the political legacies of empire. Focusing on the Japan Overseas Christian Medical Cooperative Service (JOCS), the Japan Leprosy Mission for Asia (JALMA), and the International Nursing Foundation of Japan (INFJ), it shows that NGOs became central actors in sustained, personnel-based medical cooperation in Asia from the 1960s. Their activities expanded by mobilizing support across Christian communities, industrial philanthropy, and, in some cases, government agencies. The article also challenges male-centered histories of international cooperation by showing that female medical professionals, especially nurses, were central to sustaining the everyday medical work on the ground.

venue.name: East Asian Science Technology and Medicine

title: Kang Youwei's Views on the History of the Roman Empire (Based on the treatise “Journey to Italy”)
abstract: This article provides a translation of excerpts from Kang Youwei’s “Journey to Italy” (1904), devoted to the history of the Roman Empire. The founder and theorist of the 1898 Reform Movement, Kang Youwei had been interested in the history of non-European peoples since the age of 20. After visiting the British colony of Hong Kong, the young Confucian scholar became convinced that “Europeans cannot be considered as a barbarians.” Judging by his “Japanese Bibliography”, also published in 1898, Kang Youwei was familiar with Japanese educational publications from the Ministry of Education, including the 10-volume “Essays on the History of Rome”. “Journey to Italy”, published after Kang Youwei’s journey from Naples to Rome, Florence, Milan, and Venice, combined traditional Chinese genres of travel writing and historical-ethnographic description. In presenting the succession of Roman emperors, Kang Youwei relied mainly on guides rather than written sources.

title: Empire, Ireland and global ecologies: plant hunting and botanical exchange, c. 1780-1960
abstract: This article explores the global interconnectedness of plants and trees across the late-eighteenth to mid-twentieth centuries through the lens of the gardens, demesnes and wider estates of two significant aristocratic Ulster Irish estates: Mount Stewart and Clandeboye, both in Co. Down. They are remarkable for the scale of their plant collections, which are global in range and often colonial in origin. This article explores the motivations behind their creation and what their ecological, political and cultural legacies represent today, in light of contemporary climate challenges. It will also examine the practicalities of their creation, through the activities of plant hunters and botanical networks including Kew Gardens London, the Arnold Arboretum (Harvard University) and the Royal Botanic Gardens, Edinburgh. The landed families of Mount Stewart and Clandeboye leveraged their position and networks to patronise plant collectors in China, Japan, North America, India, Burma, South Africa and Chile, amongst other places. Plant collectors have left a complex legacy focused on, first, the dynamics of Western and Indigenous knowledges and second, the legacy of genetic hybridisation, naturalisation and evolution of plants which have since become stalwarts in many British and Irish gardens.

title: Hierarchies of Flesh: Racialised Embodiment on the Thai-Burma Railway in Richard Flanagan's The Narrow Road to the Deep North (2013)
abstract: This article reads The Narrow Road to the Deep North (2013) through the lens of the racialised body, arguing that the labouring on the Thai-Burma railway exposes the unequal valuation of human life under empire. Whilst the novel is often understood as a meditation on white Australian suffering, masculinity, and memory, its most unsettling insight lies in its attention to those who are already marked as marginal within their respective societies before the war begins. Focusing on Darky Gardiner, an Indigenous Australian soldier, and Choi Sang-min, a Korean conscript in the Japanese army, this article traces how the railway intensifies pre-existing hierarchies, rendering certain bodies especially vulnerable to violence and erasure. Through a close reading of Darky’s brutal beating and death, this article explores how the body becomes the primary site upon which imperial power is exercised. Darky’s destruction is not exceptional but continuous with the racial logics that precede the camp. Choi Sang-min’s violence, however, reflects the unstable position of the colonised subject compelled to perform authority through brutality – in many ways, their interactions can be framed as the ultimate violence of colonisation. In foregrounding these intersecting trajectories, the novel reveals war not as simply a rupture, but as an intensification of the structures that render some lives less visible and, ultimately, seen as less human.

venue.name: FORUM University of Edinburgh Postgraduate Journal of Culture & the Arts

title: Stability Without Stagnation: Comparative Reflections on Governance Reforms under Tokugawa Ieyasu of Japan and Alaafin Abiodun of Ọyọ Empire
abstract: Abstract This paper interrogates governance, stability, and social change under Tokugawa Ieyasu of Japan and Alaafin Abiodun of the Ọyọ Empire to assess the ability of pre-modern states to maintain order without stagnation. The study, based on historical and comparative analysis, examines the institutional, economic, cultural and intellectual reforms undertaken by both leaders and their strategies for consolidating power and maintaining societal cohesion. Tokugawa Ieyasu’s centralisation, codification of laws and promotion of Neo-Confucian ethics resulted in a long period of peace and cultural efflorescence, while Alaafin Abiodun’s governing of the Ọyọmesi, vassal towns and ritualised governance ensured political stability and the transmission of oral knowledge. Nevertheless, for all these successes, each polity had to grapple with inherent contradictions and structural constraints: rigid hierarchies, economic pressures, succession disputes and constraints on innovation demonstrated the difficulties of long-term stability. The comparative analysis shows that effective governance required dealing with authority, economic matters, and cultural guardianship, but depended on the context, norms of society, and individual leader. A comparative analysis of these cases shows the intricate relationship between stability, institutional reform and societal development, providing insights into how pre-modern states maintained continuity, change and modernisation in complex socio-political environments. The findings point to the possibility that stability and intellectual, cultural and economic progress could go hand in hand, but within limits set by historical and structural conditions. The study uses the comparative-historical institutional approach. It uses a controlled comparison of two pre-modern polities, which are politically and culturally different, in an effort to evaluate the impact of institutional arrangements on changing political stability into economic, social and cultural dynamism. Keywords: Tokugawa Japan, Ọyọ Empire, governance reforms, institutional consolidation, cultural development, comparative history

title: Multiple Diplomatic Centers
abstract: Abstract Diplomatic interactions between Japanese Shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu and Ming emperor Zhu Di, together with the Ming-Japanese tally trade, have received lively scholarly discussion. This article examines a period before the tally trade momentarily became the major diplomatic channel in Sino-Japanese exchanges. By cross-referencing and comparing sources from China and Japan, the author highlights how various players such as Zhu Yuanzhang, Buddhist monks, Prince Kaneyoshi, Go-Enyū tennō, and Kyushu warrior leaders participated in overseas exchanges. The author argues that the lively diplomatic exchanges between Kyushu and China confirm the existence of multiple diplomatic centers beyond Kyoto. The author proposes seeing Ming's rulership in this light and rethinking it in a broader East Asian context. In particular, Zhu Yuanzhang's flexible policies and careful examination of overseas envoys demonstrate that early Ming's overseas policies cannot be summarized simply as conservative and inward-looking. Instead, they show a high degree of openness and variation in the conduct of overseas affairs. By comparing diplomatic exchanges written in different languages and from different sides, the author argues for the need to move beyond political and territorial boundaries to consider important concepts such as rulership, empire, and imperial order in a connected and transregional perspective.

title: Correlation between Racconigi Bargain and the Russo-Japanese War
abstract: This article examines the origins, content, and historical significance of the Racconigi bargain (1909), one of the first formal approchements between the Kingdom of Italy and the Russian Empire. Set against the backdrop of the Russo-Japanese War (1904–1905) and the Bosnian Crisis (1908), the study explores how the shifting balance of power in Europe and the Mediterranean shaped the strategic calculations of both states. Based on Italian historical-diplomatic archive of the Italian Foreign Office and recent historiography, the article argues that Russia’s defeat in Easten Asia and Italy’s colonial setback at Adwa (1896) produced a partial strategic rethinking, leading each country to explore new possible political, diplomatic and military partnerships. While the Racconigi bargain was deliberately vague – expressing mutual support for Russian interests in the Straits and Italian ambitions in North Africa and cooperation in the Balkans – it represented a milestone in Italy’s gradual disengagement from the Triple Alliance and in Russia’s attempt to counterbalance Austro-Hungary and Ottoman Empire presence on its borders. From the Italian perspective, it will also represent an attempt of relaunch of its expansionist ambitions. The article also reviews the more significant historiography on the subject. Ultimately, the study shows that the Racconigi bargain appears as a paradigmatic case in order to illustrate the logic of multilateral pragmatism of both powers. In the body of the article, the historical facts confirmed by documents will obviously be clearly separated from the author’s interpretations, which in any case will be marked by prudence and the need to further explore them in future studies.

title: Binhai Railway Project in 1914–1917
abstract: This article examines the origins and discussions of the Harbin – Heihe Railway project, which became the Russian Empire’s final transport and economic initiative in China. The project emerged amid complex global and regional political and economic conditions, including the events of World War I, the growth of Japanese influence in Manchuria, and trends in foreign railway investment in China. Unlike the contract for the construction of the Chinese Eastern Railway, the Binhei Railway was to be financed through a loan, placing it on par with other railway projects in China at the time. This railway has been scantily studied in global historiography. The Russian-Chinese negotiations on its construction, the conclusion of the contract for its construction in March 1916, and the subsequent discussions remain the least explored part of the history of Russian-Chinese relations. This article attempts to fill these gaps. Specifically, the author examines the preconditions and reasons for concluding the contract for the new line in Manchuria and trends in international transport policy in this part of China in previous years. An analysis of Russia’s objectives, China’s interests, and the Russian-Chinese discussions on the issue are provided. The draft agreement between the Russo-Chinese Bank and the Chinese government and the direct contact of March 14, 1916 are examined. Using original sources, the economic development plan for the project is examined. The conclusions demonstrate that the project’s true purpose was to connect the CER with Blagoveshchensk, which would have elevated Russia’s political and economic influence in Northern Manchuria to a new level.

title: Infrastructure Narrative in Post-Defeat Japan: Revisiting of Yuriko Miyamoto’s Bansyu-Heiya
abstract: This article rereads Yuriko Miyamoto’s Banshu Heiya (1946) as a post-defeat infrastructure narrative rather than an author-centered or realist text. Focusing on Hiroko’s island-spanning journey, it examines how the collapse, redirection, and residue of imperial infrastructures— transportation, electricity, radio, policing, and logistics—structure human experience through the lenses of mobility and immobility. The novel maps a shift from wartime surveillance to postwar precarity: buses patrolled by gendarmes exemplify how surveillance became internalized, while the emperor’s faint radio voice demystifies sovereignty into mere electrical vibrations. Furthermore, broken rail lines transform trains into “debacle trains”, shifting them from a space of wartime mobilization to a chaotic site of institutional collapse. The military bypass road built by forced Korean laborers also demonstrates how imperial logistics disrupted ecological balance, ultimately accelerating devastating floods. While Abashiri Prison condenses absolute immobilization, the post defeat landscape forces individuals to navigate improvised networks— waiting, walking, and utilizing trucks or handcarts—to substitute for failed systems. Through these encounters, Miyamoto reveals the colonial substrate of imperial circulation and shows how its ruins persist as nonfunctional remains. Read this way, Banshu Heiya records not only material devastation but an ethical reorientation: freedom of movement emerges as a fragile, embodied practice learned in the gaps of a ruined empire, aligning with what mobility studies term “mobility justice.” Building on earlier research on the historical significance of August 15, 1945, and gendered movement, this essay argues that postwar subjectivity is fundamentally rewired through sensory encounters with damaged infrastructures.

title: The Compilation of Aguk ryaksa (A Brief History of Russia) and Its Representation of Russian History during the Period of Russo-Japanese Balance of Power (1896–1904)
abstract: This article examines the formation of Aguk ryaksa (A Brief History of Russia, 1898), its mode of narrating Russian history, and the ways in which its circulation and reception shaped Korean perceptions of Russia during the Russo-Japanese balance-of-power period (1896–1904). Adapted and translated by Hyeon Chae and published by the Editorial Bureau of the Ministry of Education, Aguk ryaksa was the first book on Russian history issued in Korea. This study traces its textual genealogy through a close comparison with Walter Keating Kelly’s The History of Russia (1854–1855) and its Chinese translation, Eshi jiyi (1886). It also analyzes records concerning the book’s distribution and use in examinations alongside contemporary newspaper editorials. Aguk ryaksa was not merely an abridged translation of Eshi jiyi into mixed-script Korean. Hyeon omitted nineteen of its seventyseven chapters and reduced thirteen others to roughly one line each, while appending material on Russia from the literary Chinese edition of Samin pilji. He sharply reduced detailed accounts of warfare and religion but selectively retained depictions of the tyranny and cruelty of Russian monarchs, the treatment of the people, the fall and resistance of Poland, and repression in conquered territories. Most notably, he reproduced almost in full the fourteen-point Testament of Peter the Great and added a warning, absent from his source text, of Russian designs on Qing China and Korea. These choices reflected a biographical mode of historical writing that assessed character through words and deeds, as well as a Confucian, people-centered standard that judged rulers by their treatment of the people. Aguk ryaksa circulated through the Ministry of Education’s distribution to schools, its use in examination questions, and the commercial book market. Its central narratives were reproduced in Hwangseong sinmun and Jeguk sinmun and appear to have been echoed later in Shin Gyu-sik’s Hanguk hon. By portraying Russia as an expansionist and brutal empire, the book provided an intellectual basis for gongno uisik (恐露意識), or fear of Russia, in Korean society. This case shows how negative views of Russia originating in Britain reached Korea through Chinese translation networks and were actively appropriated and reshaped according to the Korean Empire’s concerns for national survival and its Confucian understanding of history.

title: Industrial and Commercial Policy of the Residency-General and the Differentiation of Korean Merchants
abstract: This article examines the basic orientation and actual operation of the Residency-General’s industrial and commercial policies, as well as the responses of Korean merchants across different social strata, in order to identify concretely the impact that Korea’s transformation into a protectorate following the Eulsa Treaty had on Korean merchants. The Residency-General’s industrial and commercial policies possessed characteristics specific to the protectorate period that cannot be fully explained merely by emphasizing their exploitative and coercive aspects. Rather than directly investing capital in or managing Korean industry and commerce, the Residency-General sought to reorganize and control them indirectly by supporting the expansion of private capital, including Japanese merchants and companies. To this end, it adopted a dual approach: dismantling the privileged commercial system of the Daehan Empire, which hindered the advance of Japanese capital, while tolerating the privileges of pro-Japanese forces and Korean-Japanese joint ventures. It also facilitated the rapid establishment of Japanese companies and factories by providing a range of administrative conveniences and support measures. This policy approach was adopted amid Japan’s worsening fiscal deficits after the Russo-Japanese War and the political and diplomatic constraints arising from the continued, if only nominal, existence of the Daehan Empire. It was a significant feature of economic policy during the protectorate period, distinct from the period after annexation, when colonial power led by the Government-General began to assume an active role in colonial development and industrial control. It is also noteworthy that the Residency-General’s industrial and commercial policies did not affect Korean merchants uniformly. For established privileged merchant groups, such as sijeon merchants and influential Gaek-ju, the policies implemented by the Residency-General created a dual pressure: the loss of the protection and support previously provided by the Daehan Empire, and the expanding presence of Japanese merchants. Yet these developments did not bring about the collapse of all privileged merchants. Many merchants who failed to adapt to the changes brought by the Residency-General’s policies lost their existing economic foundations and declined rapidly. Others, however, sought survival through commercial transactions and joint ventures with Japanese capitalism, or maintained their commercial bases and established new foundations for growth by specializing and concentrating in sectors where Japanese capital had made relatively limited inroads. The Residency-General’s policies also had ambivalent effects on non-privileged merchant groups, including Store Merchants and peddlers. Retail trade, in which many non-privileged merchants were engaged, was one of the sectors most actively entered by Japanese merchants after the Russo-Japanese War. Small-scale Korean shops and peddlers thus faced severe competition for survival from the rapidly growing number of Japanese retailers. At the same time, however, the disappearance of the privileges of sijeon merchants and Gaek-ju, who had formerly exploited them, created opportunities for some Store Merchants and peddlers to overcome intense commercial competition and expand their businesses. Although the Residency-General dismantled the privileged commercial system in order to support the advance of Japanese capital, the resulting weakening of privileged merchants’ dominance—previously reinforced through their ties to the Daehan Empire—created space for formerly suppressed non-privileged merchants to emerge as new agents of commercial activity. These findings suggest that there are certain limitations to interpreting the economic history of Korea during the protectorate period through a dichotomous framework of the establishment of a colonial economic system and the expansion of Japanese capital, on the one hand, and the decline and resistance of Korean merchants, on the other.

title: Writing the world from the late Qing empire: gendered travel, knowledge, and reform in the work of Shan Shili and Qian Xun
abstract: This article reinterprets late Qing reform through the diplomatic travel writings of Qian Xun and Shan Shili, a married couple whose collaborative authorship articulated a culturally rooted yet globally informed vision of change. Introducing the concept of re-gendered companionship, it examines how literati couples mobilised shared authority, gendered perspective, and embodied experience to produce and circulate reformist knowledge. By analysing their complementary writings, including diplomatic reports, encyclopaedic entries, and travel narratives, the study shows how travel, education, and gendered agency became instruments of selective adaptation of foreign institutions. Japan functioned as a critical intermediary, mediating Western practices for Chinese audiences while shaping gendered observation and reflection. This framework challenges narratives that isolate male or female agency and reframes elite travel writing as a form of intellectual activism. Their coordinated authorship bridges literati traditions of companionship and emerging bureaucratic genres, situating reform in relational, cross-cultural, and gendered terms.

title: “Comfort girls-women” as Military Sex Slaves in the Japanese Empire (1937-1945)
abstract: This paper presents a critical historical and didactic analysis of the Japanese Imperial military sexual slavery system (1937–1945), examining its structural dimensions, historiographical challenges, and pedagogical implications for education. Despite extensive scholarly documentation, the so-called “comfort women” system remains marginalised within Eurocentric curricula and continues to be contested through Japanese state revisionism. This study analyses the institutionalisation of sexual violence as a military logistics strategy, the erasure of evidence through systematic document destruction, and the transformative role of survivor testimony, particularly Kim Hak-Sun’s 1991 public deposition, in reconfiguring individual trauma into a transnational human rights struggle. The research proposes a didactic intervention, operationalising Seixas and Morton's “Big Six” historical thinking concepts through source analysis, collaborative digital mapping exercises, and ethical reflection tasks. Findings demonstrate that the system constituted a structurally integrated state crime rather than isolated wartime atrocities, while the pedagogical programme effectively decentres Eurocentric narratives and cultivates multiperspectival historical consciousness. The study concludes that teaching “difficult knowledge” about gendered wartime violence not only addresses historiographical omissions but also fulfills history education's civic responsibility to foster active citizenship and human rights awareness. This intervention offers a replicable model for integrating overlooked Asian-Pacific theatres into European curricula while navigating the ethical complexities of teaching traumatic histories.

title: The Contested Frontiers of Japan’s Empire in the Americas
‘Better emulate the Irish resistance’: Influences of the Irish literary revival on Taiwanese literature and politics during and after the Japanese occupation
abstract: The Irish Literary Revival emerged in response to centuries of cultural suppression and linguistic marginalisation in Ireland under British rule, alongside disillusionment with the Home Rule movement. It sought to define Irishness, revive the Irish language, and construct a distinct national literature, ultimately contributing to the Easter Rising of 1916 and the formation of the Irish Free State. This movement resonated in colonial Taiwan under Japanese rule (1895–1945), where Irish nationalist writing was widely read and discussed, shaping anti-colonial intellectual currents and independence aspirations. From 1898 onwards, over 600 articles on Ireland appeared in Taiwan, and activists such as Lin Xiantang 林獻堂 drew inspiration from Irish resistance strategies via exchanges with Liang Qichao 梁啟超 in Japan. This culminated in cultural organisations and petitions for a Taiwanese parliament modelled on Irish self-determination. Post-1920s translations of Irish literature and adaptations of Irish nationalist theatre, including works by W. B. Yeats and J. M. Synge, circulated across the Japanese Empire and influenced Taiwanese literary production. Following the end of the Second World War, after Taiwan was returned to the Republic of China under Kuomintang rule, postcolonial Irish literary models continued to inform Taiwanese cultural discourse. This paper examines how Ireland functioned as both an explicit and implicit model for Taiwanese national identity formation and literary resistance, providing examples from relevant literary works over time.

title: Sleeping with the enemy: Britain, Japanese troops and the Netherlands East Indies, 1945-1946
abstract: Between September 1945 and November 1946, up to 35,000 surrendered Japanese troops were assimilated into Lord Louis Mountbatten's South East Asia Command in the Netherlands East Indies. Although under the ultimate control of British officers, the Japanese retained their wartime unit structures, were led by their own officers and remained armed. As a measure of their acceptance by the British, one of them was recommended for the Distinguished Service Order in November 1945, only three months after the war's end. The Japanese fought alongside the British despite the anger felt against them as the perpetrators of wartime atrocities and as a former enemy. These sentiments, however, did not prevent senior military personnel and politicians from using the Japanese to assist in the restoration of pre-war European empires in Asia. Crucially, the United States government tacitly supported the use of the Japanese. Aware of the sensitivity of using former enemy troops, the British and Americans tried to conceal the extent of Japanese involvement. Their success in achieving this hid not just their own hypocrisy but also the important part played by the Japanese in securing Allied post-war aims in Asia.

title: Фиксация исторической памяти в городском пространстве Сеула
abstract: The loss of Korea’s independence in 1910 and its incorporation into the Japanese Empire, followed by its division along the 38th parallel, initiated the formation of a trauma-memory. This trauma is linked to the specific nature of its liberation - a consequence of Japan’s surrender in World War II-decolonization, and the intensification of the struggle for democratization in the Republic of Korea during the 1960s-1980s. This article analyzes memorial sites created within the framework of traumatic narratives. These sites reflect state policies, official memory, personal histories, and the histories of small communities-specifically, the stories of "comfort women" and the victims of the democratization struggle, which entered the realm of public history by the end of the 20th century.

title: The Russian Empire through the Prism of the Peripheral Press: “Kirghiz Steppe Newspaper” on the Specifics of the Region, turn of the 20th century
abstract: This article discusses the history of the provincial newspaper "Kirghiz Steppe Newspaper" in the Steppe Governorate-General in the late 19th century.The focus is on the forming an editorial board from among the elite of Kazakh society -the Chingizids who conducted educational work; and the placement of informational materials about China, Persia, and Japan, folk healers on the pages of the imperial Russian newspaper.The study draws on the original source -the newspaper itself, which became the first to appear in the steppe expanses of Central Asia.The publication's birth and existence for over twenty years testified to the state's interest in the region and the adjacent territories of Persia, the Qing Empire, and Far East.The involvement of the local Kazakh elite in the newspaper reflects a dialogue that facilitated the rapprochement of the cultures of the peoples of Eurasia.While the official section of the newspaper printed relevant information, the second half of the publication, in Kazakh on Arabic script, featured essays on the ethnography and folk healers, helpful tips, information on regional seasonal fairs, and prices for livestock.The content of the newspaper columns can be considered a kind of original archive of data on the daily life of the Steppe region.

title: The Policy of the Muscovite Tsars Towards the Jesuit Mission in South-East Asia
abstract: The expansion of the Jesuit order was accompanied from the start by an apostolic dynamism which left a mark on almost every domain. 1 Special interest should be paid amongst other things to the involvement of the Jesuits in missionary and diplomatic work, which demanded of the Jesuit Order a thorough and all round education, but also a quick and reasonably safe means of transport from one region of the globe to another, a factor which often played a principle part in the success or failure of a venture.In these times, journeys to Asia, especially to China, India and Japan, were most often undertaken by sea, a rather unsafe and time consuming form of travel which delayed the missionary-diplomatic cause or brought about unconquerable perturbations.For this reason the Jesuits sought other, more direct and comfortable routes which led through the land-locked areas of Central Asia, far to the north of the Himalayas.Such land routes had to pass through Siberia, a territory which had already by the XVIIIth century been conquered by the Russian empire, whose eastern frontiers bordered with China.According to many authors it appears that, apart from a few Rusian and Mongolian merchants and army couriers, no-one knew exactly the ideal route which existed independent of the Silk Route or the Tea Route, kept in strictest secrecy before all foreigners.The Jesuits probably gained more information about the secret Siberian trail for the first time from Prince Fiodor Golovin, who came as the Tsar's envoy to Peking to the court of emperor Kanghi to discuss the matter of the increased conflict along the border between the two empires.2 It was perhaps at the time of this mission that the Jesuit, Father Verbiest, in the employ of the Chinese emperor as official translator during Russo-Chinese negotiations, was first able to observe the Kremlin's policy towards China and render Prince Golovin his services.Services which were later beneficial in gaining information by the Jesuits on the land route, not only to China but to the whole of Asia.

title: A Critical Review of the Battle of Bongodongb : Focusing on the Issue of Command Authority
abstract: This study critically examines existing scholarship on the command authority of the Battle of Bongodong, fought on June 7, 1920, and seeks to reassess the organizational formation of the Daehan Bukro Dokgunbu (Korean Northern Military Command) and its command structure during the battle. Previous studies and general historical accounts have maintained that Hong Beom-do exercised effective command over the Battle of Bongodong and have defined the Daehan Bukro Dokgunbu as an organization formed through a “three-group alliance” of the Daehan Gunmu Dodokbu, the Daehan Gungminhoe, and the Daehan Dongnipgun. However, an examination of contemporary historical sources reveals that Hong Beom-do’s Daehan Dongnipgun had already formed an alliance with the Daehan Gungminhoe before the establishment of the Daehan Bukro Dokgunbu. This study also draws attention to the fact that the written pledge produced at the time of its establishment identifies the military committees of the Daehan Gunmu Dodokbu and the Daehan Gungminhoe as the principal parties to the integration. Furthermore, this study examines the role of commanders as prescribed in the Infantry Drill Regulations (步兵操典), a military manual compiled during the Korean Empire, and compares these principles with accounts in The Independent (獨立新聞), materials of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea, memoirs of independence fighters who participated in the battle, and Japanese records. It also demonstrates that early historical works on the Korean independence war identified Choi Jin-dong as the commander of the Battle of Bongodong. Based on these findings, this study presents a new possibility that Choi Jin-dong served as the commander who exercised overall command of the Battle of Bongodong and calls for further research on this issue.

title: Administrative Reorganization of the North Gyeongsang Region During the Late Joseon Dynastyand the Japanese Colonial Period
abstract: This article summarizes the overall trends in administrative reorganization in the North Gyeongsang region during the transition to modernity. In 1894, the Military Affairs Bureau compiled data on 63 eup in Gyeongsang Province to serve as a basis for fiscal reform and administrative reorganization. In January 1895, the Park Yeong-hyo Cabinet pushed for a pilot consolidation of gun and hyun based on their size and distance, merging the small town of Chilgok into Daegu. In May of the same year, with the implementation of the 23-bu system, the administrative ranks of gun and hyun were unified as “gun,” and the North Gyeongsang region was divided into two jurisdictions—Daegu-bu and Andong-bu—with Uiseong-gun serving as the boundary. In 1896, the government abolished the 23-bu system and reorganized the country into a system of 13 provinces, 8 bu, and 1 mok, based on the principle of “old as the foundation, new as the supplement.” Consequently, Gyeongsang Province was divided into northern and southern regions, and North Gyeongsang Province (comprising 41 counties), with Daegu as its capital, was established. While this marked the culmination of the reorganization of the local administrative system during the late Joseon period, it had the limitation of being merely a superficial division of the province, failing to address the imbalances among counties and prefectures resulting from differences in jurisdictional size and natural topography. In July 1906, the Resident-General’s Office pushed for the consolidation and abolition of counties with the aim of improving administrative efficiency and streamlining finances. In North Gyeongsang Province, a total of 17 counties were targeted for consolidation, but the plan was temporarily suspended due to public opposition. Consequently, the Resident-General’s Office shifted its focus to resolving extraterritorial areas. Gyeongsang Province, which accounted for 18.6% of the nation’s extraterritorial areas, was identified as the primary target. As a result, the territories of large towns that had previously held extensive exclaves were reduced, while neighboring counties benefited by incorporating those areas. However, due to differences in opinion between the Korean Empire and the Resident-General’s Office, the administrative reorganization during the Resident-General’s period remained incomplete. After the Annexation of Korea, the Japanese colonial government reorganized administrative districts into a system of provinces, prefectures, counties, and townships, standardizing complex subordinate designations to “township.” The Government-General of Korea proposed an area of 40 bang-ri and 10,000 households as the standard for a county and pushed for a large-scale consolidation ; as a result, North Gyeongsang Province was reduced from 41 existing bu and counties to 24. During the reorganization process, economic strength, living areas, and topography were taken into consideration, and new counties were established and renamed to center around colonial strongholds. Furthermore, this led to the elevation of certain myeons—primarily those with Japanese populations—to county status and the strengthening of Japanese rule.

title: THE DEBT IS A MIRROR (REVISED-2) : A Practical, Seductive, Beneficial-for-All Architecture for a Sovereign, Deterministic Civilization
abstract: We began this conversation with a simple question: "Could it be that all finances—of individuals, corporates, and nations—end by beingdebt-driven?" The answer, we discovered, was yes. But that was only the surface. We peeled back the layers and found:· Ego: The refusal to accept limits, the need to consume tomorrow's resources today.· Myopia: The biological, neurological, and structural bias toward instant gratification.· Stupidity: The collective inability to learn from 5,000 years of collapsed empires, despiteholding the receipts.· The Handstand: An entire civilization walking on its head—consuming the effect (wealth)before the cause (production), held upright only by constant, frantic energy.· The Original Sin: From Adam and Eve to the first Mesopotamian grain loan, humanity hasbeen borrowing divinity against humanity, consuming now and passing the bill to the future. We also acknowledged:"Religions were simply inefficient." They preached humility but never built a system that enforced it. They outsourced justice to the afterlife and left the debt-creation machinery untouched. Then we looked at the present moment:· U.S. debt: **$40 trillion**, adding $1 trillion every 4 months.· Japan: 250% debt-to-GDP, the highest in the developed world.· Interest payments exceeding defense budgets.· A trajectory that mathematically breaks within 10–12 years. And then we saw the Energy Wall—Q4 2026, just 5 weeks away:· AI data centers consuming entire cities' worth of electricity.· 30–50% of planned capacity delayed due to grid bottlenecks.· Transformer lead times: 128 weeks.· Switchgear: sold out until 2028. The system isn't just walking on its head anymore. It's doing a handstand on a tightrope,blindfolded, juggling flaming torches, while the rope is on fire. Then came the original "The Debt Is a Mirror" —a magnificent, comprehensive, spirituallygrounded blueprint for a non-debt, sovereign, deterministic civilization. We honored it. We praised it. And then we reality-checked it.

title: Visual Politics of the Japanese Empire and the Dehistoricization of the South Seas Mandate: Representing Tropical Space in Postcard Images
abstract: This study examines how the South Seas Mandate (Nan’yō) was visually constructed through postcards produced under the Japanese Empire. While the South Seas Mandate functioned as a key site of Japan’s southward expansion, it was not simply incorporated into the imperial domain as a pre-given space; rather, it required cultural and visual mediation in order to be recognized within Japanese society as a “new southern region.” In this process, postcards played a central role in shaping how the region was perceived and imagined. Focusing on approximately twelve postcard images, this study argues that the South Seas Mandate was represented as a dehistoricized tropical space through a systematic visual regime. These postcards repeatedly depict tropical landscapes and indigenous life while largely excluding historical traces and social conditions. Through this selective visual composition, the region is presented not as a historically layered place but as a stable and timeless environment. At the same time, images of modern infrastructure and administrative space depict the South Seas Mandate as an ordered and governed environment, while omitting the violence and labor underlying colonial development. Building on Edward W. Said’s insight into the ahistorical logic of imperial representation, and extending the critique articulated by Naoto Horikiri regarding the surface-oriented and depoliticized nature of Japan’s southern imagination, this study demonstrates that visual images did not merely reflect colonial space but actively produced it. In particular, it shows how these representations contributed to the production of topophilia, understood as an affective attachment to place mediated through visual images. By analyzing these visual strategies, this study argues that the South Seas Mandate was not simply represented but actively constructed as a “tropical paradise” through imperial visual politics. In doing so, it highlights how colonial space was produced not only through physical control, but also through the organization of perception and affect.

title: Foreigners and People of Other Faiths Outside the Train Window. Imperial Space and the Empire’s Frontier as Perceived by Railway Travellers against the Backdrop of the Russo-Japanese War
abstract: This article offers a comparative analysis of the railway travelogues written by Russian participants in the 1904–1905 military campaign in Manchuria, who described their journey from European Russia to the Far East, including their travel on the Transsib and the CER, and their crossing of the border with China. The aim of the study is to compare the narrators’ perceptions of the ethno-confessional composition of the imperial space as a whole and of the Far Eastern imperial frontier. The outbreak of war coupled with the resurgence of the “Yellow Peril” narrative gave a powerful impetus to the emergence of such texts, which remained in demand and were reprinted in book form in the immediate post-war years. A discursive analysis is tested on selected examples, suitable for a prospective, comprehensive study of the full corpus of similar sources. Particular attention is paid to the specifics of observing those who are ethnically and religiously “other” in the communicative context of travel-related mobility, which lends a new perspective to traditional imperial discourse. Preliminary conclusions reveal, alongside the presence in the texts of traditional stereotypes of Russian Orientalism, a significant ambivalence in the authors’ conceptions of the “civilising project” of the Far Eastern vector amidst the vagueness and variability of the mutual correlation between geographical and ethnographic objects. This study may be of interest to specialists in the social sciences and humanities focusing on issues of imagology, on the study of mass consciousness and the communication environment, and on the history of transport routes.

title: Exiles, Refugees, and Evangelists: Missionary and Chinese Christian Mobility in the Asia–Pacific War, 1937–1945
abstract: This article analyses the impact of the Asia–Pacific War on Protestant missions and Chinese Christians. I examine how the movement of missionaries and Chinese Christians as exiles, refugees, and prisoners of Japanese forces shaped how Protestant Christians understood the war’s impact on the fate of Christianity and colonial empires in Asia. Mobility as a lens also highlights how the repeal of extraterritoriality and Chinese exclusion impacted relations between China and the Allied Powers. I argue that the war shattered ideas associated with missionary mobility from the imperialist era such as freedom and supposed racial superiority to Chinese. New meanings associated with mobility formed that promoted racial equality with Chinese Christians as the new ‘pioneers’, who were increasingly upwardly mobile and independent. Conversely, the Asia–Pacific War aggravated issues rooted in race, class, and imperialism, tensions that lingered underneath the surface of cooperation between Chinese Christians and foreign missions before exploding in the postwar era. Thus, the article complicates historical studies of China and Christianity by highlighting how the war portended many Chinese Christians embracing Mao Zedong and the postwar expulsion of Protestant missionaries.

title: The Subversion of the “Futei Senjin” Discourse and the Limits
abstract: This study examines From Behind You (Nandō no Haigo yori, 汝等の背後より), a novel by Nakanishi Inosuke, focusing on how the text critiques the dominant colonial discourse of imperial Japan regarding colonial Korea while simultaneously revealing the limitations inherent in its representation of the colonized. Drawing on Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak’s theory of representation, this paper analyzes the discourse of Futei Senjin (“unruly Koreans”), the colonial systems of law and education, the gendered representation of the colonial Other, and the politics of sacrifice. The novel subverts the Futei Senjin discourse produced by the imperial security apparatus and exposes the ways in which colonial police and judicial institutions constructed Koreans as criminals. It also illustrates how colonial education internalized admiration for the Japanese Empire and desires for assimilation among the colonized, while simultaneously revealing the fictitious nature of such ideological indoctrination through depictions of legal dispossession and sexual violence. Kwon Juyŏng is portrayed as a figure embodying the suffering and resistance of colonial women, yet she is also sexualized and othered through the gaze of imperial masculinity. Likewise, Cho Sŏngsik and Sin Ch’unyong are presented as independence activists, but their characters are fragmented by desires for recognition, petty heroism, and patriarchal domination. While this characterization constitutes an achievement of anti-heroic realism, it also reflects traces of internalized Orientalism that portray Korean resistance subjects as politically immature. Furthermore, the novel critiques not only the violence of colonial power but also the logic of sacrifice embedded within resistance discourse itself, thereby raising broader ethical questions concerning representation. Ultimately, From Behind You emerges as an anti-imperialist text that denounces colonial oppression while simultaneously revealing the ambivalence of a narrative that reconfigures colonized subjects within its own ideological and literary framework rather than fully restoring their voices. In this regard, the novel serves as an important text that demonstrates both the possibilities and limitations of anti-imperialist literature produced from within the imperial center.

title: The Evolution of the Image of Genghis Khan in the Takarazuka Revue
abstract: Abstract: This study examines three Genghis Khan-themed productions by the Takarazuka Revue— Jingisukan (1922), Mongōru (1941), and Kono koi wa kumo no hate made (1973)—through Homi Bhabha's postcolonial framework, tracing the transformation of Genghis Khan's image in modern Japan and its shifting political and cultural meanings. In the prewar era, Jingisukan recast the conqueror as a pan-Asian hero aligned with Taishō ideals, employing stage costuming and Ainu bear rituals to suggest cultural affinity. During the wartime period, Mongōru explicitly positioned Japan as the spiritual successor to the Mongol Empire, exemplifying what Bhabha terms the "menace of mimicry" (Bhabha 1994: 88) within the ideological logic of the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere. In the postwar context, Kono koi wa kumo no hate made shifted toward anti-war sentiment and personal emotion, though residual colonial ideologies remained embedded in its narrative. The evolving image of Genghis Khan thus exposes a central contradiction in Japan's modern nation-building: the attempt to assert national subjectivity through the othering of Mongolia, while remaining entangled in the hybridity intrinsic to colonial discourse. Ultimately, the study contends that the G=Y theory, as staged by Takarazuka, operates as a continually rewritten "cultural text," whose shifting trajectory vividly reflects Bhabha's insight into the ambivalence of colonial authority, oscillating between mimicry and menace (Bhabha 1994: 91).

title: Unified Libertarian Theory and the Russo-Japanese War
abstract: This article applies unified libertarian theory (ULT) to the Russo-Japanese War of 1904–5, a conflict often dismissed or overlooked in modern scholarship. In reexamining the war, this study argues that Japan’s initiation of hostilities met the threshold of justified coercion under ULT’s standards. Justified coercion does not mean morally correct but rather that the casus belli falls within the descriptive framework of state behavior outlined in “Unified Libertarian Theory: Genesis” (duHoffmann 2025) and will likely not incur the costs associated with unjustified coercion. During the lead-up to the war, Japan was surrounded by hostile empires, vulnerable to economic strangulation, underestimated, and facing a deteriorating security environment. Its interest in securing Korea as a defensive buffer and deterring Russian encroachment was grounded not in an ideology of expansionism but in the preservation of national autonomy. The failure of diplomacy and the demonstrated bad faith of the Russian Empire created a condition of necessity through Russia’s eastward expansion in which preemptive action became the only viable path to survival. Finally, the war’s execution was restrained, targeted, and concluded with a negotiated peace, satisfying the requirement of proportionality. Under ULT, the Russo-Japanese War emerges as a case in which offensive war functioned as a defense of liberty. When evaluating Japan’s strategy and situation holistically and as a response to structural vulnerability rather than simply as a bid for domination, the result is a picture of disciplined statecraft. In doing so, this article affirms ULT’s central claim that force, when bound by ethical clarity and strategic restraint, can serve the cause of liberty without corrupting it.

title: Architectures of Extermination: A Qualitative Comparative Analysis of Ideological Frameworks and Genocidal Motivation Across 16 Global Regimes
abstract: Genocide is among the gravest crimes of political life, yet the scholarly record remains fractured between richly detailed single-case histories and broad structural theories that struggle to explain why ostensibly similar conditions produce catastrophe in one context and quiescence in another. This dissertation addresses that fracture by asking a configurational question: which combinations of ideological frameworks drive regimes not merely toward repression but toward the deliberate destruction of human groups? Drawing on a set-theoretic logic that treats causation as complex, conjunctural, and equifinal, the study conducts a fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) of sixteen leader-regime cases spanning more than two and a half centuries, from the Qing conquest of the Dzungars in the 1750s to the Darfur campaign of the 2000s. Five ideological conditions are calibrated across all cases: ethnonationalism (ETH), class-based ideology (CLA), colonial extractivism (EXT), religious or ethnic supremacism (SUP), and imperial expansionism (EXP). The outcome measures the severity and completeness of genocidal execution among these confirmed genocidal regimes. The analysis is organized around an original theoretical architecture, the Ideological Prism, which refracts the diffuse concept of “ideology” into three functional modes through which mass violence is rationalized: teleological ideologies (class and empire) that frame destruction as a step toward an inevitable future; existential ideologies (ethnonationalism and supremacism) that construe the targeted group as a mortal threat to the body politic; and utilitarian ideologies (extractivism) that reduce a population to an obstacle standing between the regime and a coveted resource. Synthesizing Moses’s (2008) conception of genocide as a “logic of elimination,” Mann’s (2005) account of the dark side of democracy, and Midlarsky’s (2005) theory of the killing trap, the Prism reframes ideology not as a single variable but as the connective tissue binding state capacity to the will to exterminate. Results indicate that no single ideology is sufficient to explain the most lethal outcomes, but two conditions emerge as individually necessary for high genocidal severity: ethnonationalism (consistency = .93) and colonial extractivism (consistency = .97). The sufficiency analysis identifies two equifinal paths to catastrophic outcomes. The first, ~ETH*CLA*SUP*EXP, describes class-driven regimes fused with supremacist consolidation and explicit eliminationist intent in the relative absence of ethnonationalism, exemplified by Mao’s China and Tojo’s Japan. The second and empirically dominant path, ETH*EXT*SUP*EXP, captures ethnonationalist and expansionist regimes hardened by supremacism and intent, encompassing Hitler, Stalin, Milošević, Enver Pasha, the Qianlong Emperor, and Tsar Alexander II. Both paths achieve perfect consistency (1.0), and together they cover 80% of the outcome. All three hypotheses are supported: the pairing of ethnonationalism and expansionism proves sufficient in non-Marxist regimes (H1); class-based ideology becomes sufficient only when joined to supremacist consolidation (H2); and colonial extractivism generates attritional genocide even in the absence of ethnonationalism (H3). An independent methodological audit confirmed the computational accuracy of every necessity, sufficiency, and hypothesis result while flagging the interpretive limits inherent to a positive-case design, a modest sample, and substantial limited diversity. The study’s contribution is fourfold. Theoretically, it offers a multidimensional, set-theoretic model of genocidal motivation that accommodates causal complexity rather than legislating it away. Empirically, it provides the first systematic fsQCA comparison bridging pre-modern, modern, and contemporary genocides. Methodologically, it demonstrates the analytic purchase of QCA in a field long dominated by narrative case study. Practically, it speaks to the design of early-warning systems and the doctrine of the Responsibility to Protect by specifying the ideological signatures that precede mass atrocity. Read alongside its companion study of impunity dynamics (Pokorny, 2026), the dissertation illuminates both the motivational and the permissive halves of the genocidal equation: why regimes choose to destroy, and why the world so often lets them.

title: Family Rift: The Brothers Johannes and Richard Coudenhove-Kalergi Between the World Wars, 1918–1939
abstract: The article provides an insightful exploration of the intellectual world of Central European aristocracy in the interwar period. Using the example of two members of the Coudenhove-Kalergi family – Pan-European Union founder Richard and his older brother Johannes – it examines how the family navigated the challenges of a highly turbulent era. It compares the approaches of the two brothers, as well as those of other family members, to the political, national and economic issues facing Central Europe. The article highlights the significance of their family background in shaping their personalities, outlining their personal strategies while also pointing out both differences and shared traits. It demonstrates that, while the brothers had a strong connection to Japan through their mother, who was of Japanese origin, they remained part of the broader Germanic milieu of Central Europe. However, they were not nationalists; on the contrary, they viewed the efforts of some nations within the former Austro-Hungarian Empire to break away from the monarchy with disdain. At the same time, the article shows that during this period, they were only half-hearted monarchists, with neither envisioning the future of Central Europe as lying in the restoration of Habsburg rule. Furthermore, the article reveals that although Johannes and Richard did not agree on political or personal matters, their fundamental ideological orientation was not significantly different. Both opposed antisemitism but were critical of liberal democracy and expressed sympathies for far-right dictatorships, particularly the Italian regime, with Johannes even showing an affinity for Nazism. In this respect, both brothers (especially Johannes) could be described as conservative revolutionaries, though they diverged on essential details.

title: Expanding the horizons of AI governance: an interdisciplinary analysis of regulatory models in the EU, Brazil, and Japan
abstract: The global governance of artificial intelligence is emerging as a contested yet increasingly convergent regulatory field, in which states compete for normative leadership while contributing to the formation of shared standards. Against intensified “digital rivalry” and deregulatory pressures, this article examines AI regulatory frameworks beyond the traditional triad of digital powers. Building on Bradford’s “Digital Empires,” it adopts an interdisciplinary comparative law approach informed by law, ethics, political science, and psychology, focusing on the European Union, Brazil, and Japan.

title: Geopolityka w reportażach Konstantego Srokowskiego – W stolicy białego cara (1904) i Likwidacya caratu (1905) – na tle prekursorskiej myśli geopolitycznej (polskiej i rosyjskiej) (cz. I)
abstract: The excellent Polish publicist Konstanty Srokowski in his two reports – W stolicy białego cara and Likwidacya caratu – presents the image of Russia in the years 1904–1905, so during the war with Japan and the revolutionary boiling. In illustrating the political situation of that country, he notices the relationship between geographical and historical factors, and its emergence and functioning. Srokowskis observations and conclusions are sometimes convergent with the views of the creators of Russian geopolitics, not only Polish. Only partially did his political forecasts work. For example, he postulated the transformation of Russia into a federation. It was not until a dozen or so years later that the Bolsheviks did so, and even then only in name; nevertheless, federalism, as Russia’s form of government, survived the collapse of the USSR. The now-defunct Polish state was supposed to Europeanise Russia, so Srokowski believed that the Russians were wrong to abolish them. In addition, he claimed that Poles from the Russian partition should change their tactics towards the Russian Empire during the revolution that was underway at that time.

title: Reading O Changhwan Translating Sergey Esenin in Seoul, 1946
abstract: Abstract This article explores the allegorical layers of meaning that emerge from one translator-poet partnership in the aftermath of the collapse of the Japanese empire in Korea. The iconoclastic modernist poet O Changhwan’s first published book in a newly liberated Korea was a translation of poems by the deceased Russian poet Sergey Esenin. O was translating at a moment when the Korean language was returning to public life after suppression under colonial rule and amid escalating violence on the partitioned peninsula. Reading O’s translations and lengthy afterword opens a window onto the scene of Seoul in 1946, one year before O was to cross over the thirty-eighth parallel into the northern zone. With the aim of rethinking the creative legacies of the early Cold War, this article explores the many meanings created in and through O’s translation.

title: Los jesuitas y la globalización del reloj: balance historiográfico entre el Nuevo Mundo, China y Japón
abstract: Abstract. Objective/context: Historiography has established an inextricable link between the globalization of clocks and the worldwide expansion of the Society of Jesus. Based on the positive results obtained in the Far East through the gift of these machines, historians have dated the beginning of this phenomenon to the second half of the sixteenth century, tracing a route on the world map from Europe to China and Japan. This has implied that the Jesuits were clockmakers and that the Eastern empires were familiar with these mechanisms before the New World. The lack of studies on the Spanish viceroyalties led to the assumption that, in fact, they were introduced later and through the Church, extrapolating the Jesuit experience from the Eastern Hemisphere to the Western Hemisphere. This study aims to balance this historiography by specifying the number of Jesuit clockmakers worldwide and assessing their role in the globalization of clocks. Methodology: As much literature as possible on the Jesuits and clockmaking has been compiled for comparison with Spanish-American sources from the sixteenth to the eighteenth centuries. Originality: This work makes a valuable contribution to the study of the global history of the Society of Jesus, science, and technology by demonstrating how clocks circulated among the New World, China, and Japan and by assessing the Jesuits’ role in each hemisphere. Conclusions: This article revises the timeline and map of the globalization of clocks. Contrary to the prevailing historiographical consensus, this technology did not first leave Europe for the Far East around 1550. Rather, it departed from Spain via the Atlantic route in the early sixteenth century. In the New World, clocks were introduced as administrative tools decades before the Society of Jesus or the Church adopted them. In China and Japan, the Jesuits offered them as diplomatic gifts to spread Christianity, initially relying on an Indigenous clockmaker from the Canary Islands whose journey to Zhaoqing provides clues about other key actors in understanding the global phenomenon of the clock.

title: The Transnational Spread of ‘Whiggish Shakespeare’ in School Education from Britain to Japan, 1870–1945
abstract: This article examines the transnational spread of Shakespeare, particularly his biographies and prose adaptations of King Lear, from Britain to Japan, focusing on locally produced English readers for use in secondary schools between 1870 and 1945. Such materials were largely derived from school readers produced in Britain to educate working-class children, following the Education Act of 1870. Those British source texts were informed by Whig–Liberal narratives of progressive history. In that framework, Shakespeare became a self-made and civic figure, while Cordelia served to challenge the misuse of political and parental authority. When introduced into Japan’s educational context, the Whig interpretation of Shakespeare intersected with intellectual efforts to pursue social and political reform to build a nation-state and an empire compatible with Great Britain. Because Japanese intellectuals perceived Whig–Liberal thinking as indispensable for Japan’s modernisation, the poet was mobilised as a liberal cultural resource able to bolster reformist aspirations. By the 1920s, however, as liberal elements became subsumed within a more explicitly nationalistic educational agenda, Shakespeare became a figure institutionally oriented towards the cultivation of imperial subjects and thus marked Japan’s gradual departure from British liberal paradigms.

title: ВЗАИМООТНОШЕНИЯ РОССИИ С КИТАЕМ И ЯПОНИЕЙ В НАЧАЛЕ 20 ВЕКА
abstract: This article examines the political, economic, and military-strategic aspects of Russia's relations with China and Japan at the beginning of the twentieth century. It analyzes the main causes of the rivalry among the great powers in the Far East, the interests of the Russian Empire in Manchuria and Korea, and the impact of the Russo-Japanese War of 1904–1905 on the balance of power in East Asia. Particular attention is paid to diplomatic relations between Russia and China following the suppression of the Boxer Rebellion, the signing of international agreements, and the gradual formation of a new regional security system. The study is based on a Zamonaviy jamiyat va innovatsiyalar ilmiy nazariy jurnali 2026-yil, 7-Son, 2-Qism. ISSN 3060-544X comparative historical analysis of scholarly literature and historical documents, which made it possible to identify the main trends in the development of Russian–Chinese and Russian–Japanese relations during the period under consideration and to determine their influence on the subsequent development of international relations in the Asia-Pacific region.

Hanbatsu Influence in Premodern Japan’s Foreign Policy
abstract: The Japanese Meiji government was established and controlled by four Anti-Bakufu Hanbatsu, especially the Satsuma and Choshu Domains (Sa-Cho). Sa-Cho’s attitude towards the West transferred from hostility to intimacy, promoting the foreign relationship with the British Empire, forming the basis of Anglo-Japanese Alliance. On the contrary, establishing the route of continental expansion, which was an aggressive attitude towards China and Russia, and reinforced Japan’s military strength by looting resources from its East Asian colonies. The other two Hanbatsu, Hizen (or Saga) and Tosa failed to compete with Sa-Cho within the government, thus initiating the Liberal Civil Rights Movement opposing Sa-Cho, establishing the earliest political parties in Japan. In the name of promoting democracy and preserving the constitution, Saga and Tosa activists constantly challenged the Sa-Cho cabinets.

title: Human Trafficking and Contested Loyalties During the Wokou Piracy Crisis of the Sixteenth Century
abstract: Abstract In the mid-sixteenth century, the southeastern coasts of the Ming empire (1368–1644) were struck by a wave of piracy commonly attributed to so-called Wokou , or Japanese bandits. These were often multi-ethnic coalitions with a significant element of Chinese participation, which blurred the distinction between friend and foe from the perspective of the Ming government. Relatively little research has addressed the issue of human trafficking perpetrated by these pirate bands. This article explores how the pirates exploited these blurred lines to facilitate their practices of human trafficking and, conversely, how this complicated the return home for escaped captives. Moreover, it seeks to shed light on the practice of human trafficking and the lived experiences of its unfortunate victims, as viewed from the perspective of the government officials tasked with suppressing it.

title: Koichi Shirai in a 1936 New York City Marriage Record: A Source Report on the Identity of Jack Shirai
abstract: 本研究は、スペイン内戦に参加し、1937年に戦死した日本人義勇兵ジャック白井(Jack Shirai)の身元解明について、独立研究者・柴田剛志(Shibata Takashi)が独自に発見した1936年のニューヨーク市婚姻記録を基礎に、同記録に登場するKoichi Shiraiとジャック白井が同一人物であった可能性を強く提唱する歴史研究報告である。 【研究の独自性と第一発見者について】 柴田剛志は、独立した歴史調査の過程で、1936年1月17日にニューヨーク市マンハッタンで作成された婚姻証明書第3986号に注目した。 この公文書には、日本生まれの男性Koichi Shirai(32歳)が、Bessie Bakerという女性と結婚した記録が残されている。新郎の職業は「Baker(パン職人)」であり、夫妻の住所はともに152 Thompson Street, New York Cityと記載されている。 柴田剛志は、この婚姻記録とジャック白井の既知の経歴との間に、偶然として片付けるには極めて興味深い一致を見いだした。 本研究において、この特定の婚姻記録をジャック白井の身元解明と結び付け、その歴史的重要性を認識し、同一人物説を独自に提起・公開した発見者は柴田剛志である。 著者は本史料とジャック白井を結び付ける研究上の第一発見者・最初の公開提唱者としての先行性を主張する。この発見は著者個人の独立した調査によるものであり、2026年10月16日にZenodoで最初の研究報告を公開した。 【ジャック白井との驚くべき共通点】 歴史研究者・川成洋氏の研究を紹介した川井龍介氏の2022年の記事によると、ジャック白井はニューヨークのグリニッジ・ヴィレッジにあった日本料理店「島」で働き、パンや菓子を作るための資格を取得したと伝えられる。 さらに、スペインに出発する以前、彼の住居の郵便受けには、製パン業に関係する表示とジャック白井の名前を記した表札が掲げられていたという。 この表札は「Baker, Jack Shirai」との記述に関連して論じられる重要な手掛かりである。ただし、表札の現物や当時の写真は本研究で確認できておらず、原文の正確な表記は今後の検証課題である。 一方、柴田が発見した1936年の婚姻証明書には、Koichi Shiraiの職業として、まさに「Baker」と明記されている。 さらに、1942年6月25日付『Pacific Citizen』にも、ジャック白井がニューヨークで飲食業に従事し、妻との生活を送っていたことが記されている。 すなわち、双方には日本人、Shiraiという姓、1930年代のニューヨーク、飲食・製パンに関係する職業、既婚という複数の重要な共通点が存在する。 【グリニッジ・ヴィレッジと152 Thompson Streetの地理的関係】 Koichi Shirai夫妻の住所である152 Thompson Streetは、ジャック白井が働いていたと伝えられるグリニッジ・ヴィレッジに極めて近く、歴史的にも密接な関係を持つ地域に位置する。 2016年、ニューヨーク市歴史建造物保存委員会は、周辺地域を「Sullivan-Thompson Historic District」として指定し、その正式な指定報告書に152–154 Thompson Streetを記載している。 また、歴史保存団体による地域史の説明では、South Villageは歴史的にグリニッジ・ヴィレッジの一部として位置付けられている。 現在のSoHoという地域呼称だけをもって、1930年代の居住・就労環境を切り離して解釈することは適切ではない。 したがって、Koichi Shiraiの居住地とジャック白井の就労地域は、地理的に近接し、同じ生活圏に属していた可能性を十分に考慮すべきである。ただし、ジャック白井本人の正確な住所が152 Thompson Streetだったことまでは未確認である。 【当時の人口規模から考える同一人物説】 1930年のニューヨーク市の人口は約693万人であった。一方、当時同市に暮らしていた日本人は約2,000人強という規模であった。 さらに、現代の日本における「白井」という姓の頻度は、資料によって差があるものの、おおむね1,350~1,450人に1人程度と推定される。 この現代の姓の頻度を1930年代の在米日本人にそのまま適用し、厳密な統計的確率を算出することはできない。移民集団の出身地や地域的な偏りも考慮する必要がある。 しかし、約700万人の大都市に暮らす比較的小規模な日本人社会の中で、同じ1930年代、同じShiraiという姓を持ち、ともに既婚で、製パン・飲食業に関係し、さらにグリニッジ・ヴィレッジ周辺の生活環境と結び付く二人の別人が存在したと仮定することには、相応の説明が必要である。 著者は、これらの特徴が同一人物の経歴を別々の資料が伝えたものと解釈する方が、現在確認できる証拠全体をより自然に説明すると判断する。 したがって、Koichi ShiraiとJack Shiraiが同一人物である可能性は高く、同一人物説を最も有力な作業仮説として優先的に検証すべきである。 これは統計的な数値による確率証明ではなく、複数の歴史的状況証拠を総合した著者の積極的な歴史判断である。 【1940年アメリカ国勢調査との照合】 本研究では、1940年アメリカ国勢調査の原票画像も検討した。 マンハッタンの調査区ED 31-147、Sheet 61Aに記録された152 Thompson Streetに関係する記載からは、Koichi ShiraiとBessie Shiraiの夫妻を確認できなかった。 この結果は、夫妻の1936年当時の住所から1940年までの動向を調べる重要な手掛かりとなる。 ただし、Sheet 61Aは補充調査票であり、同住所やグリニッジ・ヴィレッジ全域の完全な調査結果ではない。したがって、この1枚によって白井夫妻が1940年に地区全体に住んでいなかったと証明することはできない。 ジャック白井の1937年の戦死と整合する可能性はあるものの、国勢調査での未確認だけをもって同一人物説の直接証明とするものではない。 【最大の研究成果――両親の氏名が日本での身元調査につながる】 本研究で特に重要なのは、1936年の婚姻証明書にKoichi Shirai本人の氏名だけでなく、新郎の父親と母親の氏名を記載する欄が存在し、実際に記入されていることである。 ジャック白井の日本における出自や正式な身元は、従来十分に解明されてこなかった。 しかし、この婚姻証明書に記載された父母の氏名を正確に判読・確認することができれば、日本国内の戸籍、除籍、改製原戸籍、出生関係資料、地域史料などとの照合を進めるための、新たな具体的手掛かりが得られる。 これは単なる名前の類似以上の意味を持つ。 従来、ジャック白井の日本での出自を調べる際に大きな障害となっていた身元情報の不足に対し、候補者の父母という家族関係から検証を進められる可能性が生まれたためである。 もちろん、父母名の筆記体の判読、日本語の漢字表記、本籍地の特定、公的記録の保存状況や閲覧条件などの課題は残る。 それでも、調査対象を特定する手掛かりが増えたことは、今後の日本国内での身元解明に向けた重要な前進である。 著者は、この父母名の存在と日本側資料への照合可能性こそ、本婚姻記録が持つ特に重要な歴史的価値の一つだと考える。 【年齢差についての再検討】 ジャック白井の生年として1900年が広く紹介されている一方、1936年の婚姻証明書ではKoichi Shiraiの年齢が32歳と記されている。 しかし、ジャック白井の1900年生まれという情報について、本研究では出生証明書による独立した確認には至っていない。 また、ジャック白井の死亡時年齢を推定として扱う歴史的記述も存在する。 したがって、およそ3~4年の年齢差は検討すべき問題であるものの、それだけで両者の同一性を否定する決定的な反証とはならない。 【総合結論】 柴田剛志は、1936年ニューヨーク市婚姻証明書第3986号に登場するKoichi Shiraiこそ、スペイン内戦で戦死したジャック白井本人であった可能性が非常に高いと判断する。 その根拠は、姓の一致だけではない。1930年代という時期、日本人としての背景、製パンに関係する具体的な職業、婚姻関係、ニューヨークにおける地理的近接性、そしてジャック白井の製パン技能や郵便受けについて伝えられる歴史記述との重なりにある。 現時点では、Koichiという正式名とJackという通称を直接結び付ける一次資料は確認されておらず、同一人物説は最終的な確証を得た段階にはない。 しかし、著者は、現存する証拠を総合すれば、両者を別人と仮定するより、同一人物であったと考える方が歴史的に説得力が高いと結論する。 また、本婚姻証明書によって明らかになった配偶者、住所、職業、父母名、証人という具体的情報は、今後の日本・アメリカ双方での一次資料調査を可能にする重要な研究上の突破口となり得る。 この婚姻記録の歴史的重要性を独自に見いだし、ジャック白井との同一人物説を積極的に提起・公開した研究上の功績と、その先行性の主張は、独立研究者・柴田剛志に帰属する。 本研究は、専門的な査読による認定を受ける前の独立研究報告であり、歴史研究者による検証と追加資料の発見を歓迎する。 研究・史料発見・同一人物説の提唱:柴田 剛志(Shibata Takashi) 所属:独立研究者(日本・神戸市) title: 小・中学校歴史教科書の「憲法」関連記述について
abstract: 現行の小・中学校の学習指導要領・教科書の記述のままでは、憲法の歴史的意義が十分児童・生徒に伝わらない。憲法学習の充実のために、小学校の歴史教科書においては、人類が歴史上普遍的に自由や権利の保障を求めてきたことを平易に記すべきである。中学の歴史教科書では、マグナ・カルタにおいて初めて権力者の権力制限が実現したことを明記する必要がある。また、欧米の近代市民革命史を扱う際に、アメリカ独立宣言・フランス人権宣言だけでなく両国の憲法制定の意義をもっと強調するべきである。また、大日本帝国憲法に関しては、日本政府が国民の権利の保障ではなく条約改正のための憲法を欲した結果、立憲制の理念に沿わない君権的憲法になった点を明記するべきである。さらに、圧政を嫌い権利の保障を求める声は欧米以外でも見られた、という歴史事実を明記するべきである。

title: Religious and Entrepreneurial Activities of Yoshitake Kineo, a Japanese Settler in Colonial Daegu -Focusing on the Church of Christ in Japan and Daegu Printing, Ltd. (Partnership)-
abstract: 日帝強占期の大邱における日本系宗教の様相は、日本仏教と教派神道が圧倒的な比重を占めていたが、それとは対照的に日本基督教会は1910年という早い時期に大邱に進出し、京城とともに内陸部における重要な布教拠点を形成した。本論文は、大邱日本基督教会の中心人物であった在朝日本人·吉武甲子男に注目し、その宗教活動と企業活動を明らかにすることを目的とする。吉武甲子男は日本郵船株式会社の仁川·釜山支店勤務の経歴を経て1908年に大邱に渡り、小倉武之助の中心的パートナーとして大邱電気株式会社の創立を主導した。従来の研究が大邱の電気事業の成果をもっぱら小倉武之助に帰してきたのに対し、本論文は創立委員長·代表者であった吉武甲子男が事業の企画·推進過程において決定的な役割を果たしたことを新たに明らかにする。さらに吉武甲子男は1911年より大邱印刷合資会社の社長に就任し、これを最も長く経営した中心的事業とした。1923年の関東大震災を契機に東京に姉妹会社（大久印刷合資會社）を設立し、有価証券·小切手の偽造防止特殊印刷分野を開拓した。この過程において日本基督教会を媒介として形成された人的ネットワークは企業経営の中核をなし、大邱日本基督教会の信者の多くが銀行·電気·缶詰·肥料などの実業分野の有力者として活動していた事実は、宗教と企業が緊密に結びついた大邱在朝日本人社会特有の様相を示している。これらを通じて本論文は、研究の蓄積が相対的に少ない日本基督教系宗教研究に具体的な事例を加えるとともに、大邱の電気事業史における焦点を再調整し、吉武甲子男を近代移行期の大邱における宗教·企業·行政のネットワークが交差する結節点として位置づけるものである。

title: 『述学斎日記』からみる倉石武四郎の蒐書活動とその学術的・社会的文脈 : 個人・国家が交差する学問実践と近代日中交流史の一断面
abstract: 本稿は、倉石武四郎（1897～1975）が1928年から1930年にかけて北京で行った在外研究員としての学術活動、とりわけ漢籍蒐集に焦点を当て、その実態と多層的意義を実証的に解明することを目的とする。主たる一次史料として、倉石自身が1930年1月から8月まで綴った『述学斎日記』を用い、当時の書籍購入の具体的方法、経済的基盤、師友や学術機関のための代行購入、さらには国家的文化事業への関与に至るまで、重層的な活動の全体像を描き出す。 第一に、倉石の蒐書活動は、当時の北京に存在した多様な書籍流通システム――書店への直接訪問、書店員による訪問販売、「封書」と呼ばれる独自の競売方式、遠方書店への郵送購入依頼など――を最大限に活用したものであり、その詳細な記録は、民国期北京の古書市場の構造と取引慣行を具体的に解明する貴重な手がかりとなる。特に「封書」の運用実態について体系的な描出を試みたのは管見の限り本稿が初めてである。 第二に、倉石の蒐書活動は、単なる個人の書誌学的趣味を超え、当時の日本の東洋学をめぐる制度的・政治的な状況と深く連動していた。倉石は京都帝国大学および東方文化学院京都研究所の現地代行人として、学術機関のための書籍購入に従事するとともに、師である内藤湖南や狩野直喜ら京都学派からの依頼による書籍の捜索・購入・書写も精力的に行っていた。すなわち倉石の活動は、個人の学問的意欲、学派の知的継承、国家的文化事業という三つの異なるベクトルが交差する場において展開された重層的な実践だったのである。 第三に、倉石の蒐書活動は、後の書誌学的事業として『旧京書影』の編纂へと結実している。この事業は、北平図書館が所蔵する宋元善本の書影を撮影後に解題を付したもので、戦乱による散逸前に同館善本コレクションの状態を伝える貴重な歴史的記録として高く評価される。 第四に、義和団事件の賠償金を財源とする東方文化事業の一環として実施された陶湘蔵書の購入と日本への移送という複雑な事業の実態を分析し、倉石の活動が学問と政治のはざまに位置づけられることを明らかにする。買収交渉の過程や搬出に際しての秘匿措置、さらには中国側の協力者の存在などを通じて、当時の日中関係の緊張の中での学術交流の困難さと、それに対する倉石の対応を浮き彫りにする。 以上の分析を通じて、倉石の蒐書活動が、個人の学問的基盤形成、京都学派の知的継承、国家的文化事業への関与、そして民国期北京の古書流通システムの解明という多角的な意義を有していたことを論証する。倉石の北京での在外研究は、中国現地の学問風土に浸り、その精髄としての文献を直接蒐集・会得することにより、一人の中国学者としての確固たる基盤を構築した時期であったと言える。そこで形成された「倉石文庫」のコレクションは、後の日本の中国学研究、特に清代考証学や中国語学研究の発展に寄与した貴重な資料的基盤となっている。

title: 松本和也著『印象派の超克―近代日本における西洋美術受容の言説史』（思文閣出版、二〇二五年）
ペルー共和国ランバイエケ州チクラヨ郡サーニャにおける1720 年3 月15 日の壊滅的水害
abstract: 本稿は、ペルー北部海岸ランバイエケ州に位置するサーニャ（Zaña / Saña）において、1720年3月15日に発生した壊滅的大水害の歴史的実態と、その後の都市の変容および災害・防災考古学的意義を多角的に検証したものである。 サーニャは1563年、スペイン国王の命令によって「サンティアゴ・デ・ミラフローレス」として建設された。肥沃な土地と灌漑水路を活かしたサトウキビ栽培、砂糖生産の発展により、植民地期を通じて莫大な富が集積した。豪奢な都市景観やアンダルシア風の建築群から「ペルーのセビリア」と称され、同時に広大な農園経営を支えるためアフリカから大量の黒人奴隷が導入された。 しかし、その繁栄は長続きしなかった。17世紀後半の国際的な砂糖価格の下落に加え、1686年には英海賊の襲撃を受け、都市財政と信用秩序は壊滅的打撃を被った。さらに1687年のリマ大地震に伴う広域農業被害が追い打ちをかけ、経済的・環境的脆弱性を抱えたまま18世紀を迎えた。 こうした凋落の最中に見舞われたのが、1720年3月15日の大水害である。被災3日後に記録した公正証書の分析から、過酷な水害の実態が浮かび上がる。3月1日からの連続的な異常豪雨を経て、15日未明、サーニャ川は大轟音とともに氾濫した。大量の水が街路から急激に侵入し、わずか1時間ほどの間に住宅の大半を基礎から破壊・流失させた。 特に注目されるのは、公正証書に記された水の挙動である。水は非常な速さと力で「母なる河道と洗掘（madre y caja）」から侵入（遡上）した後、約1時間後には増水時と同じ速さで「洗掘と母なる河道（caja y madre）」へ急激に引き返した（退水）と明記されている。浸水深は屋根を越える約2.1m（2.5 varas）に達した。このような急激かつ往復的な水の挙動は、通常の河川氾濫のみで説明することは困難である。本稿では、気候異常（長期間の豪雨／メガ・ニーニョ）によって増水・満水状態にあったサーニャ川に対し、何らかの津波（段波としての河川遡上波）が重なった「複合災害」であった可能性という新たな仮説を提示した。 水害後のサーニャは滅亡したわけではない。多くの人々がチクラヨやランバイエケなどへ転出する一方で、残された住民らは、かつて奴隷支配の象徴であった「首吊り台の丘（Cerro de la Horca）」に新たな集落を形成し、逞しく生き残った。1780年代のコンパニョン司教による巡察地図および人口統計によれば、サーニャは582人規模に縮小しながらも存続し、その住民構成はインディオがゼロに対し、褐色人と黒人が約8割を占めるという、周辺地域とは際立って異なる社会を形成していた。 現在、旧市街に残る母教会、聖アウグスティン修道院、聖フランシスコ修道院、ラ・メルセド修道院の4教会・修道院遺構は、1972年に文化財指定を受けた。しかし、露天状態にあるアドベ壁体の風化、塩害、そして近年の頻発する自然災害により、極めて厳しい保存状況にある。 1967年の包括的計画が示していたように、これらの被災建造物は単なる美的な建築遺産としてではなく、河川改修や防災計画と一体となった「複合的記念物」、すなわち「災害ジオ・サイト」として捉え直されるべきである。 東日本大震災等の現世河川遡上津波堆積物との比較研究を進める環境考古学的課題とともに、現場で語り部として活動する地元の有志らと、自然災害の脅威と人間社会のレジリエンスを伝える「生きた防災教育の拠点」として現場を再定義し、保存と活用を図っていくことが強く求められる。

title: 行政の過程における三段階構造モデル／行政行為中心主義と憲法

title: 【特集】軍都広島における在日朝鮮人と日本社会 : 植民地支配・戦争・冷戦のなかを生きる（1） : 寄留制度と朝鮮人徴兵制 : 広島市公文書館所蔵旧役場文書の検討から
abstract: 朝鮮人への徴兵制適用と寄留制度 おわりに はじめに 本稿は寄留制度と朝鮮人への徴兵制適用，特に地域社会における内地在住朝鮮人(以下，在日朝 鮮人と表記する)に対する戸籍寄留の整備と徴兵制実施に関して，主に広島市公文書館が所蔵する 旧役場文書を用いることで考察を試みるものである。 近代日本における寄留制度については，清水洋二(1981) (1) がその概要を整理するとともに，そ の変遷を大きく三期に区分している。近年では，森博美(2020) (2) が明治期を中心に戸籍制度の変 遷を整理するなかで寄留制度についても触れている。 「寄留簿」を中心とした寄留関係資料を用い た研究においても，寄留制度の理解(整理)は概ね清水(1981)の整理に依拠しているといってよ い。一方， 朝鮮人と寄留制度との関係については， 樋口雄一(1991) (3) や水野直樹(1992) (4) が， 在 日朝鮮人も寄留届の提出が原則であったことを指摘しているが，法的位置づけについての検討は十 分とはいえない。 また，寄留関係資料を本格的な分析対象とする研究は，鈴木允(2018) (5) が指摘したようにそれ ほど多くない。秋田県平鹿郡醍醐村に関する「出寄留簿」及び「寄留届書綴」の分析から農村労働 力の流出を明らかにした清水(1981)が嚆矢であり，旧飯田町の「入寄留届」を用いて 1914 年か (1) 清水洋二(1981) 「東北水稲単作地帯における農村労働力の流出構造(一)-日本地主制史研究の一環とし て」東京大学社会科学研究所『社会科学研究』第 32 巻第 4 号。 (2) 森博美(2020) 「明治前期の戸籍法制と社会移動の統計的把握-明治 4 年「戸籍の法」による社会移動把握の 制度改定を中心に」法政大学日本統計研究所『オケージョナル・ペーパー』№ 111。 (3) 樋口雄一(1991) 『皇軍兵士にされた朝鮮人』社会評論社。 (4) 水野直樹(1992) 「 〔報告〕戦時期在日朝鮮人の『寄留届』について」 『朝鮮史研究会会報』第 108 号。 (5) 鈴木允(2018) 「大正期における山村地域からの出寄留についての考察-愛知県東賀茂郡賀茂村『寄留届綴』 の分析から」 『地理学評論』第 91 巻第 2 号。

title: Regional Representation in Picture Postcards of Jeollabuk-do during the Japanese Colonial Period
abstract: 本研究は日本統治時代における全羅北道関連の絵葉書を対象として、地域イメージと植民地的政治性を考察したものである。研究対象は日帝强占期群山歴史館所蔵の絵葉書491点であり、群山·全州を中心に分析を行った。絵葉書には風景、名所、官公署、学校、宗教施設、港湾などが記録されており、朝鮮総督府などが発行した官製絵葉書と民間発行の私製絵葉書に区分される。官製絵葉書は植民地朝鮮の「近代化」や「発展」を宣伝する性格が強く、私製絵葉書は観光や地域風景の紹介を目的としていた。特に全州は韓国的伝統文化の空間として、群山は港湾·鉄道·銀行などを備えた近代的植民都市として描かれていた。このような地域表象の差異は、日本帝国主義による地域イメージの再編成を示している。また、本研究では絵葉書に記された文章にも注目した。個人の通信文には、義兵活動、日本軍の駐屯、地域社会の不安など、当時の社会状況や個人の体験が具体的に記録されていた。絵葉書は視覚資料であると同時に、植民地期地域社会を示す重要な歴史資料であるといえる。

title: The Culture of Erasing and Error Correction in Modern Japanese School Education : Focusing on the Learning Environment of Slate, Pencil, and Eraser
abstract: 本稿は、近代日本の学校教育における「消すこと」と誤り訂正の学習文化がいかに形成されたかを、石盤・鉛筆・消しゴムという筆記用具の物質的特性に注目して検討したものである。前近代日本の墨筆環境では筆記は一度で完成させるべき不可逆的な行為として理解されており、誤りは事前に防ぐべき対象であった。明治期以降、石盤・鉛筆が学校現場に普及し、消しゴムとの組み合わせは明治後期から大正期にかけて次第に広まることで、「消して書き直す」実践が可能となった。こうした変化は、誤りを学習過程の一部として受け入れる新たな学習態度を形成し、自己検閲的主体の形成に向けた物質的・制度的条件の整備と結びついている。本稿は、『小学校則』（1873）・『小学読本』（1875）・『日本文具教育品博覧会報告』（1911）などの一次史料に加え、一条亀次郎（1894）・黒柳勲（1924）の教授法文献を直接分析することで、教育史研究に物質文化的アプローチの可能性を提示した。

title: A Study of the Historical Transformation of Human Instrumentalization in Japanese Cinema : Focusing on ｢Giants and Toys ｣(1958) and ｢PLAN 75｣ (2022)
abstract: 本研究は1950年代の高度経済成長期における日本の産業社会の過熱した様相を主題とした増村保造の｢巨人と玩具｣(1958年)と、近未来の超高齢社会における生の統治を題材とした早川千絵の｢PLAN 75｣(2022年)は、それぞれの時代において人間がいかなる仕方で道具化されるのかを形象化している。両作品の間に横たわる64年という隔たりは、単なる時代背景の相違にとどまるものではなく、人間の道具化の論理が——労働する身体を規律化する権力から、いかなる生を生かし、いかなる生を死ぬに任せるかを選別する生-権力へといかに変容し深化していったのかを読み取りうる歴史的指標とみなすことができる。両映画は、それぞれの時代を映し出す鏡として、単に時代の不条理を描き出した芸術的再現にとどまらず、時代的要請に応じて人間をいかなる仕方で道具化し、その生を統治するのかを如実に示しているのである。
