title: 近代における立山信仰世界の継続と変容 －芦峅寺善道坊の愛知県三河地方を対象とする 檀那帳や戒名簿の分析から－
abstract: 明治維新以後、加賀藩芦峅寺衆徒の勧進布教活動は大きな転換期を迎えた。近世における芦峅寺衆徒は、全国各地に形成した独自の信仰圏の檀那場を巡回し、廻檀、配札、仏前廻向、立山曼荼羅の絵解き、各種の布施、立山参詣の斡旋など、多面的な宗教実践によって、広域的な信仰圏を維持していた。 しかし明治期以降、神仏分離、廃藩置県、近代的交通網の発達、人口移動、戸籍・教育・衛生制度の整備などにより、近世的な檀那場秩序は急速に変容を余儀なくされる。特に愛知県三河地方では、鉄道開通による移動革命、商品農業化、都市への人口流入、家制度の再編などが急進し、民衆の宗教意識や共同体構造が激変した。 本稿では、芦峅寺の宿坊・善道坊に遺された江戸後期から大正期にかけての檀那帳、祠堂回向簿、戒名簿、及び近年筆者が入手した新出の護符類史料を多角的に分析する。これにより、近代の社会変動の中で、立山衆徒の勧進布教活動が従来の「配札・物品頒布」中心のあり方から、「祖先供養・夭折児供養」を軸とする死者供養へと比重を移し、活動の基礎台帳を「檀那帳」から「戒名簿」へと移行させることで檀那場を再編・継続させていった動態的適応過程を明らかにする。

title: ベルギー・ポピュリズムの新展開? : 転換点としての2024年総選挙と統一地方選挙
abstract: [要旨] 本論文では、2024年6月のベルギー総選挙と同年10月の統一地方選挙で台頭した新フランデレン同盟 (N-VA)、フラームス・ベラング(VB)、労働者党という3つのポピュリズム勢力を中心に、ベルギーのポピュリズム勢力の台頭と課題について論じる。N-VAは総選挙で第一党を維持したものの、浮動票の確保に苦戦した。さらに、同党は連立交渉で事実上連立の枠組みが一通りしかないことを利用し、中道左派政党の前進に合意を迫ったが、反発されて交渉が長期化した。こうしたN-VAの強引な態度は自治体レベルでも見られ、地方政党がVBとの連立を選択する原因となった。VBとの協力を一切拒否する「防疫線」の崩壊とも言える事例だが、より制約の多い国政レベルで実現するかは不透明である。労働者党も勢力を拡大しているが、極端な党員への制約で離党者が相次いでおり、既成政党への批判票を十分に集められていなかった。このようにベルギーのポピュリズム勢力はそれぞれ課題を抱えているが、それでも他の先進国同様、抗議する主体から統治する主体への転換が確認できる。

title: ダイジェスト版・我が国における国際課税の法と政策─研究会報告の概要
abstract: 本稿は、本学法律科学研究所2025年度第４回研究会(2025年12月17日) (於法律科学研究所会 議室)で筆者が報告した、我が国の主に第二次世界大戦前の所得課税における外国人課税や英独 立法、国際連盟によるモデル租税条約の策定過程に関する研究報告(ダイジェスト版)の概要で ある。研究会では次の構成で論点を整理し概論した。 はじめに～問題の所在 １．非居住者外国法人課税の系譜 ２．プロイセン所得税 ３．英国法 ４．国際連盟モデル租税条約の策定 まとめ 以下では、この構成に従い、概要を述べる。 はじめに-問題の所在 2012年頃からOECD/IFは、BEPS(Base Erosion and Profit Shifting、課税ベース侵食と利益 移転)と呼称される「行き過ぎた課税逃れ」に対応するための、国際課税制度の大規模な見直し 作業を行っている。2025年乃至26年に至っても、BEPS2.0の枠組み調整や国内法化などが続いている。それは100年来の大改革といわれ、100年という言葉が鍵となっている。この100年来とい う表現は、当然のように過去を振り返らせ、1920年に成立した国際連盟におけるモデル租税条約 の策定過程を意識させる 1 。国際連盟は、今日に続く、恒久的施設(permanent establishment) や所得区分と課税権配分を結合させ、 「恒久的施設なければ(事業所得)課税なし」という考え 方を定着させたが、今日になってそのような考え方が揺らいでいる。 一方、日本は明治維新以降、雑税整理、地租改正を経て明治20年に近代的な所得課税を国レベ ルで行うようになった(所得税法の制定) 。しかし、我が国の先行研究では、どういうわけか、 この明治20年所得税法前後から昭和40年全文改正頃までの主に第二次世界大戦前の所得課税にお ける外国人課税の状況が整理されておらず

title: 【比較地政法学シリーズ】 ルースキー・ミールの法理学 ——プーチンの挑戦と周辺国の応戦様式—— 格義・格義排除の反復構造と宿業転換の条件
abstract: 本論文は、1990年代の研究過程で見出された一つの奇妙な事実——航空機不法奪取ヘーグ条約(1970年)の国内実施において、ソ連が東欧諸国に統一的な変型方式を強制していた事実——から出発する。この30年前の問いは、2021年7月のプーチン大統領論文「ロシア人とウクライナ人の歴史的統一について」が「われわれは一つの民族である」と主張する場面において、同一の縁起的連関の現代的展開として再浮上する。本論文はこの二つの事象を貫く論理構造を、比較地政法学(Comparative Geopolitical Jurisprudence)という新たな分析枠組みによって解剖する。 中心概念は「格義」(Geyi)と「格義排除」(Geyi-Exclusion)である。格義とは、受容側が外部の規範体系(国際法・民主主義・法の支配)を自らの既存の概念装置によって消化・吸収し、内的本質を保持しながら外来の知を内面化する過程を指す。格義排除とは、いったん受容・定着した外部規範体系を、政治情勢の変化と連動して周期的かつ持続的に空洞化・排出する操作である。本論文は、ロシア法の歴史全体を「ブルジョワ革命なき格義の試み」という構造的条件から不可避的に生じる、格義と格義排除の6サイクルの反復として把握する。ビザンツとの接触による存在論的主権の原型形成(第1サイクル)から、ピョートル大帝の強制的格義(第2サイクル)、1864年改革と銀の時代の唯一の深い格義(第3サイクル)、ソビエト国際法学の体系的格義排除(第4サイクル)、ポストソビエト期の格義再試行とその流産(第5サイクル)、そして現代プーチン期の完成された格義排除(第6サイクル)へと至る歴史的実証が、第1章および第2章の法社会学的解剖を通じて展開される。 第3章では、この圧力構造のもとで周辺国が採る六つの異なる応戦様式——ベラルーシ(服属と調整権の全面放棄)、ウクライナ(対抗格義と物理的破壊)、カザフスタン(全方位ヘッジングと古典的国際法のバリケード)、モルドバ(沿ドニエストルの楔による構造的阻害)、アルメニア(集団安全保障条約機構幻想の崩壊と戦略的孤立)、ハンガリー(EU内部からの便乗とその終焉)——を、比較地政法学的に類型化する。西サハラ勧告的意見(1975年)の原則を中央アジア植民地化史に適用する試みは、ソビエト社会主義自体の「致命的パラドックス」を告発するものである。 第4章は量子法理学(Quantum Jurisprudence)と仏教哲学の三諦(空諦・仮諦・中諦)を認識論的枠組みとして、四基準(調整権の外部収奪度・強行規範違反の明白性・義務生成枠組みの能動的破壊・記録の累積密度)によるカルマ評価を行い、ロシア連邦を「構造の破壊者」として、また各主体の帰責を差異化して確定する。第5章は、この診断から独立に導出される宿業転換の条件を、四本柱(担い手と本体の連結・格義排除の完成阻止・カルマ記録の永続的維持・一念特異点への因果条件の蓄積)からなる建築設計として提示する。2026年4月のハンガリー総選挙における格義排除の民主的停止は、ロシアにおける宿業転換の可能性を実証する先例として位置づけられる。 結語は、断罪でも友好でもない立場のもとに、格義排除の因果的必然性を理解することと、その帰結を記録し続ける使命との共存を、本論文全体を貫く命題として確定する。「決着の時期は予測不可能だが、決着は訪れる」——この中道的命題が、比較地政法学の実践的結論である。 キーワード:比較地政法学、格義、格義排除、等位理論、宿業転換、ルースキー・ミール、存在論的主権、量子法理学、三諦 目次 序論 航空機不法奪取ヘーグ条約から「歴史的統一」論文へ——30年後の回帰 第1章 ロシア法の格義・格義排除の反復構造——歴史的解剖 第2章 プーチン主権論の法社会学的解剖——現代ロシアの格義排除・ドクサ・カルマ 第3章 周辺国の応戦様式——6事例の比較地政法学的解剖 第4章 カルマ判定——ルースキー・ミール圏における違法性の記録と責任の帰属 第5章 宿業転換の条件——比較地政法学的設計論 結語 航空機不法奪取ヘーグ条約から「歴史的統一」論文へ——30年後の回帰

title: 廃帝考――淡路廃帝の命名と『続日本紀』における廃立の正統性
abstract: 天平宝字八年(七六四)、孝謙太上天皇は淳仁天皇を廃し、淡路公に降した。『続日本紀』は大炊王の即位から在位を一代の歴史として編成し、その紀首に「廢帝」と記す。本稿は、中国正史で「廢帝」の名のもとに記された廃立事件の事績を分析し、この呼称が歴史叙述において担う分類上の意味を検討する。 『晋書』の司馬奕は、桓温が太后の権威と伊尹・霍光の先例を用いて廃位し、公へ降した君主であり、同書は桓温の誣告を記して「彼異阿衡、我非昌邑」と評した。『陳書』の陳伯宗も太后令によって王に降され、廃立者の陳頊は自ら即位した。同書所載の廃位令は昌邑・太和の先例を引き、魏徴評は陳頊を「無伊尹之志」と評する。両正史において、廢帝の記録には廃された君主の処遇と廃立者の適格性の判断とが結びついている。 日本側でも、天平宝字二年の詔は仲麻呂を伊尹・阿衡になぞらえるが、仲麻呂は後の廃立において淳仁を支持する側であり、淳仁を廃する側ではなかった。さらに孝謙は淳仁を復位させず、自ら重祚した。 以上の事績の対応を踏まえ、本稿は、「廢帝」という命名の背景に中国正史の廃立先例への比定があった可能性を論じる。さらに、光仁・桓武朝が称徳の権威を継承して同一王統を記したという編纂条件のもとで、呼称・典故・事績の照応が廃立者の適格性を問う読解を開くことを示す。特定文献の直接借用や編纂者の批判意図の確定とは区別する。

title: 法皇考――宇多が拒んだ「皇」は、なぜ「法皇」として返されたのか――
abstract: 昌泰二年(899)、仁和寺で出家した宇多は「已云出家、何得称皇」と述べ、太上皇尊号の停止を求めた。ところが、遅くとも延喜六年(906)の同時代行政文書には、宇多を指す「太上法皇」が現れる。皇称を拒んだ人物に、なぜ再び「皇」を含む呼称が付されたのか。本稿は、この矛盾を後世の「法皇=出家した上皇」という完成した定義から逆算せず、899年の文書往復、宇多の自己規律、仏教漢語「法王」の多義性、中国・日本の宗教的帝王語、道鏡の「法王」「法皇」、および菅原文人圏の言語環境から再構成する。本稿の中心的仮説は、「法皇」という同じ二字が宇多側と朝廷側で逆方向から読まれ得た、というものである。宇多にとっては、僧団内の位階を上げる皇号ではなく、法との関係において人物を外部から称する呼称として理解し得た。他方、朝廷にとっては、太上皇尊号を停止してもなお、元天皇・帝父に「皇」の字を残すことができた。この両義性を可能にした語彙的前史として、仏を「法王」とする仏典、中国語圏の宗教的帝王語、最澄の「法皇牟尼」、島田忠臣の「詩帝」を検討する。さらに、平安前期に皇位を窺った僧として否定的に記憶された道鏡が、『日本霊異記』では「法皇」と記される事実を重視する。宇多がこの意味で「法皇」を説明され、正式に受容した場面を示す直接史料は確認できない。本稿が復元するのは命名者の意図や記録されなかった会話ではなく、899年の尊号拒否と906年以後の「法皇」称の流通とを同時に成立させ得た意味構造である。

abstract: 本研究は、戦時体制期における日本キリスト教界の戦争協力言説が朝 鮮キリスト教界に受容·再生産される過程を、日本組合教会の公認機関誌 『基督教世界』と朝鮮YMCA機関誌『靑年』の分析を通じて究明したものであ る。アメリカ会衆派教会の派遣により始まった日本組合教会は、日露戦争 以降アメリカ宣教部との関係を断絶し国家主義的性格を強化したのち、韓 国併合を契機として「キリスト教内鮮一体」を掲げて朝鮮伝道に乗り出し た。1936年から1940年にかけて『基督教世界』に掲載された戦争協力言説は、 天皇神格化とキリスト教の従属化、「聖戦」の正当化と「伝道報国」言説、皇紀 2,600年を契機とする戦争協力論理の極大化という三つの類型として展開 された。この言説は、日本組合教会と人的ネットワークを共有していた『靑 年』を通じて植民地朝鮮に移植·再生産された。移植の経路は、日本組合教 会関係者による直接寄稿と、洪秉璇をはじめとする朝鮮人筆者による再生 産という二つの方式として現れた。後者は日本の論理を朝鮮の文脈に合わ せて変容·内面化したという点において、植民地的主体による能動的再生 産の様相を示している。さらに朝鮮YMCAは、学生動員、戦時組織の構成、日 本YMCAとの制度的統合に至るまで、戦争協力を具体的な実践へと移していった。以上の分析は、戦時体制期における朝鮮キリスト教界の戦争協力 が日帝の強圧による受動的反応ではなく、具体的な人的ネットワークと媒 体を通じて作動した言説の形成·移植·再生産の結果であったことを示し ている

title: 再帰的帝国主義と連続的植民地化の遭遇 : 1874年台湾遠征,琉球王国の終焉,そして日本帝国の戦略的起源
abstract: This paper challenges the conventional historiography of Japanese imperialism, which marks its genesis in 1895, the year Meiji Japan acquired Taiwan as its first overseas colony, and characterizes it as merely derivative of Western models.We argue that the start of Japan's imperial project can be at least traced back to the 1874 Taiwan Expedition, and the former's characteristics can be adequately understood through the theoretical frameworks of recursive imperialism and contiguous colonization.Recursive imperialism is defined as the process by which an aspiring power masters, adapts, and redeploys the normative tools of the dominant international order to pursue its own ambitions.Contiguous colonization refers to the administrative absorption of an adjacent polity, a modality distinct from the welltheorized Western colonial models.Using a structured, focused comparison of the 1874 Taiwan Expedition and the 18721879 annexation of the Ryukyu Kingdom, this paper employs processtracing to demonstrate the intimate link between the two events.The analysis reveals that the external, performative act of recursive imperialism in Taiwan provided the indispensable international legal precedent for completing the internal, administrative process of contiguous colonization in Ryukyu.This research offers a dual contribution: it provides a more nuanced, actorcentric account of Meiji statecraft for diplomatic history and helps rectify postcolonial theory's "Eurocentric blind spot" by providing a framework for analyzing a nonWestern empire such as Japan.

title: Ichinosuke Takagi Appearing in Modern Newspapers of Colonial Korea -Focusing on the Social Functions Carried Out by a Professor at Keijō Imperial University-
abstract: 본고는 종래 연구대상으로 검토되지 않았던, 식민지조선의 근대 신문 기사에 주목하여 당시 경성제대 국문학(일본문학) 교수인 다카기 이치노스케(高木市之助)의 사회적 활동과 그 역할을 체계적으로 고찰한 연구이다.먼저 《대한민국 신문 아카이브》, 《동아디지털 아카이브》, 《아카이브 조선》의 검색 시스템을 사용하여 검색한 결과, 총141여건의 방대한 용례가 발견되었다. 이 용례들을 그 내용에 따라 [A] 인사 (28件), [B]기고문, 강연내용, 출판 (13件), [C] 사회활동 (90件), [D] 그 외(10件)로 분류하여 고찰해 보았다.이와 같이 각 분류에 따른 활동의 성격과 변화양상을 분석한 결과, 다카기 이치노스케의 기사는 기고문이나 출판 등 그의 글에 관한 내용이 비교적 적고 행사, 위원회, 좌담회, 방송 등 사회활동에 관한 기사가 그 대부분을 차지하고 있었다. 특히, 1927年총독부 학무과 시학위원이 된 이후부터는 총독부 관계 행사나 위원회의 참가가 두드러지며, 1932년부터는 교육회가 주관하는 강습회나 와카 대회, 소학 창가의 심사위원으로도 참여하고 있다. 그러한 사회 참가와 더불어 그의 글과 강연의 내용도 1937년 전시 체제 이후부터는 황국신민화를 선도하는 내용으로 변질되어 갔다.즉 이러한 다카기 이치노스케의 활동은 일 개인의 궤적을 나타내는 것이 아니라, 당시 일본 식민지 체제 시스템의 운용을 보여주는 것으로, 전시 체제 일본의 식민지 지배가 조선 사회에 구축되어 가는 양상을 보여주는 일례라 할 수 있다.

venue.name: Korean Journal of Japanese Language and Literature

title: A Comparative Study of Jinjō Shōgaku Rikasho and Science Textbook for Common Schools: Editorial Principles and the Selective Inheritance of Modern Scientific Knowledge
abstract: 본 연구는 일본 문부성 편찬 『尋常小學理科書』와 조선총독부 편찬 『普通學校理科書』를 비교하여, 조선총독부가 일본 이과교과서를 어떠한 원리에 따라 수용·편찬하였는지를 규명하는 데 목적을 두었다. 이를 위해 『尋常小學理科書』 제4·5·6학년 아동용과 『普通學校理科書』 권1·권2·권3을 비교 대상으로 설정하고, 편찬 체계와 범례를 검토한 후 단원 구성, 본문, 삽화를 중심으로 대응 관계와 편찬 양상을 실증적으로 분석하였다. 분석 결과, 『普通學校理科書』는 일본 『尋常小學理科書』를 편찬의 기본 원형으로 삼아 학년 체계와 단원 구성, 본문의 서술 구조, 삽화의 교육적 기능을 전반적으로 계승하고 있었다. 반면 단원 배열과 표기, 일부 생활위생 관련 내용과 학습 소재가 선택적으로 수정되었으며, 제염과정 등 기존 학습 내용에 대해서는 시각자료가 보강된 것으로 나타났다. 이러한 결과는 『普通學校理科書』가 일본 교과서를 단순히 번역하거나 복제한 것이 아니라, 근대 과학지식의 기본 구조를 계승하면서 일부 학습 소재와 내용, 표기 및 시각자료를 선택적으로 조정·재구성하는 편찬 원리에 따라 편찬되었음을 보여준다. 또한 본 연구는 단원 구성, 본문, 삽화를 유기적으로 연결하여 분석함으로써 식민지기 교과서 편찬의 실제 과정을 실증적으로 규명하고, 근대 과학 리터러시의 형성과 전파 과정을 이해하기 위한 새로운 분석 관점을 제시하였다는 점에서 의의를 갖는다.

venue.name: The Korean Journal of Japanese Education

title: The Formation and Development of Korean Buddhist Magazines during the Japanese Colonial Period: The Magazine Activities of Japan-Educated Korean Buddhists
abstract: 본고는 일제강점기 한국 불교 잡지의 변화와 발전을 근대적 매체 환경의 전환 속에서 검토하고, 그 과정에서 일본 유학생들이 수행한 역할과 기여를 분석한다. 근대 인쇄문화와 출판 기술의 확산은 불교 담론의 생산과 유통 방식을 변화시켰으며, 잡지는 불교의 사상과 실천을 새롭게 조직하는 매체로 기능하였다. 이에 본고는 일제강점기 한국 불교 잡지의 전개를 1910년대와 1920년대 이후로 구분하여 살펴본다. 1910년대 불교 잡지는 교단 기관지 계열을 중심으로 형성되었으며, 행정적 통지와 내부 소통의 기능에 상당 부분한정되어 있었다. 그러나 『유심(唯心)』의 등장은 불교 잡지가 교단 내부의 매체를 넘어 근대적 교양 잡지로 확장될 가능성을 보여 주었다. 또한 이 시기 일본 유학생들은 주로 기고자의 위치에서 근대 불교 담론의 형성에 참여하였다. 1920년대 이후에는 불교 잡지의 발행 주체와 내용이 더욱 다변화되었고, 『취산보림(鷲山寶林)』과 『불교(佛敎)』는 이러한 변화를 대표하는 사례로 나타났다. 『취산보림』은 사찰 중심의 매체 실험을 통해 불교 잡지의 분화를 예고하였으며, 『불교』는 장기간의 정기적 발행과 전문적 편집 체계를 바탕으로 근대 불교 언론의 제도화와 전문화를 구현하였다. 본고는 일본 유학생들이 일본에서 접한 불교의 근대성을 한국 불교계의 문제의식 속에서 선택적으로 수용하고 재구성하였으며, 이를 잡지라는 매체를 통해 구체화하였다는 점을 밝힌다. 이를 통해 일제강점기 한국 불교 잡지는 식민지 내부의 종교매체에 그치지 않고, 한국과 일본을 오가는 지식·인적 네트워크 속에서 형성된 초국가적 근대 불교 담론의 장으로 이해될 수 있다.

venue.name: Journal of Eastern-Asia Buddhism and Culture

title: A Study on the Representation of Japan and Subjectivity in Modern Korean and Chinese City Fiction - A Comparative Study of Park Tae-won’s “A Day of Mr. Gubo a Novelist” (1934) and Shi Zhecun’s “One Rainy Evening” (1933) -
abstract: 본 연구는 박태원의 ｢소설가 구보씨의 일일｣(1934)과 스져춘의 ｢장맛비 내리는 저녁｣(1933)을 비교 분석함으로써, 1930년대 (반)식민지 도시소설에서 일본 표상이 수행하는 서사적 기능과 그것이 주체적 현실 인식으로 전환되는 과정을 고찰하는 데 목적이 있다. 두 소설은 각각 경성과 상하이라는 근대 도시 공간을 배경으로 도시와 도시인의 삶을 그려낸다. 근대적 공간으로서의 도시는 두 주인공에게 정신적 결핍을 해소하리라는 기대를 품게 하지만, 불신이 내재한 도시 문화 속에서 그 기대는 실망과 환멸로 전환된다. 그러나 이 환멸은 단순한 좌절로 귀결되지 않는다. 두 주인공은 일본이라는 또 다른 표상 공간을 경유하며, 그 경유는 현실로부터의 이탈에 머무르지 않고 자국의 현실을 보다 구체적으로 재인식하게 하는 촉매로 기능한다. 본고는 이 과정을 분석함으로써, 일본 표상이 서구와 일본에 대한 일방적 추종이 아닌 주체적 현실 인식을 추동하는 서사적 장치임을 논증한다. 나아가 두 텍스트 사이의 상이성보다는 상동성에 주목하여, 한중 모더니즘을 서구로부터의 일방적 수용으로 환원하는 시각을 넘어서고, 1930년대 동아시아 근대문학이 공유하는 주체적 현실 인식의 양상을 규명하고자 한다.

title: Customary Practices Concerning Forfeiture Clauses in Pledges and Forfeiture-Type Mortgages
abstract: 본 연구는 한국 전통사회와 근대 전환기에 존재하였던 유질(流質) 및 유저당 (流抵當)에 관한 관습과 법리를 고찰함으로써, 현행 민법상 유질계약 금지규정 의 역사적 형성 과정을 규명하는 것을 목적으로 한다. 이를 위하여 조선시대 법전과 고문서, 대한제국기 민사판결, 󰡔慣習調査報告書󰡕 및 󰡔民事慣習回答彙 集󰡕, 조선고등법원 판결 등을 종합적으로 분석하였다. 조선시대의 전당(典當)은 오늘날의 질권과 저당권을 포괄하는 담보제도였으며, 그 가운데 이전(移典)은 유질 또는 유저당에 상응하는 관습적 담보제도로 기능 하였음을 확인할 수 있었다. 조선 후기의 전당문기와 각종 문헌 자료에는 채무 자가 변제기 내에 채무를 이행하지 못할 경우 담보물을 채권자가 취득하도록 하는 특약이 나타난다. 특히 ‘영영차지지의(永永次知之意, 永永此持之意)’는 기한 도과 후 채권자가 담보물을 영구히 취득한다는 취지를 표시하는 문언으로서, 전통사회에서 유질적 담보 관행이 실질적으로 존재하였음을 보여준다. 비록 국가의 법정책은 채무자 보호를 위하여 이러한 관행을 억제하려는 방향 으로 전개되었으나, 실제 거래관계에서는 유질적 전당의 효력이 상당 부분 인 정되었다. 관습조사 자료에서 확인되는 이전(移典)은 단순한 전질(轉質)에 한정되지 않고, 전질형 이전, 유질형 이전, 중복전당형 이전 등 다양한 유형으로 존재하였다. 특히 유질형 이전은 ‘변제기 도래 이후’, ‘전당권설정자의 동의 또는 승낙’을 전 제로 담보물의 소유권을 채권자에게 귀속시키는 방식으로 작동하였다. 대한제 국기 한성재판소와 평리원 판결 역시 이러한 이전 관행의 효력을 인정하였으 며, 이는 전통적 담보 관습이 근대적 재판제도 안에서도 일정한 법적 의미를 부여받았음을 보여준다. 1906년 ｢土地家屋典當執行規則｣에서는 토지·가옥 전당에 관한 유질계약을 명문으로 허용하였다. 이는 조선의 전통적 담보 관습을 제도적으로 승인한 입 법으로 평가할 수 있다. 경성공소원, 대심원 및 초기 조선고등법원 판결도 유 질계약의 효력을 인정하였다. 그러나 1912년 ｢朝鮮民事令｣의 시행으로 일본 민법상 유질계약 금지규정이 조선에 의용되면서, 변제기 전 유질계약은 더 이 상 허용되지 않게 되었다. 이후 조선고등법원은 유질계약과는 구별되는 유저 당계약의 효력을 인정하면서, 그 요건과 효과에 관한 독자적인 판례법리를 전 개하였다. 결국 한국 전통사회에서 유질과 유저당은 원칙적으로 금지된 제도가 아니라 관습적으로 승인된 담보 방식이었다. 1906년의 유질 허용 입법은 이러한 관습 을 반영한 결과였으나, 1912년 이후에는 일본 민법의 영향 아래 유질은 금지되 고 유저당만이 제한적으로 인정되는 방향으로 법질서가 재편되었다. 따라서 한국 담보 법제의 형성 과정은 전통적 담보 관습과 근대 계수법이 충돌하고 조정되는 과정이었다고 평가할 수 있다.

venue.name: Korean Journal of Construction Legal Affairs

title: The Activities of Modern Multinational Troupes and the Hybridity of Performance Culture
abstract: 근대 동아시아 공연문화는 국가 단위로 깔끔하게 구분되지 않았다. 연희자들은 조선인․중국인․일본인․영국인이 뒤섞인 합동 흥행의 형태로 무대에 섰다. 특히 공연내용도 단순히 ‘어느 나라의 전통’으로 환원되지 않고, 줄타기․공중회전․마술․곡예․환술이 결합된 혼종적 레퍼토리로 구성되었다. 연희자 이봉운은 조선의 줄타기광대로, 일본 자료에서는 ‘조선 기술사’ 또는 ‘공중회전술’의 주역으로 소개되며, 줄타기와 공중회전으로 관객을 끌었다. 김원기는 조선인 난장이 곡예사로, 일본에서는 일촌법사로 불리며 방울받기․줄타기․환술 계열의 기예를 선보였다. 강진부는 김원기와 짝을 이룬 또 다른 난장이 연희자로, 이촌방이라 불리며 함께 호흡을 맞춘 파트너로 추정된다. 한봉산 일행은 중국인 단장 한풍산과 조선인 김원기가 함께한 공연단으로, 기술․곡예․마술을 내세워 일본 각지에서 흥행했다. 1920년대가 되면 대형 공연단을 꾸려 조선에 들어왔는데 대마술과 기예를 중심으로 60여 명 규모의 흥행을 벌였고, 여성 연기자들까지 동원한 대규모 쇼 형태였다. 근대 동아시아 공연문화에서는 조선인 연희자를 주변화한 것이 아니라, 오히려 그들의 기예를 통해 다국적 흥행의 완성도를 높인 사례로 해석된다. 본고에서 살펴본 공연문화의 혼종은 단순한 혼합이 아니라, 제국의 이동성․식민지적 시선․전통연희의 재구성이 한 무대에 겹쳐진 근대 공연문화의 특징으로 이해할 수 있다.

title: The Expansionism of Victims and the ‘Empire’ Never Experienced : The Trajectory of Korean Alternative History Fiction and the Clash of East Asian Desires
abstract: 본 연구는 대중의 역사 인식이 투영된 공공역사(Public History) 텍스트로서한국 대체역사물의 진화 궤적을 추적하고, 동아시아 3국(한·중·일)의 대중문화기저에 내재한 제국주의적 팽창 욕망의 충돌 양상을 비판적으로 고찰한다. 서구의 대체역사물이 전체주의의 폭력성을 경고하고 자국 체제의 모순을 들추는 ‘디스토피아적 대항 기억’으로 기능해 온 반면, 한국의 텍스트는 현실의 지정학적패배를 가상 공간의 압도적 무력과 관료 시스템으로 보상받으려는 유토피아적갈망을 띤다. 본고는 한국 대체역사물이 1941년 제국주의 프로파간다의 이식 이래, 2000년대 국수주의적 밀리터리 서사의 대두, 2010년대 웹소설 생태계의 관료주의적 국가 개조(자본주의 리얼리즘), 그리고 레거시 미디어의 입헌군주제 판타지로 진화해 온 과정을 분석한다. 이를 통해 텍스트 기저에 국가 주도의 방어적 민족주의역사 교육이 잉태한 ‘경험하지 못한 제국’에 대한 동경이 도사리고 있음을 논증한다. 이는 식민 지배의 피해자가 가해자의 제국주의적 폭력성을 그대로 답습하고내면화하는 모순이다. 나아가 본 연구는 한국의 가상적 제국 기획을 일본·중국의 텍스트와 비교한다. 한국의 팽창주의는 전후 민주주의 교육을 부정하고 범죄의 역사를 윤색하려는 일본 우익의 역사수정주의(가상전기), 백년국치(百年國恥)의 트라우마를 극복하고 중화 패권(팍스 시니카)을 완성하려는 중국의 국수주의 서사와 가상 공간에서 정면으로 충돌한다. 이를 통해 동아시아의 대체역사물이 하위 장르를 넘어 배타적 민족주의가 격돌하는 ‘서사의 전쟁터’로 전락했음을 경고한다. 궁극적으로본고는 맹목적 팽창주의로 오염된 공공역사의 장에서, 역사학계가 대중과 소통하며 건강한 대안적 상상력을 파종하는 지적 주체로 나서야 함을 제언한다.

title: 滇西边境民族大学生思想政治教育模式优化与实施路径
abstract: 滇西边境地区民族大学生思想政治教育面临教育内容与学生需求脱节、教师队伍建设不足、资源支持有限等问题。本文立足滇西地区多民族文化与地缘特性,分析当前思想政治教育的现状与问题,提出了以民族文化传承与教育创新相结合的优化模式。通过政策支持与资源整合、教学方法与课程设计创新、校园文化活动推广及社会实践拓展等路径,构建多维评价体系,确保模式的实效性和可持续性。研究表明,优化后的模式不仅能提升教育效果,还为边疆民族地区高校提供了实践参考,具有重要的推广价值。

title: 患者为中心与全渠道整合视角下创新药上市策略优化
abstract: 本文聚焦中国医疗生态变革背景下创新药上市面临的现实挑战,以患者为中心与全渠 道整合双维度构建上市策略优化框架。结合患者旅程理论与全渠道营销理论,研究构 建患者需求识别—渠道协同触达—医学教育转化—治疗依从性提升的上市模型,通过感 染领域案例验证框架有效性。实证结果表明,基于患者为中心的上市策略可缩短市场 教育周期,提升诊断率与治疗转化率,在医保准入后持续提高患者留存率,为跨国药企 在华建立高效商业化体系提供实践路径。

title: 自动化行政处罚中电子数据的证明力与审查标准研究
abstract: 随着数字政府建设的推进，自动化行政处罚已成为行政执法的重要方式。电子技术监控设备生成的电子数据作为定案核心，其证明力认定与审查标准面临新挑战。当前司法实践中存在设备审查形式化、算法黑箱导致质证困难等问题。基于权益保障与技术理性的平衡，应构建分层级的证明标准体系，并从设备源头合法性、数据生成真实性、算法逻辑正当性三个维度确立实质化司法审查路径，以实现技术赋能与法治秩序的有机统一。

title: 数字化转型背景下基层党建与思想政治工作融合机制探析
abstract: 数字化转型促进基层党建与思想政治工作有效衔接,本文基于数字化转型视角,探讨 基层党建与思想政治工作融合的内在机理以及存在的问题,在此基础上提出“平台驱 动——数据赋能——机制协同”三维融合发展模式,并结合某一城市“红云智联网”智慧党 建平台具体应用情况,利用相关资料说明数字技术对于党员教育培训、舆情监测研判 以及党组织之间协调配合等方面所起的作用。研究显示,数字化融合机制对加强基层 党组织工作的精准性和思想政治工作的有效性起到推动作用,在线学习党员参与度提 高至95.8%,思想状况预警反应速度降低到93.8%,是推进新时期基层社会治理现代化 的具体抓手和有益探索。

title: 基于新课标的“过程与控制”项目式学习设计与实践
abstract: 本文基于《义务教育信息科技课程标准（2022年版）》的核心理念，以小学六年级“过程与控制”模块中《连续变化的数据》与《开关量的真与假》课程整合为例，设计了《科创成果展无人守护怎么办？》项目式学习案例。通过真实情境“校园科技展品保护”驱动，构建“问题分析—硬件应用—编程验证—迭代优化”的学习框架，引导学生借助传感器（声音、红外、光敏）采集环境数据，依托“输入-计算-输出”控制系统原理，运用图形化编程实现噪声预警、触碰警示及光线感应等功能设计。教学实践中，通过AI工具辅助思维拓展、硬件操作与分层任务适配学生认知负荷，结合“三明治反馈法”和“徽章卡”多元化评价体系，促进学生问题解决能力、计算思维及合作创新能力的提升。案例表明，跨学科融合的项目式学习能够有效突破抽象概念的教学难点，同时强化学生的技术伦理与社会责任感。研究提出四条实施建议：立足真实情境激发探索意识、分层任务指导降低认知负荷、过程性评价促进深度学习、跨学科实践渗透社会责任，为新课标背景下信息科技课程教学提供参考范例。

title: 隐性成本视角下建筑工程施工阶段造价失控的根源与治理路径
abstract: 建筑工程施工阶段隐性成本隐蔽性强且影响规模大，是常规造价管控体系的核心覆盖盲区。本文首先识别施工阶段隐性成本的两大核心构成，分别为施工组织类隐性成本与管理协调类隐性成本，明确两类成本的产生场景与表现形式。随后从前期成本测算、施工过程管控、事后成本核算三个维度，剖析隐性成本视角下施工阶段造价失控的核心根源。最后结合各类根源的特征，提出对应的全流程治理路径，为施工主体优化造价管控体系提供新的切入方向，助力施工环节降本增效目标的实现。

title: 融合户外教育与安全创新：构建山地运动可持续发展框架
abstract: 随着山地运动参与人数突破4亿人次，其大众化发展与安全保障不足的矛盾日益凸显，2024年我国山地户外探险事故达274起，死亡84人。本研究基于可持续发展理论与体教融合理念，采用问卷调查法（N=502）、案例分析法和统计分析法，系统探究户外教育与安全创新的融合路径。研究构建了“教育赋能-安全创新-协同治理”三维山地运动可持续发展框架，明确了分级教育体系、智能安全防护、多主体协同等核心实施路径。实证结果显示，该框架可使参与者安全意识提升37.2%，事故应急处置效率提高41.5%。研究为山地运动安全防控与产业高质量发展提供了实证支撑，也为国际山地运动可持续发展提供了中国方案。

title: 顺天久安,负阴抱阳——基于中华元典智慧的人性阴阳流变百年反腐治本论
abstract: 摘要:历代吏治治理始终陷入“屡治屡腐、循环往复”的千年困局,传统铁腕反腐、权力制衡、制度规制三类治理范式,均属于治标之策,存在结构性短板,无法实现长治久安。 本文立足中华元典智慧,以《道德经》“负阴抱阳”阴阳大道、郭店楚简“性自命出,命自天降”天命人性论为双重理论根基,独创人性阴阳流变吏治体系,构建区别于古今三类传统模式的第四代全新治本治吏范式。 本文提出:人性公私阴阳皆由天命派生,公私二元特质不可根除、只可制衡;历代吏治崩坏的核心根源为制度阴阳偏枯、人性单向流变;依托“一岗双荐、阴阳对冲”的干部双荐制度,可顺天命、合人性、控流变。 该方案具备极强落地优势:不削减现有官员固有职权,不增设任何行政层级、全新专职监督机构,不改动、不废除现行成熟反腐监督体系;同时与铁腕反腐、权力制衡、制度规制三类传统治理路径完全兼容、互不矛盾,可在三者基础之上叠加推行,仅嵌入原有干部提名流程即可推行,无额外行政编制与运行成本。 核心机制在于:不依赖“圣人”治吏,而是利用人性中幽暗与明德的天然张力,通过制度设计让幽暗对冲、让明德自发叠加,使制度在任何人性结构下皆能自动运转、自我纠偏。通过事前源头制衡叠加现有事后治理手段,长期动态平衡重塑吏治生态,跳出千年治乱循环,达成顺天久安的百年治理目标。 研究表明,该体系摒弃机械制衡思维,根植中国本土天命经学与天道哲学,是适配中国吏治生态、兼具理论原创性与实践长效性、落地成本极低且兼容现有全部治理框架的中式治本治腐方案。 关键词:顺天久安;人性阴阳流变;干部双荐制;幽暗与明德;性自命出,命自天降;负阴抱阳;百年反腐治本;低成本治理;体系兼容;叠加式治理

title: 思想政治教育视域下大学生生态价值观现状研究—基于广西10所高校的抽样调查
abstract: 培育大学生生态价值观是新时代高校落实立德树人根本任务、服务美丽中国建设战略的重要体现,也是思想政治教育的重要内容。研究基于对广西10所高校2035名大学生的问卷调查,从思想政治教育的认知认同、情感认同、行为践行三个维度剖析大学生生态价值观现状。调查发现,当前大学生生态价值观呈现认知碎片化与理论系统性不足、集体认同高与个人责任担当弱、行为便捷化与深层践行动力缺复合特征,背后折射出智媒体时代学生思想认知多元化、个体价值选择功利化倾向及思想政治教育中生态维度融入不足等深层思想动因。为此,高校应充分发挥思想政治教育主渠道作用,通过将习近平生态文明思想深度融入思政课程教学、强化实践育人中的价值引领与信念塑造、营造浸润式绿色校园文化氛围、构建"大思政"格局下的协同育人机制等路径,实现生态价值观从认知到认同、从情感到意志、从理念到行动的完整转化,切实引导大学生成为生态文明建设的坚定信仰者、忠实践行者和积极传播者。

title: Innovation performance of external rural tourism enterprises and high-quality rural development(乡村外来旅游企业的创新绩效与乡村高质量发展)
abstract: This study aims to explore the impact of innovation performance of external rural tourism enterprises on high-quality rural development based on questionnaire surveys conducted in case sites of the "Xiangban Group" in Jiangsu, Shanghai, Zhejiang, and Sichuan. Empirical analysis was employed to examine the intrinsic relationship. The results indicate that: (1) The innovation performance of external rural tourism enterprises significantly promotes high-quality rural development, particularly in the dimensions of industrial prosperity, ecological livability, local custom civilization, effective governance, and affluent living; (2) Exploratory innovation shows no significant correlation with cultural high-quality development, probably due to the constraints from cultural property rights protection as well as the short-term nature of such innovations; (3) Exploitative innovation enhances industrial efficiency but fails to contribute to the technological advancement and innovation-driven economic scaling required for industrial high-quality development; (4) Innovation performance plays a mediating role in the innovation of external rural tourism enterprises and the high-quality development of rural areas.The findings suggest that the innovation performance of external enterprises serves as a critical pathway for achieving rural high-quality development. It is recommended that local governments focus on the innovativeness and performance of enterprises in investment promotion, promote the implementation of the "investment-attraction for wisdom-creation" strategy, and strengthen dynamic collaborative management to form a synergistic force for high-quality development.旨在探讨乡村外来旅游企业的创新绩效及对乡村高质量发展的影响。基于上海乡伴集团在江苏、上海、浙江和四川等案例地的问卷调研，通过实证分析，验证了乡村外来旅游企业的创新行为与乡村高质量发展存在关联性。研究结果表明：（1）乡村外来旅游企业的创新绩效对乡村高质量发展具有显著正向影响，具体体现在产业兴旺、生态宜居、乡风文明、治理有效和生活富裕5个维度上；（2）乡村外来旅游企业的探索式创新与乡村文化高质量发展间无显著相关性，可能受限于文化产权的保护与短期创新实践；（3）乡村外来旅游企业的利用式创新虽能提升产业效率，但与乡村产业高质量发展的科技化和创新经济规模无关；（4）创新绩效在乡村外来旅游企业创新与乡村高质量发展间起中介作用。研究表明，提高外来旅游企业的创新绩效是实现乡村高质量发展的重要路径之一，建议地方政府在招商引资中注重企业的创新性与绩效表现，推动“招商选智”策略的实施，强化动态协同管理，以形成高质量发展合力。

title: 习近平关于公权力重要论述的三维阐析：时代生成、科学内涵及价值意蕴
abstract: 习近平关于公权力的重要论述，是新时代中国共产党人围绕权力本源、运行及监督形成的系统化理论成果。相关重要论述以马克思主义权力观为理论根基，以“两个结合”为方法论支撑，在推动国家治理现代化的实践中生成发展，具有深厚的理论积淀与实践基础。其科学内涵以“权为民所赋、权为民所用、把权力关进制度的笼子里”为核心要义，构建起权力来源观、权力行使观与权力监督观相贯通的内容体系，深化了对中国共产党执政、社会主义建设、人类社会发展的规律性认识，为新时代治国理政提供了根本遵循，为人类政治文明进步贡献了中国智慧。

title: “第四支队伍”视域下高校辅导员核心素养的内涵拓展与提升路径
abstract: 高校辅导员作为高校育人“第四支队伍”，是新时代立德树人的核心力量。人工智能赋能教育变革背景下，传统辅导员素养框架难以适配数字化、专业化育人新要求。立足“第四支队伍”战略定位与辅导员角色转型需求，在政治、道德、职业传统三维素养基础上，拓展协同、数智、发展素养，构建层级分明、功能互补的辅导员六维核心素养体系，厘清各素养维度的核心内涵与功能价值，从协同培育、数字赋能、实践锤炼、制度保障四方面搭建系统化、长效化的素养提升路径。

title: 基于大学生群体画像的“精准思政”研究
abstract: 大数据时代为高校思想政治教育创新提供了技术上的可能，同时也带来了对高校思想政治教育工作针对性和实效性的更高要求。从大学生群体画像和精准思政内在逻辑维度出发，以高校思想政治教育资源供给侧结构性改革为契机，构建“精准识别-精准供给-精准评估”三维实践框架。通过系统解构大学生群体核心属性与线上行为规律，阐释大数据技术的赋能机理，提出以思政类短视频为核心载体的精准施政策略，凸显网络环境净化对精准思政实施的长效保障功能。研究表明，深化大数据技术应用、完善群体画像驱动的精准思政模式，是推动高校思政教育创新发展、破解传统育人困境的重要前提与关键路径。

title: "大思政"格局下音乐美育与高校党建协同育人模式研究
abstract: 在新时代教育改革的背景下,"大思政"理念的提出推动了思想政治教育模式的系统创新。音乐美育凭借其独特的审美价值和情感功能,与高校党建的政治引领形成了天然契合。本文从"大思政"的理论内涵出发,分析了当前高校思政教育存在的结构性矛盾,并探讨音乐美育在弥补认知与情感割裂、提升教育吸引力方面的独特优势。在此基础上,提出课程协同、活动协同和平台协同的"三维一体"路径,并构建认知、情感、行为、影响"四维一体"的评价体系。研究表明,音乐美育与高校党建的协同不仅有助于实现知识传授与价值塑造的统一,也为立德树人的根本任务提供了可操作的实践范式。

title: 比较视域下中国特色社会主义道路对苏联模式的超越
abstract: 苏联模式曾长期被视为社会主义建设的“标准模板”，但因内在结构性危机而未能自我革新，终成苏联解体的制度根源。与之形成鲜明对照的是，中国在经历了对苏联模式的移植、反思与突破之后，走出了一条充满生机与活力的中国特色社会主义道路。“一种性质，两种模式”的不同结局构成了本文研究的核心问题：中国特色社会主义道路究竟在哪些维度上实现了对苏联模式的超越？本文将从经济、政治、文化三个维度展开比较分析。

title: A Global History of Modern Japan
abstract: In this innovative and timely history, Frederick Dickinson reenvisions the modern world through the prism of Japan, reexamining well-worn assumptions of familiar global processes. If viewed through the lens of modern Japan, such typical signposts of transition as Reformation, Renaissance, Revolution, and Reconstruction shift from normative categories to reconsiderations of the human experience. Nineteenth-century industrialization, modernization, and empire-building mark not a “rise of the West” but the dawn of a global age. The “American Century” is best understood not as a triumph of democracy but as an era of profound global economic, political, geopolitical, and cultural transformation. This new, integrative model for national history writing replaces narratives of exceptionalism with the intellectual foundations for global citizenship.

title: Understanding Modern Japan Through Its Literature
abstract: In today’s ever-shrinking "global village", intercultural communication based on mutual respect and understanding is more important than ever. The humanities foster precisely this kind of understanding of cultures other than our own. One of the most effective ways to gain deep insight into another society is through its literature, which offers an insider’s perspective on history, religion, politics, and social values. Understanding Modern Japan Through Its Literature, based on more than fifty years of research, provides such an in-depth view of one of the world’s most fascinating cultures. The volume explores how Japanese writers and intellectuals responded to the turbulent history of the past century and a half, from Western imperialism and Japan’s own imperial expansion to wartime defeat, atomic destruction, and postwar economic recovery. By examining literary responses to these dramatic transformations, the book reveals how Japanese authors struggled to construct and reconstruct national identity amid imperialism, modernization, capitalism, fascism, and globalization. In doing so, it offers an intimate and compelling portrait of Japanese experience throughout the twentieth century.

title: Japan After Dark
abstract: Laura Nenzi draws readers into a fascinating world of samurai, shipwrecks, nocturnal monsters and partying crowds, in this richly detailed, illustrated and evocative history of the night. The world over, the installation of public lights transformed the night, reshaping expressions of authority; altering centuries-old forms of production and consumption; and enabling the expansion of legitimate daytime activities into the night hours. The cities of Tokugawa Japan, however, lacked any kind of public illumination until the late nineteenth century. Nonetheless, Nenzi shows, many of the attributes associated with the modern night were firmly in place in cities and villages well before the age of streetlights. This exploration of the transformation of early modern Japan after dark challenges accepted definitions of modernity, encouraging readers to rethink the way we write history.

title: The Science of Economic Activities — Volume 2: Principles of Economic Activities
abstract: The Science of Economic Activities is a six‑volume original theoretical system reconstructing the underlying operating laws of human socioeconomic development. Built upon social cooperative division of labor and labor‑time accounting, this series provides a complete framework covering research methodology, core economic‑activity principles, market mechanisms, the distribution‑and‑ exchange principles of consumer‑goods chains, universal economic constitution, quantitative formulas, core models and nine governance‑support systems. It offers theoretical references for understanding and addressing real‑world challenges including poverty, unemployment and global conflicts. As Volume Two of the six‑volume monograph series, this volume systematically unfolds the foundational principles of the discipline. Departing from assumption‑driven reasoning in conventional economics, it derives economic rules from real‑world production, division of labor, and exchange processes. It explains core principles covering consumer‑goods production, cost, net profit, currency, distribution and exchange, and clarifies the internal logic of market circulation equilibrium. Based on two unified foundational axioms and verified by the successful economic development practices of East Asian economies, this volume validates the rationality and practicality of the new economic theoretical system. The Fundamental Economic Principles to Eliminate Unemployment, Poverty and War I. Theoretical Axioms: Empirically Verifiable Underlying Premises of Economic Development (Feasibility Argumentation) Departing from the hypothesis-driven and reality-detached analytical paradigm of mainstream economics, this theory is grounded in the practical development experiences of real economies across the globe and establishes two core foundational axioms. Empirical evidence demonstrates that the total elimination of large-scale unemployment, endogenous poverty, and regional conflicts induced by economic imbalances fulfills fully objective, executable, and replicable real-world conditions for human society. From a global perspective, all essential preconditions for addressing these three pivotal global challenges have been fully established: First, the natural resources, technological advancements, and mature social systems required to eradicate unemployment and poverty already exist on a global scale. (1) The Earth’s natural resource reserves are adequate to sustain a global population of billions at the living standards characteristic of developed economies; (2) Modern technological systems capable of mass-producing abundant, low-cost consumer goods have matured and proliferated worldwide; (3) An efficient social collaborative division-of-labor system has been established. Supported by sophisticated social production models, it delivers consistent, high-efficiency output of sufficient consumer goods to maintain a modern society with universal prosperity; (4) Industrial engineering has fully standardized the production workflows, operational procedures, standard labor hours, and all technical requirements for consumer goods manufacturing, enabling rapid cross-regional replication of mature production models; (5) Collaborative production and social division-of-labor principles significantly boost aggregate social output. They enable developing economies to advance economic development through commercialized operational models and achieve cross-border replication of industrial systems alongside rapid industrialization. Second, human labor time is an inherently scarce socioeconomic resource. Unemployment constitutes a severe structural distortion of economic operations, contradicting the fundamental nature of economic systems and resulting in the waste of precious human labor resources. Case Study 1 The developmental trajectory of East Asian economies provides conclusive empirical validation of this theory. Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Hong Kong of China, and Taiwan of China have rapidly transformed from backward, poverty-stricken agricultural societies into highly developed economies with sophisticated social division of labor, successfully accomplishing social transformation toward universal prosperity and full employment. Supported by systematic, standardized economic operational mechanisms, mainland China has implemented the largest and fastest poverty alleviation and unemployment governance initiative in human history, fundamentally reversing the long-standing predicaments of widespread poverty and mass unemployment. Case Study 2 Developed economies across Europe and North America offer a second set of compelling empirical cases. These regions have largely eliminated mass unemployment and systemic poverty. The limited poverty and unemployment observed within these societies primarily stem from individual educational gaps, skill mismatches, or short-term cyclical economic fluctuations that lead to individualized rather than structural deprivation. These representative cases definitively prove that poverty, unemployment, and underdevelopment are not inherent or unavoidable destinies for any nation or region. Once an economy adopts a scientific, complete, and standardized operational system, it can rapidly escape underdevelopment and evolve from a traditional society plagued by high unemployment and widespread scarcity into a modern, developed society characterized by full employment, abundant material supply, and stable social order. This provides robust, practical evidence for the systematic global eradication of poverty, unemployment, and economically driven regional conflicts. In contrast, mainstream neoclassical economics constructs its theoretical framework on artificial hypothetical assumptions rather than authentic production and division-of-labor practices. Its analytical scope is confined to superficial market price volatility and partial equilibrium phenomena, while entirely overlooking the fundamental socioeconomic logic based on real labor input, resource constraints, and systematic social division of labor. Incapable of quantitatively explaining the structural contradictions between production, distribution, and consumption, traditional economics cannot fundamentally resolve persistent global crises, including structural unemployment, endogenous poverty, and economy-triggered regional conflicts. Conventional macroeconomic tools—including monetary policy, fiscal stimulus, and social welfare subsidies—only alleviate superficial economic symptoms in the short term and fail to eliminate recurring economic crises, structural social imbalances, and geopolitical frictions rooted in economic inequality. II. Core Ultimate Questions: Systemic Dilemmas Unsolved by Global Economics for a Century Based on the aforementioned empirical axioms and a century of turbulent global economic development, this theory refines seven foundational questions that have long perplexed mainstream economic research. These century-old structural dilemmas cannot be reasonably interpreted or thoroughly resolved by conventional economic frameworks, and they constitute the core research focus and central logical thread of this theoretical system. 1. Given that poverty eradication, full employment, and long-term economic stability are practically achievable, what are the necessary and sufficient underlying conditions to completely eliminate social unemployment, endogenous poverty, and economically induced regional conflicts? A. Principle of Full Employment: Resolve Unemployment at the Root Unemployment fundamentally originates from the structural imbalance between aggregate social labor time supply and labor time demand. The essence of full employment governance lies in achieving dynamic equilibrium between annual total labor demand and annual total labor supply across the entire society. Core Equilibrium Equation: Annual Labor Time Demand = Annual Labor Time Supply Quantitative Formula: Total Market Consumer Goods Output × Standard Labor Time per Unit Output = Economically Active Population × Annual Statutory Working Hours (Annual Total Days minus Legal Rest Days) Full employment requires not only aggregate labor time balance but also precise structural matching between industrial skill demands and worker skill endowments. Governments can popularize standardized compulsory education and professional vocational training systems to continuously upgrade public professional competencies and universal employability, enabling ordinary laborers to adapt to mainstream industrial positions. By integrating industrial engineering standards, quantitative mathematical modeling, and complete economic operational principles, societies can conduct precise numerical deduction, real-time dynamic monitoring, and scientific macro-regulation of the labor supply–demand system, thereby maintaining long-term, stable full employment. B. Efficient Social Collaborative Division-of-Labor System: Fundamentally Eradicate Endogenous Poverty The establishment of an efficient, orderly, and nationally adaptive social collaborative division-of-labor system is the core prerequisite for eliminating endogenous poverty. A mature division-of-labor system enables the free flow, precise allocation, and spatial agglomeration of diverse production factors, forming large-scale industrial cluster effects. This continuously reduces manufacturing costs, optimizes macroscopic supply–demand structures, balances market circulation, and generates stable, abundant, low-cost consumer goods, comprehensively elevating societal material living standards. Furthermore, a complete collaborative division-of-labor system can be complemented by inclusive social security and insurance mechanisms to address individualized poverty caused by temporary unemployment, illness, or other unforeseen contingencies among vulnerable groups. title: The stolen room
abstract: Paris, autumn . Kōjirō Matsukata, a Japanese aristocrat with a deep passion for Western art, acquires Van Gogh’s The Bedroom at Arles. This exceptional canvas enhances a remarkable collection built up over decades, with love for and respect for European art. But the Second World War will upend the collection’s fate. In , in the offices of the French Provisional Government, one of the most sophisticated art spoliations in modern history is set in motion. Eighty years later, Pierre Bertier, a professor driven by a thirst for justice, uncovers the hidden mechanisms behind this spoliation. Armed only with his determination, he embarks on a titanic struggle against the French diplomatic apparatus. As told in this novel inspired by real events, the Matsukata affair shows that justice is not measured merely by the achievement of tangible restitutions, but also—and above all—by the gradual transformation of public debate. Sometimes, persistently asking the right questions matters more than immediately obtaining the right answers.

title: All the Seas Were Ink
abstract: In this innovative history of the travels of law, Iza R. Hussin explores how law moves, what happens when it arrives, and how it gains its onward momentum and direction. Through the itineraries of Abu Bakar, Sultan of Johor (1833–1895), Hussin uncovers a world of sovereigns in the shadow of empire, from Hawaii to Singapore, Java to Japan, Delhi to Constantinople, Cairo to London. In his travels, Abu Bakar navigated archipelagic and imperial logics of authority, chased sovereignty at sea, and translated Islam across a shifting global landscape. These itineraries gave rise to Southeast Asia's first constitution, and the world's longest-running continuous experiment in modern Islamic constitutionalism, revealing histories of imperialism and international law, and forgotten genealogies of sovereignty, constitutionalism, and Asian internationalism. Through the compelling story of Abu Bakar's travels, Hussin argues for a new understanding of the imperial international order, Islamic constitutional history, and the making of the modern Muslim state.

title: MACEDONIA AND MACEDONIANS, BRIEF HISTORY https://macedonian-istoria.blogspot.com/
abstract: INTRODUCTION What is the Macedonia and who are the Macedonians? Circular letter to the western allies of the American Minister of Foreign Affairs, Stettinius, in 1944, about Macedonia. (U.S. State Department, Foreign Relations Vol. VIII, 868.014 / 26 Dec. 1944), "The Department has noted increasing propaganda rumors and semi-official statements in favor of an autonomous Macedonia, emanating principally from Bulgaria, but also from Yugoslav Partisan and other sources, with the implication that Greek territory would be included in the projected state. This Government (of USA) considers talk of Macedonian 'nation', Macedonian 'Fatherland', or Macedonian 'national consciousness' to be unjustified demagoguery representing no ethnic, nor political reality, and sees in its present revival a possible cloak for aggressive intentions against Greece. The approved policy of this Government is to oppose any revival of the Macedonian issue as related to Greece. The Greek section of Macedonia is largely inhabited by Greeks, and the Greek people are almost unanimously opposed to the creation of a Macedonian state. Allegations of serious Greek participation in any such agitation can be assumed to be false. This Government (of USA) would regard as responsible any Government or group of Governments tolerating or encouraging menacing or aggressive acts of 'Macedonian forces' against Greece." MACEDONIAN PREHISTORY: Macedonian Prehistory: Is it the cradle of the first human on Earth? 1. Ouranopithecus macedoniensis is a prehistoric species of Ouranopithecus from the Late Miocene, found in Macedonia (Greece), 9 million years old. More details can be found at Ouranopithecus - Ouranopithecus macedoniensis. 2. A groundbreaking analysis of other ancient fossils discovered in macedonia is challenging traditional theories about where human ancestors evolved. Scientists examining 8 to 9 million year old jaw bones from the village of Nikiti have found evidence suggesting that early ape ancestors of humans may have evolved in Southeastern Europe before migrating to Africa, rather than evolving exclusively on the African continent as Charles Darwin proposed in 1871. The research team led by David Begun from the University of Toronto's Department of Anthropology analyzed fossilized jaw bones originally thought to belong to Ouranopithecus, an extinct Eurasian ape. However, their reexamination revealed hominin like canines and premolar roots that suggest these remains may represent a previously unknown proto hominin species. This discovery builds on the team's 2017 identification of Graecopithecus, a 7.2 million year old ape found in Greece and Bulgaria that shows features potentially linking it to early hominins. According to this hypothesis, the older Nikiti ape would have directly preceded Graecopithecus, and then early hominins migrated south into Africa around 7 million years ago where their descendants eventually evolved into the genus Homo. Begun points out that ancient Southeastern Europe was once home to ancestors of giraffes, rhinos and antelopes that we now associate with Africa, suggesting that if these animals successfully migrated from Europe to Africa millions of years ago, ape ancestors could have followed similar routes. However, the scientific community remains divided on this theory. Many experts argue that the Nikiti ape might be completely unrelated to human ancestors, possibly developing similar features through convergent evolution rather than direct ancestry. The out of Africa model continues to be supported by a more robust fossil record and DNA evidence from later periods. While the Nikiti fossils alone do not definitively overturn established theories, they open fascinating questions about hominin origins and highlight the need for more fossil discoveries from both Europe and Africa dating between 8 and 7 million years ago to establish clearer connections. 3. Graecopithecus Graecopithecus is an extinct genus of hominid that lived in Southeast Europe during the Late Miocene, around 7 million years ago. Initially, this species was identified based on a single jawbone with teeth, found in Pyrgos Vasilissis, Athens, Greece, in 1944. Later, in 2012, other teeth were discovered in the Azmaka quarry in Bulgaria. Given that few, and poorly preserved, materials have been found so far, scientists consider it the "least known European Miocene hominoid." In 2017, an international team of paleontologists, led by Madelaine Böhme of the Eberhard-Karls-University of Tübingen, Germany, published a detailed analysis of the teeth and age of the specimens. They concluded that Graecopithecus could be the oldest hominin, meaning it might be the oldest direct ancestor of humans, having separated from the chimpanzee lineage. Graecopithecus tooths (Azmaka, Bulgaria). See more at Graecopithicus. 3. Archanthropus of Petralona, Chalkidiki Macedonia (See more at Wikipedia, Archanthropus Petraloniensis). Around 800-700 thousand years old, (dated by the Uranium-Thorium method by Japanese nuclear scientists) it is identified either as Homo erectus, or a Neanderthal, or an early form of Homo sapiens. Of course, those who worship Orthodoxy speak instead of some archaic hominid that is not related to the aforementioned "classic" homos. Two skeletons 800,000 years old were also found in the cave. DISPILIO. THE OLDEST KNOWN TEXT. The Dispilio Tablet is a wooden plaque with inscribed markings, discovered during the excavations of George Hourmouziadis at Dispilio in Macedonia-Greece, and carbon 14-dated to 5202 (± 123) BC. It was discovered in 1993 in a Neolithic settlement on the shore of a lake that occupies an artificial island near the modern village of Dispilio on Lake Kastoria in Kastoria, Western Macedonia, Greece. Dispilio Tablet Dating The Dispilio Tablet was one of many artifacts found in the area of Macedonia. However, the importance of the tablet lies in the fact that an unknown written text was engraved on it, dating back beyond 5,000 BC (7,000 years from today). Researchers used radiocarbon dating to accurately determine the date of the wooden plaque to about 5,260 BC, which would make it significantly older than the writing system used by the Sumerians. The text on the plaque includes a type of carved script which probably consists of a form of writing that predated the Linear «B» script used by the Mycenaean Greeks. Like the tablet, many other ceramic pieces were found that also have the same type of writing on them. Samples of the carved signs on the wooden Dispilio tablet and other clay finds discovered at the site (a) as compared to Linear A signs (b) and signs found on Paleo European clay tablets (c). (Yorgos Facorellis / CC BY 3.0) MYTHOLOGY Mount Olympus, located in Macedonia, was the center of the Macedonian state and a holy place for all Greeks, because it was the seat of the Greek gods. Next to Olympus is Mount Pierion, where the Macedonian King Pierus introduced the cult of the Muses, who were named after his daughters (nine Muses). According to Hesiod, around 750 BC ("Theogony," book "Catalogue of Women," A, 2, where Hesiod describes the genealogy of the Greek tribes), Macedon and Magnet (Magnet belongs to the Thessalian tribes, Magnesia, the area around the modern city of Volos and Magnesia in Asia Minor) were children of the god Zeus and Pandora. Pandora was the daughter of Deucalion. She was the sister of Hellen (ancestor of the Greeks), who was also the son of Deucalion. Deucalion was the first man in the world, the man who was saved from the cataclysm after the Great Flood. The "Flood of Deucalion" is the Greek version of Noah's Flood. That version is much older (it is probable that Jewish mythology copied that myth directly from the Greek or indirectly from the Mesopotamian version, like Gilgamesh) and refers to a real event, i.e., the flooding and submergence of the Aegean hills and the creation of the Aegean Sea at the beginning of the geological period Holocene, i.e., around 10,000 BC. title: Routledge Handbook of the Economic History of Colonialism
abstract: European colonial rule in Asia, Africa, and the Americas was a world-changing force and left a variety of legacies - demographic, economic, environmental, technological, and cultural. The economic history of colonialism has seen an outburst of research in the last 20-odd years; but, with many significant new works appearing in specialist journals, students and teachers of the field may still find it challenging to explain what this scholarship adds up to, its most significant claims and breakthroughs and how it relates to older versions of the economic history of colonialism. This handbook gathers a set of specially commissioned essays written by leading contributors to the field which focus on the two principal waves of European colonialism since the 15th century: the first in which Europeans converged mainly on the Americas (c. 1490s-1820s) and the second in which attention was focused on acquiring control over large swathes of Asia and Africa (c. 1850s-1970s). It shows students of economic history the key facts that need to be explained about the imperial powers, the colonial experience, and why the European empires outside Europe are significant for the economic history of the world. The handbook also includes studies of the Japanese and American Empires in Asia, as these were provoked by and in nature quite comparable to the formation of European empires thus providing worthwhile and meaningful comparisons. This handbook will serve as a vital resource for research, teaching, and reference, offering readers insights into economic history, colonialism, globalisation, and the forces that have shaped the modern world economy.

title: Dual-track Diplomacy
abstract: Between 1931 and 1937, Nationalist China was caught between Japanese imperial expansion and the unpredictable intentions of the Soviet Union, facing an increasingly hostile external environment. This book reconstructs how China navigated this precarious situation through a sophisticated strategy known as 'dual-track diplomacy'. While seeking to delay a full-scale war by accommodating Japan, Chiang Kai-shek endeavoured to improve relations with the Soviet Union as a potential counterweight. Moving beyond traditional narratives, the book analyses the underlying mechanics of diplomatic practice, revealing how factional divisions, overlapping authorities, and secret channels were exploited as strategic assets. It shows that the careful management of the divergence between internal authority and external posture influenced how China's diplomatic orientation was perceived abroad. This approach enabled Nanjing to engage in parallel, and sometimes contradictory, diplomacy with Tokyo and Moscow. By integrating Sino-Japanese and Sino-Soviet relations into a single framework, the book offers a new perspective on East Asian international history during the interwar period. It will appeal to scholars and students of modern Chinese history and East Asian international relations.

title: Engagements with Modern Japanese Literature
abstract: Engagements with Modern Japanese Literature offers an accessible introduction to the development of modern Japanese literature from the Meiji period (1868–1912) to contemporary Japan. It combines literary history and literary analysis to provide an overview as well as in-depth understanding of literary development in the past 150 years. Modern Japanese literature includes an abundant body of work that allows readers to gain insight into the literary, cultural, social, historical, and political development of modern Japan. Angela Yiu begins by exploring the voices of modernity in Meiji literature, including the work of Higuchi Ichiyō, Izumi Kyōka, Natsume Sōseki, and others. Yiu then turns to utopianism and modernism in Taishō and Prewar Literature (1912–1936), and considers Shirakaba-ha writers. The book also looks at women in war and postwar literature (1926–1952), examining a wide range of authors including Ishikawa Jun, Sata Ineko, Hayashi Fumiko, and Sakaguchi Ango. It provides rich insight into the legacy of six major writers from 1950–1970, including the two Nobel Prize laureates Kawabata Yasunari and Ōe Kenzaburō, as well as Mishima Yukio, Enchi Fumiko, Abe Kōbo, and Ishimure Michiko. It concludes by focusing on literature in contemporary Japan from 1989 to the present, offering fascinating insight into the work of Murakami Haruki, Tawada Yōko, Mizumura Minae, and many others. Consistently structured, each chapter introduces key concepts and literary developments; detailed analysis of selected authors and major works; and helpful bolding throughout of important terms discussed further in the glossary. It also features an invaluable glossary, lists of useful resources, major publications and events, and a bibliography of Further Reading. Written with the dual purposes of a teaching resource and an introductory guide, this is an essential text for students and teachers of Japanese literature and culture.

title: China Reborn, 1895–1912
abstract: Abstract China Reborn, 1895–1912 challenges the master narrative of modern Chinese history, which has long framed the fall of the Qing empire and the rise of the Republic of China as the inevitable triumph of Chinese nationalism. This nationalist narrative obscures an intricate reality: many of the so-called nationalists were simultaneously localists, whose political pursuits were rooted in the specific crises of their native places and designed to redress them. Nor does nationalist teleology adequately explain why localism—so often a force that toppled old dynasties only to install new ones—suddenly turned against dynastic rule altogether and championed a republic instead. Departing from the familiar sweep of national history, this book proposes a trialectic framework—local, national, and transnational—to reinterpret the transformation of the Qing empire. It shows how a new China was born out of the dynamic interplay among localism, nationalism, and imperialism. Combining a social history of the activities of Qing elites educated in Meiji Japan and an intellectual history of their localist pursuits, it illuminates how Japanese knowledge crossed national boundaries to ignite local changes that ultimately remade the Qing empire. Through their experiences abroad, these elites reinforced native-place bonds, deepened local sentiment, and embraced new localist visions of China. Drawing on Japanese knowledge, they formulated four lines of localist strategies and took pains to translate them into practice in an effort to reconfigure the Qing empire.

title: The Phantom Hitchhiker
abstract: The Phantom Hitchhiker offers the first organic study of one of modernity’s most haunting stories: the encounter with a figure—generally a young woman—whose presence unsettles the border between life and death. Focusing on the porous relationship between literature and folklore, the book follows the ‘phantom hitchhiker’ motif as it moves across oral storytelling, fiction, journalism, cinema, television, and the subcultures of the early digital age. Centred on Italy yet resolutely transnational, the book reveals a subtle, longstanding affinity with the Japanese tradition of ghostlore—a long-distance dialogue, grounded not in surface similarity but in deeper patterns of cultural sensibility. What emerges is a story that is anything but static: a motif continuously reinvented, capable of illuminating the shifting borders between life and death, belief and fiction, local memory and global circulation. The author brings to the material a command of multiple languages and literary traditions, combined with an acute sensitivity to the cultural dynamics of modernity, particularly in terms of the metamorphoses and survivals of the supernatural in an age of presumed disenchantment. The volume weaves close reading and literary theory with approaches drawn from folklore studies and media history, offering a genuinely innovative account of how ghost stories travel, transform, and survive across cultures and discursive regimes. It will prove fascinating for scholars and students in folklore, literary studies, Italian studies and the humanities, as well as for readers drawn to the spectral textures of modern culture and to the afterlives of the stories we continue to tell in the dark.

title: Iberian Crossroads
abstract: Abstract Iberian Crossroads unveils for the first time Spain’s rich contributions to the birth of the modern world. More than a country confined within the territorial boundaries of the Iberian Peninsula, the book shows how in the “long” nineteenth century Spain was immersed in a dense web of global connections spanning the Americas, Europe, Africa, and Asia. The emergence of citizenship and new constitutional cultures, the movement of slaves and political exiles across national borders, and the changing imperial dynamics are but a small sample of world phenomena in which Spain’s role was key, a role which remains largely unexplored by historians. In delving into the Spanish involvement in world history, the book also sheds light on the multiple and complex ways in which Europe experienced globalization. Against the tendency of examining the long nineteenth century through the traditional lens of the Great Powers, the case of Spain provides a fresh, alternative angle from which to appreciate Europe’s dynamic interactions with the world. Iberian Crossroads offers, in short, a timely contribution to the greater task of transcending isolated national histories as well as a manifesto calling for a more plural and diverse history.

Bisexuality and Beyond
abstract: Abstract Bisexuality and Beyond is the first historical study of bisexuality in Britain. It uses original oral histories alongside extensive archival research to explore the creation of the gay/straight binary from the perspective of those who fell beyond its limits, challenging historical narratives about liberationist politics and identity formation. Historians of sexuality agree that the binary divide between gay and straight is a relatively recent invention, only becoming dominant around the mid-twentieth century. The history of bisexuality is the missing piece in this narrative. This book looks at the broader circumstances of this period to investigate the problems of defining bisexuality and its politics coherently, and of navigating its relationship to gay and lesbian politics. This book therefore sets out the concept of ‘multiple-gender-attraction’, an umbrella term that encompasses and extends beyond the category of bisexuality. It is not an identity label, but a description of potential attraction, drawing on queer historical approaches to explore the distinctions between emotions, behaviour, and identity. Through detailed histories of the gay liberation movement, lesbian feminism, and Britain’s first bisexual organizations, Bisexuality and Beyond argues that the binary of gay and straight was created and reinforced by gay and lesbian politics as well as dominant straight society. By placing bisexuality and multiple-gender-attraction squarely in the frame, this book changes how we understand the emergence of identity politics in modern Britain, challenging established notions about the ‘queer’ inclusivity of counter-cultural activism, and intervening in histories of identity, selfhood, community, and radicalism.

Early Modern Neurodivergence
abstract: Abstract Early Modern Neurodivergence explains how what we nowadays call neurodivergence was understood, described, and lived in Europe during the era of 1550–1750. Focusing on texts from Britain, Spain, and Poland, this literary study centres neurodivergent experiences and ways of engaging with texts throughout. Through the Classical and Renaissance figure of Echo, the introduction lays out ‘reading for resonance’ as a useful way of approaching early modern neurodivergence. The four chapters explore: neurodivergent representation in Lope de Vega’s play La Dama Boba, stimming while reading Miguel de Cervantes’ novel Don Quijote, the sonnet sequence as a neurodivergent literary form (focusing on Jan Kochanowski’s Treny and Anne Lok’s A Meditation of a Penitent Sinner), and a practice-as-research project reading the 1747–1748 Scottish case about Idiocy, Blair v Blair as a piece of verbatim theatre. The book’s coda challenges Anglo-American claims that neurodiversity studies is a ‘new’ field and looks towards a future where all who want to be included are in this field and no one is left behind.

The New Modern Conductor
abstract: Abstract The New Modern Conductor, inspired by the classic text of Dr. Elizabeth A. H. Green, offers an innovative approach to conducting based on establishing pulse rather than on beating time. As the physical craft of conducting cannot be separated from the music being conducted, learning both is crucial. The New Modern Conductor intersperses chapters devoted to technical skills, both conducting and musical, with “Score Study” chapters—score analyses, teaching the reader how to study, understand, and conduct the composer’s music. When studied at the same time—handcraft and scores—the reader can integrate both toward mastery of conducting. Scores chosen are within reach of the beginner and can be studied either in their entirety or in sections, and practiced with small ensemble, two pianos, one piano, or with an entire ensemble. Replacing obsolete beat pattern graphics, video links are provided to demonstrate specific conducting gestures. Working through The New Modern Conductor, the student is exposed to dozens of different composers and works, including links to scores and performances. Standard works for orchestra are the focus, but there are chapters devoted as well to wind, choral, and collaborative conducting, including opera, musical theater, and dance. Later chapters address practical aspects of conducting, careers, emerging composers, broadening the reach of our art, and the role of the conductor in the community. Instead of tests, there are questions. One question leads to the next, and still more questions, which, if pursued, lead to knowledge, understanding, and after many scores and much work, mastery.

title: Modern Russian Prose
abstract: The textbook analyzes well-known works of Russian literature written in the first quarter of the twenty-first century that reflect various directions and trends in the contemporary cultural process. The first section of the book contains a brief overview of the theory of postmodernism as well as metamodernism, a movement that is currently in the process of formation. The second section provides general information about contemporary writers who have attracted critical attention and are involved in the literary prize circuit, accompanied by a critical analysis of the works by the authors presented in the book. Intended for students studying the course “History of Contemporary Russian Literature”.

title: Morbid
abstract: A darkly comedic journey into the science of aging—where ethics are irrelevant, the studies are a sales pitch, and the “world's oldest living people” all turn out to be dead. Our morbid fascination with death and dying has created an opening for all manner of skullduggery in the science of aging—an area of study that Morbid reveals to be rife with misleading claims, mistaken assumptions, and outright chicanery. The world’s oldest man is a fake, Blue Zones are debunked, and five decades of research on human longevity is moot. What begins with a petition to exhume a famous corpse descends into amusing, if edifying, chaos as Saul Justin Newman sets out to discover what’s rotten and what’s real in the science of dying. Unraveling an immense scientific scandal, the author finds a billionaire wrapped up in a scheme to tap the blood of Texas teenagers, the whole field of aging awash in dubious money—and himself somehow accused of spying for Russia by a CIA operative. But under the shocking absurdities lurk deadly serious questions about how people age, how long they live, and why. Newman addresses these questions with genuine curiosity and scientific rigor, contributing mathematical evidence and evolutionary insights into the mystery and mechanics of why we age and why we die.

Sounding Nation, Hearing Race in Modern Music
abstract: Abstract Sounding Nation, Hearing Race in Modern Music uses close readings of musical works and original archival research to document the influence of transnational exchanges on the imaginings of racial and national identity in interwar concert music. Even as scientific racism continued to shape public thought and policy, the very meaning of “race,” and its connection to national identity, was reimagined in this era. Between the wars, stages across Europe, the United States, and Latin America were flooded with ballets, operas, and program music that explicitly thematized race. Critical responses to such works debated not only their aesthetic merits but also the visions of national identity they represented. Musical works were often understood to project racial and national identities, making music criticism an important forum for debate. This book centers the United States, Brazil, and France, reflecting both composers’ travels and these nations’ common concerns. United as wartime allies in the Great War, each navigated legacies of enslavement, colonialism, and imperialism; in the aftermath of the First World War, each rewrote immigration policies in an attempt to (re)shape an idealized national body. In a series of case studies focusing on works by Darius Milhaud, Heitor Villa-Lobos, George Gershwin, John Alden Carpenter, William Grant Still, and Francisco Mignone, this book examines the malleability of ideas of race, Self, and Other; the close relationship between the social sciences, music, and race; the processes through which race was rendered “audible” to period audiences; and the ways primitivism was racialized and subsequently reimagined by marginalized composers.

Oxford Studies in Early Modern Philosophy
abstract: Abstract Oxford Studies in Early Modern Philosophy is an annual series presenting a selection of the best current work in the history of early modern philosophy. It focuses on the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries—the extraordinary period of intellectual activity that begins, roughly, with Descartes and his contemporaries and ends with Kant. It also publishes work on thinkers or movements outside of that framework, provided they are important in illuminating early modern thought. The core of the subject matter is philosophy and its history. But the volume’s chapters reflect the fact that philosophy in the early modern period was broader in scope than it is currently taken to be and included a great deal of what now belongs to the natural sciences. Furthermore, philosophy in the period was closely connected with other disciplines, such as theology, law, and medicine, and with larger questions of social, political, and religious history. Volume 13 includes chapters dedicated to a wide range of topics in the philosophies of René Descartes, Thomas Bonarte, Blaise Pascal, Benedict Spinoza, Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz, Christian Wolff, Alexander Baumgarten, Christian Crusius, Immanuel Kant, and David Hume.

Anne Bradstreet Now
abstract: Abstract This book re-envisions Anne Bradstreet’s legacy by presenting contemporary poets’ and writers’ reflections that illuminate her enduring influence, artistic complexity, and cultural relevance. It highlights Bradstreet’s early feminist impulses, her spiritual devotion, and the power of her elegies, love lyrics, meditations, and autobiographical writing that shape conversations about early American literature. The book emphasizes how her stature persists across nearly four centuries through both her notable achievements and the controversies that continue to complicate her reception. It demonstrates how leading American poets use new poems and essays to situate Bradstreet within diverse literary, cultural, political, and theological frameworks that call for ongoing reinterpretation. Finally, the book shows how Bradstreet’s work continues to resonate, challenge, frustrate, astonish, and inspire readers and writers who confront her evolving legacy.

Brokering a Race War
abstract: Abstract Brokering a Race War traces the complex experiences of second-generation Japanese American (Nisei) soldiers and civilian linguists during the Pacific War and in occupied Japan. Framed in a transimperial context, this book examines the interactions between the United States and Japan as well as Japanese Americans’ complicated relationships to white Americans and Japanese nationals from 1941 through 1952. With a focus on Nisei’s interstitial positions and brokering roles, the book interrogates the changing meanings and shifting grounds of race, citizenship, and culture. It unravels how these minority American soldiers came to appreciate the power of their birthright citizenship in the context of the total war against and the subsequent domination of the enemy who shared their same ancestry. This book also explains how the rise of inclusionary nationalism in post-World War II America was intertwined with the making of Nisei soldiers as an embodiment of “minority imperial citizenship.” Their work as military and civilian linguists in occupied Japan turned them into the frontline executors of US imperial power under the guise of spreading colorblind democracy and capitalism to the Cold War Asia-Pacific and beyond. By examining the involvement of Japanese Americans in America’s “Good War” and the occupation of defeated Japan from a transimperial perspective, Brokering a Race War presents a critical intervention into the oft-celebratory representations of minority US servicemen as a trope for America’s disavowal of racism and a paragon of its multicultural democracy.
